Selling fast in Seattle

In Seattle you can list through an agent, sell the house on your own, or accept a cash bid from someone who buys it as-is. The pace depends on what shape the house is in, whether renters occupy it, and how much you are prepared to fix up first.

The market is expensive, and most households rent. About 784,777 people lived here on July 1, 2025, up from 737,015 in the 2020 census, and owners occupy only 43.7 percent of homes. Figures for 2020 to 2024 put the median owner-occupied home at $938,600, median gross rent at $2,030 a month and median household income at $123,860. There are 363,466 households of about 2.00 people each, and the mean commute is 26.0 minutes.

Plenty of local sellers own a rental, inherited a house, or hold an older place that needs work. Each situation has its own rules, explained below.

Light rail has also changed which addresses feel convenient. The 1 Line reached Northgate in October 2021 and Lynnwood in August 2024, so a house within walking distance of a station can be worth pointing out in the listing.

Hills, water and the disclosure form

The city lies on slopes between Puget Sound and Lake Washington, in earthquake country, with a rainy season that runs October through March. Roofs, basements and drainage take a beating, and the state's seller form probes every one of them.

Sample questions: Did the roof leak in the past five years? Has the basement flooded or leaked? Has the lot settled, slipped or slid? Was there material damage from an earthquake, flood or landslide? Whatever you leave out, an inspector is likely to find, so tell the buyer first.

Hills are part of the city's identity. Capitol Hill, First Hill, Beacon Hill, Queen Anne, Magnolia and West Seattle are the usual list, and the highest point inside city limits reaches 520 feet above sea level at Myrtle Reservoir Park in High Point. Slope matters to a buyer: ask yourself what your lot has done in heavy rain, and keep any geotechnical or drainage paperwork handy.

The magnitude 6.8 Nisqually earthquake on February 28, 2001, did heavy damage in Pioneer Square, which stands on reclaimed land, and the Seattle Fault runs just south of downtown. A house with a retrofit, a new foundation or a chimney repair should have that work documented in your sale folder.

If a neighbor's slope, a retaining wall or a shared drainage line affects your lot, mention it on the form too. Buyers forgive known issues more readily than surprises.

Excise tax and what you owe at closing

For most Seattle sellers the excise tax on real estate is the biggest closing cost. Washington expects the seller to pay it. When a seller does not, responsibility shifts to the buyer and an unpaid amount may turn into a lien. The state's share is tiered, with each slice of the sale price taxed at its own rate:

  • 1.1 percent applies up to $525,000.
  • 1.28 percent covers the part between $525,000 and $1,525,000.
  • 2.75 percent covers the part between $1,525,000 and $3,025,000.
  • 3 percent applies to everything above $3,025,000.

For sales beginning January 1, 2027 the tiers break at $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000, and the four rates stay the same. A local rate comes on top, listed in the Department of Revenue's local rate table. To find the local rate for a Seattle address, ask your closing agent or the King County treasurer.

Payment goes to the county treasurer by the sale date, defined by the state as the day the deed is notarized. After a month of nonpayment, interest accrues at the 6 percent the Department of Revenue lists for 2026 and 2027. The state can audit a sale, so keep your records for at least four years. Your parcel's property tax balance and due dates are available from the King County treasurer.

Paperwork the seller hands over

If the property is improved residential land, you owe the buyer a completed disclosure statement, unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt. The deadline in RCW 64.06.020 is five business days after both parties accept a written purchase contract, though they may agree to a different period.

From delivery, the buyer has three business days to rescind in writing, or may give that right up. Only the seller signs the form, and it is no warranty. Topics include title, water, sewer, structure, systems, homeowners' associations and environmental conditions, with a reminder about carbon monoxide alarms and a smoke detector.

Give construction history the most attention. The form wants to know about conversions, additions and remodels, and whether every building permit and final inspection was obtained. Did you finish a basement or add a bedroom years back? Find those records before you answer. The Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections can tell you what is on file for your address.

A rough timeline for a quick Seattle sale

Fast sales in Seattle start with homework done before any offer lands. One workable order:

  1. Settle the tenant question first. A rented single-family house with a tenant who must leave needs 90 days of written notice, so that clock comes before listing.
  2. Gather permit papers and inspection records so the state form can be completed in one sitting.
  3. Request the tax balance from the county treasurer and ask your closing agent which local excise rate fits your address.
  4. Once a contract is signed, hand the buyer your disclosure statement inside five business days.
  5. Allow the buyer three business days to rescind, then proceed to title work, the notarized deed and recording.

No repair crew is needed for any of this. A cash buyer will take a worn house as-is, with the offer already adjusted.

Selling a Seattle rental

With a tenant in the house, two rule sets apply: Seattle's rental registration program and the state's process for ending a tenancy. The city's Rental Registration and Inspection Ordinance wants a rental registered once it has a tenant, and a short-term rental that is not the operator's primary residence must register before it is listed. Registrations are good for two years.

RRIO fee or penaltyAmount
Registration, one rental unit$126
Each additional unit at the same property$31.50
City inspector, one rental unit$241.50
City inspector, each additional unit$52.50
Filing fee for a private inspector's results$63
Penalty for a violation$150 a day for the first 10 days, then $500 a day

A property is selected for inspection once in its first five years, then faces a 10 percent chance of selection again in the next five. At least 60 days are allowed to complete it, and tenants must be told at least two days before the visit. Typical failures include absent smoke or carbon monoxide detectors, missing handrails and exposed wiring. The RRIO helpline number is (206) 684-4110.

A tenanted single-family house can be cleared for sale under RCW 59.18.650, provided the tenant gets 90 days of written notice. Listing at a reasonable price within 30 days after move-out shows the sale is real. Put the house back up for rent, or take it off the market, within 90 days and the law presumes you never meant to sell. Improper removal costs the landlord the larger of the tenant's damages or three times monthly rent, with attorney fees and court costs added.

When a cash sale makes sense

Cash is often right for a fixer-upper, an estate house, a rental whose tenants are hard to manage, or a hard move date. Before saying yes, work through this list:

  • Learn who pays the excise tax and any title or escrow fees, and get that in writing.
  • Fix the closing day, and ask whether the buyer accepts the house with tenants staying.
  • Compare the bid with what similar houses nearby sold for lately.
  • If the house has been rented, check where you stand with the rental registration program.
  • Collect permits for additions, because the disclosure form still asks about them.

After you say yes, escrow opens and a title search begins. Any mortgage is cleared from proceeds, and you sign the deed before a notary. The county receives the affidavit and tax, and money is released after recording. Nobody orders an appraisal or lender review, so title work and your own calendar mostly set the date.

Frequently asked questions

Who pays the real estate excise tax when I sell a house in Seattle?

The seller, in the usual case. Skip it and the buyer becomes liable, with a possible lien on the property. The county treasurer collects by the sale date, at state rates from 1.1 percent to 3 percent plus a local rate.

Do I have to give a buyer a disclosure statement in Seattle?

In most improved residential sales, yes. RCW 64.06.020 gives you five business days after the contract is accepted, and the buyer then has three business days to rescind in writing. A waiver or exemption changes this.

Do I need to register my Seattle rental before I sell it?

Yes, once a tenant lives there. A registration lasts two years, and being late or skipping an inspection costs $150 per day for 10 days, then $500 per day.

Can I sell a Seattle house that has tenants in it?

Yes. Buyers can accept the lease as written. If you need the house empty first, RCW 59.18.650 asks for 90 days of written notice and a genuine listing effort within 30 days of move-out.

What if my Seattle house has an addition built without a permit?

The sale can still go ahead. Answer the permit question on the state form truthfully, and check with the Seattle Department of Construction and Inspections for records on your address.

Spokane housing at a glance

Spokane lies along the Spokane River in eastern Washington, roughly 18 miles from Idaho and 229 miles east of Seattle. An estimated 230,783 people lived here on July 1, 2025, a gain of 0.8 percent over the April 2020 base. Homeowners hold 58.8 percent of households, and the median home is valued at $363,500. One citywide number says little about your block. Recent sales nearby are a better guide to price.

The 2026 wildfires and selling

For anyone whose house or street was hit, this is the first thing to sort out. The Old Trails Fire in early August 2026 destroyed more than 600 buildings, and Spokane has been running a recovery program for burned and damaged properties ever since.

Help available through the city's wildfire page and the county's recovery pages includes:

  • A free asbestos survey, on request, for owners of properties the Old Trails Fire affected.
  • A year of free application completeness screening from Permavia for residential rebuilding permits. It is optional and does not replace the city's own review.
  • Spokane County's Demolition and Rebuilding FAQ and Next Steps FAQ.
  • A phone line: 311 inside the city, or 509.755.CITY (2489) from elsewhere, Monday through Friday, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m.

Owners who lost a house, or who hold a damaged one, often weigh rebuilding against selling the lot or the shell. Before signing anything, get your insurer's answer in writing on how a sale affects an open claim, and ask the county assessor how the damage changes your assessed value.

Buyers of fire-area property may ask for the survey results, the permit history and any insurance paperwork. Keep these together in one folder so you can share them quickly and show a buyer how the house reached its current condition.

A practical order for owners near the Old Trails Fire: first, call 311 or 509.755.CITY (2489) and ask which recovery steps apply to your parcel. Second, request the free asbestos survey if your property qualifies, since it documents the condition of the site. Third, read the county's Next Steps FAQ before you decide between rebuilding and selling. Finally, decide whether you want Permavia's free screening for a rebuild application, because that choice only makes sense if you plan to rebuild rather than sell.

Historic districts and neighborhoods

Location shapes value. Downtown and Riverside are the business core, South Hill rises to the south, and Browne's Addition, west of downtown, is a National Historic District of Queen Anne and Craftsman mansions. Hillyard, in the northeast, started in 1892 around the Great Northern Railway yard. East Central, the University District and West Central complete the older core, and 18 National Register historic districts exist citywide.

Living in one? Before you repaint, re-side or replace windows to prepare for a sale, ask city planning staff whether exterior changes need design review. Spokane Public Schools (District 81) covers most of the city, and the Mead School District serves parts of north Spokane County beyond city limits.

Historic status can help or hinder. Some buyers seek out an older home with period detail, while others worry about rules for renovation. Know which group your neighborhood attracts, and describe the house with that in mind.

In Browne's Addition and Hillyard, clear photos of period details such as porches and windows can show what makes the house distinctive.

Permits to close out before you list

Sort out permits with the city before you list. Spokane handles permits through its Accela Citizen Access portal. The Development Services Center is open in person from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, and from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Wednesday.

  • Look up the permit history for projects you did or inherited: a finished basement, a new deck, a replaced water heater.
  • Ask staff how to resolve an expired or open permit, ideally before a buyer's inspector spots it.
  • Use only the city's portal to pay. Fake permit invoices are circulating, and the city never requests payment through emailed wire instructions.

For lot size and the legal description that belongs on the deed, check the county's parcel information search, which also shows tax history and assessed value.

If you hold a permit for fire-related work, bring that file to the first conversation with any buyer. A clear paper trail shows what was repaired and when.

Ask the permit center for a printout when a permit is closed, and keep it with your deed. A buyer's agent will often ask for it, and handing it over at once builds trust.

Excise tax and disclosure paperwork

Excise tax on a Washington real estate sale is ordinarily the seller's cost. The Spokane County Treasurer collects it, and the sale date is the due date, even if the deed is still unrecorded. State tiers open at 1.1 percent on the first $525,000, with 1.28 percent applying through $1,525,000. Sales beginning January 1, 2027 use $551,000 and $1,551,000 as those thresholds. Your local share comes on top, so call the treasurer for the full rate before you work out your net.

If the tax sits unpaid for a month after the sale, interest starts at the 6 percent rate the Department of Revenue lists for 2026, and the debt can become a lien.

Most house sales require a seller disclosure statement. The buyer should get the finished form five business days after both sides sign the contract, and then holds three business days to rescind unless you agree to something else (RCW 64.06.020). It asks about the structure, the roof, systems, and smoke and carbon monoxide alarms. A buyer may choose to waive it.

If fire insurance paid out on your property, mention any payments or liens to the title company early, because they can change what is paid at closing.

When a cash sale makes sense

Consider cash when time or the house's condition counts for more than a bit of extra price. An agent listing means prep work, open houses and a wait for the buyer's lender. A cash buyer takes the place as it is and may close on a day that suits you. That helps with fire damage, an inherited property, or a rental where the tenant is difficult.

Ask any Spokane bidder to commit these terms on paper:

  • The total price, plus who covers excise tax and recording fees.
  • A closing date and the name of the title or escrow firm.
  • Whether repairs, leftover belongings and open permits stay with the house.
  • An expiration for the offer, and what becomes of any earnest money.

Run the numbers against a listing that nets you the price minus repairs, commission and carrying costs. If the cash offer is lower, that gap pays for skipping the work and the waiting.

Once you say yes, a title company combs through the public record while escrow holds the paperwork. Your mortgage balance, if any, is settled from the proceeds. You sign the deed before a notary, the county receives the tax and affidavit, and you are paid after recording.

Frequently asked questions

How fast can I sell a house in Spokane?

That depends on the route. Cash skips the loan approval, so it can finish sooner than a listing, but title work and the escrow company decide the real closing date.

Who owes excise tax on a Spokane sale?

Usually the seller. The Spokane County Treasurer collects it as of the sale date, with state tiers opening at 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 and a local share on top. The treasurer can quote the combined rate.

Can I sell a fire-damaged house in Spokane?

Yes. Owners affected by the August 2026 Old Trails Fire can ask the city for a free asbestos survey, and the county posts demolition and rebuilding guidance. Check with your insurer first about how a sale affects an open claim.

Must a Spokane seller provide a disclosure statement?

Most residential sales require it, delivered five business days after the contract is signed. The buyer may waive it, and some transfers are exempt. Once delivered, the buyer has three business days to rescind.

Where do I check property tax history for a Spokane house?

The Spokane County parcel information site shows tax history and assessed value. For a payoff or proration at closing, ask the Spokane County Treasurer.

Tacoma housing at a glance

Home values here center on $479,600, and 55.8 percent of households own their place. Roughly 229,816 people live in Tacoma, the Pierce County seat and a hub for the whole South Sound. If a tenant lives in your house, the median rent to compare against is $1,676.

Joint Base Lewis-McChord sits a few miles south, and Seattle-Tacoma International Airport is 22 miles north in SeaTac. Residents average 28.8 minutes getting to work, which is a fair selling point in a listing description.

Neighborhoods buyers ask about

Expect the first question from a buyer to be which part of Tacoma the house is in. Locals sort the city into Central Tacoma, New Tacoma around downtown, North Tacoma, Northeast Tacoma, West Tacoma and the Port of Tacoma area.

  • Central Tacoma: Hilltop, Delong Park, the Wedge, Bryant and College Heights.
  • North Tacoma: the Proctor District, the North Slope, Old Tacoma, Ruston Way, Skyline and Yakima Hill.
  • West Tacoma: the Highlands, Narrows, Titlow and Salmon Beach.
  • Downtown: the Stadium District, the Theater District, the Dome District and the Thea Foss Waterway.

Transit adds value near the core. The T Line links Tacoma Dome Station, downtown, the University of Washington Tacoma campus and Hilltop, while Sounder trains and express buses head toward Seattle.

Two boundary quirks matter. Ruston is its own incorporated town and Browns Point is unincorporated, so find out who has authority over your parcel before phoning Tacoma's permit desk. Older homes may also fall inside one of the five historic overlay zones. The city's preservation program covers 165 landmarks and more than 1,000 historic properties, so ask before planning any exterior change.

Shoreline, elevation and views

Water and slope define much of Tacoma. Ground rises from sea level to roughly 500 feet around Commencement Bay, and plenty of streets have Mount Rainier views. Low ground by the Port of Tacoma lies in the path of a Puyallup River lahar should the volcano erupt, a topic some tide-flat buyers raise.

The smell once nicknamed the Tacoma Aroma disappeared after the Simpson Tacoma Kraft mill shut in September 2023. Downtown has been rebuilt since the 1990s around the UW Tacoma campus, the T Line and a restored Thea Foss Waterway. The Tacoma Narrows bridges tie the city to Gig Harbor and the Kitsap Peninsula.

Property maintenance rules starting in 2027

Tacoma's new property maintenance standard begins January 1, 2027. Under Ordinance 29125, International Property Maintenance Code standards join the city's Property Maintenance and Nuisance Code, and the city gets stronger tools against repeat and chronic violations.

Staff handle about 4,500 maintenance cases a year under Chapters 8.30 and 2.01. Section 7 holds the expanded enforcement program until at least nine months after the council funds it, so how much changes day to day depends on later budgets.

Owners of vacant, neglected or tenant-occupied houses should ask whether a complaint is open against the property before listing. Details are at tacoma.gov/IPMC.

Paying Pierce County property tax

Tax bills for Tacoma addresses come from the Assessor-Treasurer, 2401 S. 35th St., Room 142, phone (253) 798-6111. Closing settles whatever is unpaid and divides the year between you and the buyer, so ask for a payoff number well ahead.

  • Pay online through the parcel search site.
  • Pay by phone at (253) 798-3333.
  • Mail a check to Pierce County Finance.
  • Walk in at the cashier lobby, 1501 Market St., Suite 120, weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

A state program expands in January 2027 and will lower taxes for more Pierce County owners who are 61 or older or who have a qualifying disability. If you or a relative who owns the house might qualify, ask the Assessor-Treasurer before you sell.

Excise tax and the seller disclosure

Excise tax on the sale is the seller's bill, payable to the county treasurer when the sale occurs. The state takes 1.1 percent of the first $525,000 and 1.28 percent of what falls between $525,000 and $1,525,000, then a local share goes on top.

State law adds a paperwork duty. Under RCW 64.06.020 you hand the buyer a signed property condition form within five business days after the contract is signed. Questions run through the roof, plumbing, electrical and heating, and the form reminds you that carbon monoxide alarms and a smoke detection device are required.

Before you list: a short checklist

  • Locate the newest tax statement and any special assessment notices.
  • Ask the county what it would take to clear unpaid tax.
  • Dig out permits for jobs such as a garage conversion or added bathroom.
  • Confirm nothing is open against the parcel at the city or county.

Put these in a single folder before showings begin. Buyers and title staff will request most of them, and whatever title work uncovers is paid from your proceeds, so learning the amounts now helps you plan.

From offer to closing

After you accept an offer the steps arrive in a set order. Title or escrow requests payoffs for unpaid tax or liens. The condition form reaches the buyer inside five business days of signing. This year's property tax is prorated so you pay for your months and the buyer pays for theirs.

Excise tax goes to the county treasurer on the sale date. Since the state share steps up with price and the local share varies, have your closing agent quote the exact figure before you sign.

A cash purchase involves no lender, which removes the usual appraisal and loan committee. Remaining risks are title surprises, an open permit or complaint, and your own moving date, so settle those first. If you own a rental, tell the buyer early whether a tenant stays, since that changes who can walk the house and when the keys change hands.

Should I list my Tacoma house or take a cash offer?

Weigh your repair budget, your calendar and what an inspector would flag. A listing reaches the whole market. A cash offer gives up some reach for speed and simplicity, which fits a vacant home, an inherited one or a rental with tenants still living there.

Judge written offers by what lands in your pocket. Ask who pays excise tax, how long the price holds, the closing date, and whether the buyer takes furniture and leftovers as they are. Get every term in writing, and compare the net from a listing, after repairs and carrying costs, against the net from a cash offer.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a house in Tacoma that needs repairs?

Yes. A cash buyer may take the house in its current condition. On most residential sales you still fill out the seller disclosure describing what you know about the property.

What does Ordinance 29125 mean for Tacoma sellers?

It sets a new maintenance standard starting January 1, 2027. Expanded enforcement begins no sooner than nine months after the council funds it, so look for open code complaints before you sell.

Who collects property tax on a Tacoma house?

Pierce County, through the Assessor-Treasurer's office in Tacoma. Call (253) 798-6111 about values, statements and exemptions, and ask for a payoff before closing.

Who pays the excise tax when a Tacoma house sells?

Usually the seller, to the county treasurer on the sale date. The state rate steps up, beginning at 1.1 percent on the first $525,000, and a local share is added.

How many people live in Tacoma?

About 229,816 as of July 1, 2025, up from 219,346 at the April 2020 count. It is the third most populous city in Washington.

We buy Vancouver houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

How fast can I sell a house in Vancouver, WA?

How quickly a Vancouver sale closes comes down to the buyer's money, the title work and one county stop that every Clark County deed must make. Cash removes the lender from the picture, so owners facing a move, an inherited house or a big repair bill often start there. Listing the traditional way means showings, an appraisal and a loan approval first.

Vancouver is the Clark County seat, sitting on the Columbia River's north bank opposite Portland. About 199,698 people live here, 4.6 percent more than in 2020. That growth brings plenty of buyers and investors to the same streets you live on, so collecting more than one offer is realistic.

Vancouver housing numbers

Owners occupy 50.8 percent of homes, so roughly half the housing stock is rented. Landlords and investors may bid on a fixer-upper just as readily as a household planning to live there.

Housing measureVancouver

Median home value$462,400

Older neighborhoods and inspection issues

Downtown and most of the older housing sit in West Vancouver. The east side grew after an annexation in 1997 that brought in 11,258 acres and 58,171 residents, with NE Andresen Road as the usual boundary between the halves.

Several well-known neighborhoods began as wartime housing. When the Kaiser shipyard drew tens of thousands of workers in the 1940s, the Vancouver Housing Authority was created along with six developments: Fruit Valley, Fourth Plain Village, Bagley Downs, Ogden Meadows, Burton Homes and McLoughlin Heights. Expect inspectors in those areas to press on age-related items.

  • Original wiring and panels
  • Galvanized or older supply plumbing
  • Foundations, crawl spaces and drainage
  • Roofs and insulation

Roofs, gutters and crawl spaces take the most wear from about 42 inches of rain a year, falling mostly from fall to spring, so look at them before you price the house.

Over a third of the urban area is in unincorporated pockets, among them Hazel Dell, Felida, Orchards and Salmon Creek. Confirm your address is within city limits, because the permit and rental rules that follow apply only inside them.

School districts and commuting

Vancouver Public Schools serves most of the west side and Evergreen Public Schools most of the east. A few edges of the city belong to Camas or Battle Ground, so look up your street with the district before quoting schools to a buyer.

Interstates 5 and 205 both cross the Columbia into Portland, SR 14 runs east from downtown, and SR 500 links I-5 to I-205. Rush-hour traffic is heavy on the Interstate Bridge and the Glenn Jackson Bridge, and C-Tran runs local and express buses. Homes near the freeways often appeal to commuters who value a shorter trip.

Do I need a permit before selling a Vancouver house?

Only if you do work before closing. Vancouver requires a residential building permit for building, altering, adding to, repairing or demolishing homes. Typical permitted projects:

  • Additions and remodels
  • Adding a garage, carport, deck or patio cover
  • Adding or removing walls
  • Converting a basement, attic or garage into living space
  • Changing the footprint of a structure

Small stand-alone electrical, mechanical or plumbing jobs fall under a trade permit instead, and tree removal needs a city permit. Suspect an earlier owner skipped a permit? A field evaluation permit lets city inspectors decide which permits and corrections are needed. Call the Permit Center at 360-487-7833.

The city's updated zoning code allows more middle housing, up to six units on one lot. A buyer with development plans may value a lot differently than someone who just wants to move in.

Selling a rental

Landlords selling inside city limits should know about two programs. Since January 1, 2026, owners of residential rentals in Vancouver register each unit every year for $30 per unit. Health and safety inspections are planned to begin in mid 2027.

When a registered rental sells, the registration moves to the new owner within 60 days of the property transfer, with no extra fee. If you stop renting, you can deregister the property. Questions go to rentalregistration@cityofvancouver.us or 360-487-7928.

A short-term rental, meaning stays under 30 consecutive nights, carries its own permit. Applicants need a Washington business license with the city endorsement, liability coverage of at least $1 million and a mailed notice to abutting neighbors. The city caps permits at 870, which is about 1 percent of its homes. Leases and homeowners association rules still apply, so a buyer with this plan should verify the status on the city's short-term rental page.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Vancouver houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Deed and excise tax in Clark County

In Clark County the Treasurer sees a sale before the Auditor does. The Treasurer takes the real estate excise tax, and under RCW 82.45.090 the Auditor cannot record a deed until the tax is paid or marked not due.

Payment is due 30 days after the sale date, plus a $5 processing fee. The state portion rises with price:

  • 1.10 percent on a price up to $525,000
  • 1.28 percent from $525,000.01 to $1,525,000
  • 2.75 percent from $1,525,000.01 to $3,025,000
  • 3.00 percent above $3,025,000

A local rate goes on top, and your closing agent or the Treasurer can quote the total for your price. Visit the Treasurer at 1300 Franklin Street, 2nd Floor, Monday through Thursday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Once the tax is paid, the Auditor's Recording Department in the same building records the deed. Its number is 564-397-2208.

The seller disclosure

The form in RCW 64.06.020 applies to improved residential property. Sellers deliver it within five business days of a mutually accepted written contract unless the parties choose a different schedule, and the buyer can then rescind within three business days.

Known unpermitted work goes on the form. Selling as-is does not erase that duty, although it does mean you are not promising repairs.

What a cash sale skips

With no lender, a cash buyer needs no appraisal or loan approval, so the house does not have to meet a bank's condition rules. The county steps stay the same: disclosure form, excise tax at the Treasurer and recording at the Auditor. Title or escrow staff usually walk the papers through both offices.

Before you accept, estimate your net after commission, repairs and carrying costs, find out who pays the excise tax and get the closing date written down. With a rental, ask how the buyer plans to handle the tenant and the registration transfer.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a Vancouver, WA house as-is?

Yes, and they are common. The disclosure form under RCW 64.06.020 still applies, and unpermitted work you know about belongs on it.

Who records the deed when a Vancouver house sells?

The Clark County Auditor's Recording Department, but only after the Treasurer handles the excise tax affidavit. Both offices are at 1300 Franklin Street, and title or escrow companies normally submit the paperwork for you.

What happens to my Vancouver rental registration when I sell?

The new owner takes it over within 60 days of the transfer at no added fee. If the buyer will live there, the registration can instead be ended by deregistering.

Does Vancouver cap short-term rental permits?

Yes, at 870 permits, roughly 1 percent of homes. A buyer counting on short-term rental income should ask the Permit Center about availability before paying extra.

Which school district is my Vancouver house in?

Most of west Vancouver is in Vancouver Public Schools and most of east Vancouver is in Evergreen Public Schools. Small portions are in the Camas and Battle Ground districts, so check the address with the district.

Bellevue's housing market

Bellevue is a high-value market. Median value for an owner-occupied home was $1,340,300 over 2020 to 2024, and 154,193 people live here as of July 1, 2025. Owners occupy about 52.0% of housing, median household income is $165,576 and median gross rent is $2,572. The city grew from 122,363 people in 2010 to 151,854 in 2020.

It is an Eastside city in King County, across Lake Washington from Seattle and between that lake and Lake Sammamish. Interstate 405 runs north to south, Interstate 90 crosses the southern part, and State Route 520 roughly marks the northern edge. Kirkland and Redmond sit to the north, Issaquah to the east, Mercer Island across the East Channel Bridge, and Newcastle and Renton to the south.

Neighborhoods and school districts

The city names fourteen neighborhoods:

  • Downtown, Wilburton/BelRed and Eastgate/Factoria.
  • Bridle Trails, Northwest Bellevue, Northeast Bellevue and West Bellevue.
  • Crossroads, Lake Hills, Newport and Somerset.
  • Cougar Mountain/Lakemont, Woodridge and West Lake Sammamish.

The great majority of the city is in the Bellevue School District, whose main public high schools are Bellevue High, Interlake, Newport and Sammamish. Parts of the city fall in the Lake Washington, Renton and Issaquah districts instead. Look up your address before listing, because buyers will ask.

Light rail and commuting

Downtown Bellevue is the second largest city center in Washington, with about 1,300 businesses, 45,000 employees and 10,200 residents, and transit has caught up with the jobs. Sound Transit's 2 Line runs from Lynnwood to Redmond through Seattle, Mercer Island and Bellevue. The South Bellevue to Redmond Technology station section opened April 27, 2024, and the Seattle to Bellevue section opened in March 2026. The Bellevue Transit Center downtown serves both King County Metro and Sound Transit buses, and a fare-free electric shuttle run by Circuit began operating in August 2023.

Homes near a station can mention the walk to the train in the listing. Commute time across the city averages 23.6 minutes.

Short-term rentals

A whole house usually cannot be rented short term. Bellevue's Land Use Code defines transient lodging as a stay of less than 30 days, and an entire single-family home or a home with an accessory dwelling unit cannot be used that way. Rentals of 30 days or more are allowed, and an ADU may be rented only long term. If a buyer is counting on vacation-rental income, say so plainly in your listing.

Type of homeShort-term rental rule
Entire single-family home, or home with an ADUNot allowed for transient lodging.
Rooms in an owner-occupied single-family homeAllowed as a boarding house or bed and breakfast: owner-occupied, at most two rooms and two adults per room, with an approved home occupation permit (LUC 20.20.140).
Apartment, condo or planned unit development in a residential districtAllowed with a Short-Term Stay Use Registration Notice, limited to five units and 20% of the units in the development (LUC 20.20.800).

Development Services Land Use takes questions at 425-452-4188 or landusereview@bellevuewa.gov.

Work that needs a permit

Bellevue Development Services publishes a list of work that requires permits. These are the items most likely to surface before a sale:

  • Additions that add square footage, including a second story or dormers, need a permit with plan review.
  • Converting a garage or carport into living space needs a permit with plan review.
  • Decks with a walking surface more than 30 inches above the ground need a permit with plan review.
  • Interior remodels that create new walls or turn a basement into living area need a permit.
  • Furnaces, heat pumps, new gas lines, new electrical circuits and EV charging stations need permits.
  • An interior accessory dwelling unit needs approval, and the review takes several weeks.

Some jobs need nothing. Replacing kitchen cabinets or countertops, swapping a window or door for the same size in the same spot, and building a fence under eight feet tall are all permit-free, though fences over 4.5 feet often cannot sit in front-yard setbacks. In an emergency, such as a failed water heater or furnace, repairs can start first and the permit follows on the first city work day afterward.

Property tax, disclosure and closing

King County bills property tax on a Bellevue house, in two installments due April 30 and October 31 (RCW 84.56.020). The lien starts January 1. With no contract term on the subject, RCW 84.60.020 charges you for the days you owned the home that year and the buyer for the rest. Escrow prorates the bill at closing, and any unpaid balance comes out of your proceeds.

RCW 64.06.020 also requires a seller disclosure statement for improved residential property. The clock is five business days from mutual acceptance of the written contract, and the buyer can waive the form. A buyer who receives it can rescind within three business days.

Excise tax when you sell

On most sales the seller covers the state excise tax and escrow sends it to the county treasurer at closing. The state schedule for 2027 sales has four bands: 1.1% to $551,000, 1.28% to $1,551,000, 2.75% to $3,051,000, and 3% beyond that. At Bellevue's median home value of $1,340,300 a sale reaches the second band. A local portion is added, and your closing agent can give you the full figure before you sign.

Paperwork buyers ask for

Permit history draws the most questions in Bellevue. Collect records for any second story, dormer, garage or carport conversion, deck over 30 inches, basement remodel, furnace or heat pump, gas line, new circuit or EV charger. If an accessory dwelling unit exists, know whether it was approved and whether it is rented long term. Call Development Services if a record is missing, and expect that an interior ADU review takes several weeks. Having answers ready keeps a cash offer from stalling over a permit question.

What a sale looks like step by step

First, check the school district and gather permit records for any addition, garage conversion, deck or remodel. Second, complete the disclosure statement. Third, ask your lender for a payoff figure and King County for the current tax balance. Fourth, once you accept an offer, escrow opens title work and prorates taxes. Fifth, you sign and the sale funds on closing day, with excise tax paid from your proceeds. With a cash buyer there is no bank appraisal or loan approval in the way, so the pace is set by title work and how quickly your papers are in order.

Can I rent my whole Bellevue house short term?

No. Bellevue does not allow an entire single-family home or a home with an ADU to be used for transient lodging, which is a stay under 30 days. Rentals of 30 days or more are allowed.

Does replacing kitchen cabinets in Bellevue need a permit?

A building permit is not required for replacing kitchen cabinets or countertops. A plumbing or electrical permit may still be needed if that work is part of the job.

Which school district serves my Bellevue home?

Most of the city is in the Bellevue School District, but portions are in the Lake Washington, Renton and Issaquah districts. Check the district for your exact address.

How soon must a Bellevue seller give the buyer the disclosure statement?

Five business days after both sides accept the written contract. The buyer can waive it, and some transfers are exempt. Once delivered, the buyer has three business days to rescind.

Who pays the state excise tax on a Bellevue sale?

Usually the seller, paid through escrow on the sale date. A local portion is added, so ask your closing agent for the total.

Your options for selling a Kent house

A Kent homeowner has three ways out: hire a listing agent, run the sale personally, or accept an offer from someone who needs no mortgage. Time, effort and price shift with each, so hold them up against your own deadline.

  • Listing with an agent: plan on staging, cleaning and repairs, followed by showings, the buyer's inspection and a lender's sign-off.
  • Selling on your own: price and terms are yours to set, and so are the advertising, contract and closing paperwork.
  • Selling to a cash buyer: nobody underwrites a loan, so the sale moves quicker. Request the figure you would net and set it beside the other two routes.

A building with tenants raises extra questions, covered below, because Kent runs its own rental inspection program.

Kent's three areas and flood history

Kent has three sections. West Hill runs along Interstate 5. The Valley is mostly industrial and commercial, with some medium-density housing and parkland beside the Green River. East Hill is largely residential with retail. Downtown sits on the east side of the valley, about 16 miles from downtown Seattle and downtown Bellevue. Lake Meridian on East Hill is the largest lake, and Clark Lake and Lake Fenwick are ringed by city parks.

The Green River matters to anyone selling in the Valley. Floods from the Green and White rivers troubled the area for decades until Howard A. Hanson Dam went up at Eagle Gorge in 1962. The city keeps a Floodplains page with flood resources and FEMA elevation certificates, plus a Green River flooding information page. If your house is near the river, ask the city for the elevation certificate and floodplain status before a buyer asks.

Kent housing at a glance

Kent has 134,871 residents, a hair under the 2020 count of 136,588. Households average 2.84 people, and the median value of an owner-occupied home is $587,800. The jump from 92,411 residents in 2010 came partly from annexing the Panther Lake area in 2010.

Rental housing rules and your sale

These apply to buildings with two or more units. A 2018 city ordinance requires periodic health and safety inspections by a qualified inspector for apartments, townhomes, fourplexes, triplexes and duplexes inside city limits. A standalone house is not on that list. If you own a duplex or small building and plan to sell, the program shapes what a buyer will ask about.

  • Registration: covered rentals register online every year, with a deadline of November 1.
  • Inspection cycle: each property is inspected once every three years. North East Hill, north of James Street, is on the 2026 cycle. West Hill and the Valley, west of Highway 167, are due in 2027, and South East Hill, south of James Street, in 2028.
  • Penalties: owners whose units fail must make repairs and pass reinspection before renewing the multi-family business license. Failure can bring penalty fees and revocation of the license.

For license questions, call 253-856-5200. Ask the city which cycle year your address falls in before you set a closing date, and keep the latest inspection paperwork in your sale file.

What you file and pay at closing

Washington's real estate excise tax is the largest closing item. Sellers usually cover it, and if they do not, the Department of Revenue treats the buyer as responsible. The state charges 1.1 percent of the first $525,000 and 1.28 percent of the slice from there to $1,525,000, and a local rate rides on top.

Passing title by deed takes three things: an excise tax affidavit, the deed and the payment. Skip mailing them to the state, since a misdirected packet can hold up the county filing and trigger penalties and interest. Deliver them to the treasurer in the property's county, King County for Kent, or let escrow file for you. Payment falls due on the sale date, and a month of delay starts penalty and interest.

Permits buyers ask about

Kent's Permit Center takes electronic applications by appointment and issues residential permits for additions and alterations, plumbing, re-roofing and mechanical work. The city publishes separate short forms for a residential plumbing permit, which covers replacing fixtures and hot water tanks, for a re-roof, and for mechanical equipment including gas piping. If a previous owner swapped a water heater or replaced a roof, ask the Permit Center whether a permit was pulled, and check the Permit Logs page for issued permits.

Code Enforcement can tell you whether any case is open on your property, so ask before you set a closing date. An open case can slow a sale, and fixing it first usually costs less than negotiating a credit with the buyer afterward. Keep any letters or notices in your sale file.

Roads, transit and schools

Commuters use State Route 167 north to Renton and south to Puyallup, and parts of Interstate 5 and State Route 18 lie in the city, with State Route 516 crossing east to west. Kent Station is the hub for Sounder commuter trains to Seattle and Tacoma, plus King County Metro and Sound Transit Express buses, and RapidRide A runs along SR 99 in west Kent. The I Line is scheduled to connect downtown Kent with Renton and Auburn in 2027. Average travel time to work is 30.4 minutes.

Most addresses belong to the Kent School District. Others sit in Federal Way Public Schools, Tahoma, Highline or the Renton School District, so verify yours before the listing goes live.

Before you accept an offer

  • Require the price, closing date and every closing cost in writing.
  • Ask the lender for a payoff statement with the exact balance.
  • Find out how the buyer will prove funds and whether an inspection can cancel the deal.
  • Owners of a duplex or small building should pull rental registration and the latest inspection report.
  • Check with the Permit Center on any water heater, roof or remodel you doubt was permitted.
  • Let escrow estimate state and local excise tax so your net is visible.

Someone keeping your tenants will ask for leases and the inspection record, while someone moving in will care more about permits and flood status. With both sets of papers on hand, you can answer either buyer fast.

Frequently asked questions

Does Kent's rental inspection program cover a single-family house?

No. The program covers apartments, townhomes, fourplexes, triplexes and duplexes, each with two or more units. Owners of those buildings register every year by November 1 and have an inspection once every three years.

Where do I file the excise tax affidavit for a Kent sale?

Take it to the treasurer of the county that holds the property, which means King County for Kent, along with the deed and payment. A packet sent to the state by mistake can stall the filing.

Which school district serves my Kent address?

The Kent School District covers most of the city. Pockets belong to Federal Way Public Schools, Tahoma, Highline Public Schools or the Renton district, so look up your exact address.

How far is Kent from Seattle?

Roughly 16 miles from downtown Seattle and downtown Bellevue. Drivers use State Route 167 or Interstate 5, and Sounder trains leave Kent Station for downtown Seattle at peak weekday hours.

Is flood risk a concern for Kent houses?

It can be in the Green River Valley. Howard A. Hanson Dam went up in 1962 after decades of flooding, and the city keeps a Floodplains page with FEMA elevation certificates. Ask the city about floodplain status for your parcel.

Can I sell an Everett house that has an accessory dwelling unit?

Yes, and the city has relaxed its rules. Everett permits accessory dwelling units in all zones other than Light Industrial and Heavy Industrial. The city defines an ADU as a unit under 1,000 square feet that is subordinate to the main home, and each lot may hold two. A dwelling under 1,200 square feet needs no off-street car parking.

Fees matter to the next owner. Transportation impact fees are waived for one added ADU, school impact fees are waived for ADUs, and park impact fees are cut by half. In June 2026 the city also launched a gallery of pre-approved ADU designs, with a licensing fee of about $1,500.

  • If the unit was built without a permit, ask Everett Permit Services at PermitServices@everettwa.gov what it takes to legalize it before you list.
  • Basements and attics count as ADU space, garages do not, and each separate dwelling unit needs its own utilities.
  • In a historic overlay, any ADU that is not entirely inside the existing home goes to the Historical Commission.

Your choices if you need to sell fast

Three routes cover most Everett sales, and your deadline plus the state of the house should choose between them.

  • Agent listing: reaches the most buyers, though showings, inspections and loan contingencies can stretch the timeline by weeks.
  • Investor or cash buyer: you often pick the closing date and face fewer conditions, but the price tends to land under what a polished listing could bring.
  • For sale by owner: no listing commission, but pricing, disclosure forms and negotiating are yours.

Before signing with anyone, read the purchase agreement and ask to see proof of funds. Then set each offer next to your net after liens, taxes and loan payoff. The escrow company's closing officer can lay those figures out in a written estimate.

Excise tax and closing paperwork

Every Washington sale carries a real estate excise tax, normally paid by the seller. RCW 82.45.060 builds the state share in steps. The first $525,000 of the price is taxed at 1.1 percent, the slice to $1,525,000 at 1.28 percent, the slice to $3,025,000 at 2.75 percent, and the rest at 3 percent. Starting with sales on January 1, 2027, the first step stretches to $551,000. A local rate rides on top of the state share, so the Snohomish County Treasurer or your escrow officer can give you the full number.

When title passes by deed, the treasurer receives the excise tax affidavit, the deed and the payment. Walk-in service at the excise tax counter runs Monday through Friday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., at 3000 Rockefeller, Everett, WA 98201.

The county splits the yearly property tax bill into April 30 and October 31 installments, and a mailed check needs a postmark on or before the day. An unpaid second half racks up interest and gets settled out of your proceeds at closing. The next first-half date is April 30, 2027.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Everett houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with property taxes owed

Interest starts once a payment is late. RCW 84.56.020 sets 9 percent a year on overdue taxes for residential property of four units or fewer, with no extra penalties, while bigger or nonresidential parcels face 12 percent and penalties. Charges post on the first of every month. If the April 30 first-half payment is missed, the entire year's tax becomes delinquent.

Foreclosure becomes possible once taxes for a third delinquent year are owed in full. The county holds its Tax Lien Foreclosure Sale online and files the property list in court each May. An owner near that point can sell and have the back taxes paid from the proceeds at closing. State law also lets interest and penalties be waived in narrow cases, so ask the Treasurer's office if yours might qualify.

From offer to closing

Having documents in hand before the first offer saves days. The usual sequence looks like this.

  • Insist that every offer is written down with price, closing date and the costs you would carry.
  • Learn how the buyer is paying and whether an inspection or a loan can undo the deal.
  • Request a lender payoff statement so the exact loan balance is known.
  • Collect permit papers for any basement, backyard unit or addition, and drainage papers if the lot slopes.
  • Ask escrow to add up excise tax, open property tax and other closing costs into one net figure.
  • Sign the deed and affidavit, then confirm the excise payment reaches the county treasurer.

A cash purchase has no lender appraisal or loan approval to wait on, so title work and your preferred move-out date drive the calendar. A listing adds showings, repair talks and the buyer's financing schedule.

Frequently asked questions

How many people live in Everett, WA?

About 113,567 people lived here as of July 1, 2025, up from 110,629 in the 2020 census. No other Snohomish County city is bigger.

Who pays the real estate excise tax when an Everett house sells?

Usually the seller. When the seller skips it, the buyer inherits the responsibility and the unpaid amount can attach to the property as a lien. RCW 82.45.060 holds the state tiers, and a local rate is added.

Are accessory dwelling units allowed in Everett?

Yes. ADUs are allowed in every zone except Light Industrial and Heavy Industrial, with up to two per lot and a size cap of 1,000 square feet. Check the permit history of any existing unit before you sell.

When are Snohomish County property taxes due?

April 30 for the first half or the whole year, and October 31 for the second half. A mailed payment counts if its postmark is no later than the deadline.

Which school district serves my Everett house?

Everett Public Schools serves most of the city. The Mukilteo School District takes the southern and western neighborhoods, so verify your address first.

Selling in Spokane Valley

Locals call it The Valley. Spokane Valley is the biggest suburb of Spokane, spread along the Spokane River between Spokane and Coeur d'Alene, Idaho, and it wraps around the separate city of Millwood on three sides. As of July 1, 2025 it had an estimated 108,405 residents, 5.2 percent above the 2020 base.

Home prices are modest compared with the Seattle area, so the state's tiered excise tax takes a smaller share of a typical sale. The closing section below explains how.

Short commutes help here. A drive of 20.8 minutes on average is a plain, true selling point, and Interstate 90 access is the first thing many buyers ask about.

A city built from several communities

The city dates to March 31, 2003, when Dishman, Opportunity, Trentwood, Veradale, part of Greenacres and East Spokane joined together, with Yardley and Chester inside the boundaries too. That patchwork shows in the housing. Farm and orchard land became postwar subdivisions, and the streets bend, stop and restart, with many cul-de-sacs. Buyers still use the old community names, so mention the one your house belongs to when you describe it.

The incorporation came after years of debate about local control, and the city has stayed a patchwork of distinct areas since. If your house sits near a boundary with Spokane or Millwood, confirm the jurisdiction before you ask about permits, because the office to call changes with the answer.

Roads, transit and schools

Interstate 90 runs through the middle, and the city is reached by exits 285 through 293. Drive times are short for this region. Buyers most often name these routes:

  • Sprague Avenue, the main shopping street, which doubles as Interstate 90 Business.
  • Trent Avenue, State Route 290, heading northeast to the Idaho border.
  • Pines Road, where State Route 27 begins at its northern end.
  • Argonne, Mullan, Pines, Evergreen and Sullivan, the main north to south arterials.
  • Bus service from Spokane Transit Authority via the Pence-Cole Valley Transit Center, plus a few park-and-ride lots.

School districts overlap the city. Central Valley is largest, East Valley and West Valley follow, and part of the western edge belongs to Spokane Public Schools. Lines ignore city limits, so look up your address before naming a school in a listing.

Permits and business licenses

Spokane Valley asks for a permit on new homes, duplexes, garages, decks, pools, spas and fences, and on any addition or interior alteration to a house. The interior point deserves attention if you did the work yourself. The Permit Center is inside City Hall at 10210 E. Sprague Avenue, phone 509-720-5240. Filings include site plans, construction plans and a copy of the sewer permit from Spokane County Utilities. The online portal accepts applications, with payment by check or by card plus a 2.5 percent convenience fee.

All businesses in the city need an annual state business license, and the city's general license costs $25 to start and $25 to renew. A home business needs a separate permit. Renting out the house? Call the Business Licensing Specialist at 509-720-5333 to find out whether a rental needs a license or registration.

Selling a single-family rental that has a tenant requires 90 days of written notice under RCW 59.18.650, and you must list within 30 days after the tenant moves out.

Excise tax and recording steps

Money and paper both flow through the Spokane County Treasurer, and the order matters. Washington's excise tax on real estate touches nearly every sale. You deliver the affidavit and the deed to the Treasurer first, and the Spokane County Auditor records the deed afterward. Payment may be cash or a check made out to the Spokane County Treasurer, though cash should never go in the mail. Call 509-477-4713 with questions.

The state share begins at 1.1 percent of the price up to $525,000, then rises in higher tiers. A $382,300 median home value sits below that first break, and for sales from January 1, 2027 the break moves to $551,000. Your local rate is added, and the Treasurer or closing agent can quote it. Sellers usually pay. The state reads the notarized deed date as the sale date, and a payment more than a month late accrues interest.

Since the Treasurer sees the paperwork before the Auditor does, a missing signature or half-finished affidavit can stall recording. Check each line before you drive downtown, and ask a closing agent to review the packet if one is handling your sale.

Property tax due dates

Spokane County mails a single yearly statement that carries two coupons, one for each half of the tax.

  • Pay the first half by April 30 and the second by October 31.
  • When the total is under $50, everything is due April 30.
  • A deadline on a weekend or county holiday rolls to the next business day.
  • No statement in hand by March 31? Search for it on the county's SCOUT system or phone the Treasurer.

Find out your balance from the Treasurer before you sign. At closing, the agent splits the year's property tax between you and the buyer by closing date.

Separately, the state seller disclosure statement goes to the buyer within five business days of the contract being accepted. Three business days follow in which the buyer can rescind, unless that right was waived.

When a cash sale fits

Maybe you have repairs you would prefer not to make. That alone can be a reason to request a cash offer and set it beside a listing. Listing brings more buyers, but also showings, repair requests and a wait on the buyer's mortgage. A cash buyer offers speed and certainty and pays less in return.

Here is how it goes after you accept. Escrow opens and title is searched. Any loan is paid from proceeds, you sign before a notary, and the deed and affidavit go to the Treasurer and then to the Auditor for recording. Money is released after recording. Since no appraisal or lender review is needed, your calendar and the title work decide the date.

Put the deed, a loan payoff statement, permit records and your most recent tax statement on the table at your first meeting. If you altered the interior without a permit, stop by the Permit Center first and learn what an inspector could ask.

A tenant in the house changes the plan. Share the lease terms with the buyer before any offer is signed, and build the notice period into your closing date. Buyers who know about the tenant from the start rarely reopen the price later.

Frequently asked questions

How many people live in Spokane Valley, WA?

Roughly 108,405 as of July 1, 2025, up from 102,976 at the 2020 census. Incorporation took place on March 31, 2003.

When are Spokane County property taxes due?

Half by April 30 and half by October 31. Bills under $50 are due in full April 30, and a weekend or county holiday shifts the date to the next business day.

How do I pay the real estate excise tax on a Spokane Valley sale?

Deliver the affidavit and deed to the Spokane County Treasurer first. The Auditor records the deed after that. Pay with cash or a check made out to the Treasurer, and never mail cash.

Do I need a permit to remodel before selling in Spokane Valley?

Yes. A residential permit covers an interior alteration to a home, duplex or accessory structure, along with additions, decks, pools, spas and fences. Call the Permit Center at 509-720-5240.

Which school district is my Spokane Valley house in?

It varies by address. Central Valley, East Valley and West Valley serve most of the city, with part of the west in Spokane Public Schools. A district boundary map settles it.

Your options for a quick Renton sale

Selling a Renton house in a hurry comes down to three paths: hire an agent, go it alone, or let a cash buyer set a short timeline with you. Speed, price and hassle seldom move together, so decide which one you can least afford to lose.

  • An agent listing suits a home in good order when waiting out showings and loan approvals is acceptable.
  • A cash deal suits a house with repair needs, tenants, an estate, or a looming deadline.
  • A sale by owner only makes sense if you can handle the contract, the disclosure form and the excise tax affidavit yourself.

Judge every offer on the same four items: the price, the closing day, who covers closing costs, and how problems found in inspection get resolved.

Renton housing figures

Renton is an inner suburb about 11 miles southeast of downtown Seattle, on the southeast shore of Lake Washington at the mouth of the Cedar River. About 104,975 people lived here in July 2025, down 1.8 percent from the April 2020 estimates base. Commuters weigh price against drive time, so a home near the transit center or a freeway interchange often gets more attention than one with a long trip to either.

Close to half of households rent. Expect to meet sellers who are landlords, who inherited a rental, or who own a basement or backyard unit. If that sounds like you, the registration notes further down come first.

Schools, unincorporated areas and flood questions

Most of Renton is in the Renton School District. Smaller pockets fall in the Issaquah, Kent and Tahoma districts, so confirm the district for your address before you advertise. Fairwood, the East Renton Plateau and West Hill are unincorporated and are not part of the city, which matters if a buyer assumes city services and permits apply there.

Renton also has a flood history along the Cedar River, and the state disclosure form asks about flooding, drainage problems, floodplains and critical areas. Answer from what you know of your own lot, and look at current floodplain information for your address before you list.

If you are not sure which side of the city line your house sits on, check before you list. Permit rules, utilities and the office you call for records all depend on the answer.

Rental registration and accessory units

A tenant or a second unit on the lot changes your to-do list. Landlords and property managers register residential rentals each year on or before January 1. Covered properties include renter-occupied single family homes, condos, duplexes and apartment complexes, along with owner-occupied duplexes and homes that rent out an accessory dwelling unit. Registration is currently free. Short-term rentals and single room rentals need a City of Renton business license instead.

The program enforces the state Landlord-Tenant Act and the city's building standards. Once a violation is verified, the landlord has 15 days to respond and correct it. Clear any open warning before you sell a rental, because a buyer's inspector will find it.

Accessory units are easier to create than they used to be. Renton passed Ordinance 6160 on June 16, 2025 to comply with state House Bill 1337, and the Permit Ready ADU program offers eight pre-approved plans at no charge to owners inside city limits. A buyer who wants an ADU may value a lot with room for one, and you can say so in the listing. Check the city's current ADU rules before promising anything specific.

If you own a rental, walk through it once before you list. Look for anything that could draw a warning under the city's building standards, such as a broken smoke alarm or a failed handrail. A cleared record and a registration number in hand make a smoother conversation with a buyer, and with the buyer's lender if one is involved.

Excise tax at closing

The seller typically carries Washington's excise tax on real estate. Payment is made to the county treasurer, and the notarized deed date counts as the sale date for the Department of Revenue. Sales that begin January 1, 2027 are taxed by the state at 1.1 percent on the first $551,000 and 1.28 percent on the portion up to $1,551,000, with steeper tiers past that. The county's local share comes on top.

To learn the local share for a Renton address, and which tiers apply to a closing before the new year, ask escrow or the King County Recorder's Office.

Save paperwork supporting the price and any exemption. Four years is the retention period the Department of Revenue asks for, which also matches the window for requesting a refund.

Disclosure and property tax steps

Most improved residential sales require a seller disclosure statement (RCW 64.06.020). The buyer should have it within five business days of contract acceptance unless waived, and gets three business days afterward to rescind. Questions cover roof leaks in the last five years, flooding and drainage, shorelines, wetlands, floodplains, sewer hookup, and building permits for remodeling.

Because property tax travels with the parcel, the closing agent splits it between you and the buyer. April 30 is the first-half deadline and October 31 the second for bills of $50 or more (RCW 84.56.020). Pay the first half late and interest begins; on homes with four or fewer units the statute fixes it at 9 percent a year and bars extra penalties. Get a fresh King County Treasury statement before you sign so the contract matches the county's records.

What to gather before accepting an offer

Having the paperwork at hand speeds up every kind of sale. Put these in one folder:

  • Your deed and the newest loan payoff statement.
  • A rental registration number and lease copies when tenants live there.
  • Permit records for an ADU, basement unit or addition.
  • The latest King County property tax statement.

A cash purchase moves in short steps. Once you accept, escrow starts and the title company searches the record. The mortgage payoff comes out of your proceeds, the deed is signed in front of a notary, and the county receives the excise tax with the affidavit. Funds are released when the deed is recorded. With no appraisal and no lender sign-off to wait for, the date depends on title work and your own calendar.

When a tenant occupies the house, say so to the buyer early and share the lease. The disclosure form, your registration status and the lease need to line up.

Frequently asked questions

How fast can I sell my house in Renton, WA?

Cash deals can close as soon as the title work is finished, often on a day you choose. Listings run longer because of showings, inspections and the buyer's lender. Insist on a written closing date.

Do I need to register my Renton rental before I sell it?

When the rental is covered, register or confirm your registration before listing. Registration renews each year by January 1, and a verified violation must be fixed within 15 days of a warning. Short-term rentals use a business license.

Who pays the excise tax on a house sale in Renton?

Normally you do, as the seller. When the seller leaves it unpaid, the buyer becomes liable and a lien can follow. The county treasurer collects it, figured from the sale price.

Does the Cedar River flood history affect my sale?

It can, because the disclosure form asks about flooding, drainage problems, floodplains and critical areas. Answer from what you know about your own property, and check current floodplain information for your address before you list.

Can I sell a Renton house with an accessory unit?

Yes. Disclose the unit and confirm its permits, because the state form asks about permits and final inspections for conversions and additions. A rented unit should be part of your closing plan.

Ways to sell a Federal Way house

Three paths are open to a Federal Way owner: hire an agent, handle the sale personally, or hand the keys to a buyer who needs no mortgage. Weigh the house's shape, your moving date and what you still owe the lender.

Federal Way occupies the southwest corner of King County, roughly 25 miles south of Seattle, with 99,729 residents. The count is 1.3 percent lower than in 2020, so the city is not adding people. What Federal Way buyers notice

Green space adds appeal in some neighborhoods. Steel Lake Park is on South 312th Street, Lake Killarney is close by, and Dash Point State Park is the one developed waterfront park within city limits. A cabin from 1883 in West Hylebos Wetlands Park is the oldest known building in town.

A few eastern areas, including Star Lake, Camelot, Lakeland and Jovita, were named potential annexation areas. Confirm your parcel is inside the city before you call the Permit Center. The city's maps, the King County Parcel Viewer or the Permit Center itself can all supply a parcel number.

Excise tax when you sell

This one is the seller's bill. RCW 82.45.080 assigns Washington's real estate excise tax to the seller, payable to the county treasurer as of the sale date even if recording happens later. For a Federal Way deed, that treasurer is King County's.

Rates climb with price. The Department of Revenue currently shows 1.1 percent up to $525,000, then 1.28 percent to $1,525,000, 2.75 percent to $3,025,000, and 3 percent beyond. For sales on or after January 1, 2027 the breakpoints become $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. Cities add a local rate, which your escrow officer can quote for your parcel.

A month after the sale, penalty and interest start accruing, and a lien can follow an unpaid balance. Have escrow print the excise tax on its own line of your settlement statement.

Do I need a permit or approval before selling a Federal Way house?

Building, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, demolition and fire prevention permits, plus land use and sign permits, all go through the City of Federal Way Permit Center. It is the place to ask about repairs you want to finish before listing, or about work a former owner may have done unpermitted.

  • Phone and email: 253-835-2607 or permitcenter@federalwaywa.gov.
  • Hours: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Wednesdays and city holidays, the day after Thanksgiving among them, the public counter is shut.
  • Applications: request a Document Upload Link, which may take a few days, and submit reviewable plans electronically. Residential electrical, mechanical and plumbing permits can also be filed online through My Building Permit.

Be wary of an email that claims to be from the city and asks for a wire transfer. The city does not do that, so phone the Permit Center before sending money.

The first installment comes due April 30 and the second October 31. Under RCW 84.56.020 the county treasurer collects, which means King County. Pull the current statement for your parcel before listing, since title work will reveal any open balance. If you pay through a lender, still check the county record yourself so nothing surprises you at the closing table.

If closing falls mid-period, escrow divides the bill between you and the buyer. Confirm your latest payment has posted first, so the division starts from the right figure.

Commutes, transit and schools

Drivers reach Interstate 5 at the 348th Street, 320th Street and 272nd Street exits, and State Route 99, the Pacific Highway, cuts through town. Buses from King County Metro, Pierce Transit and Sound Transit Express stop at the Federal Way Transit Center on 23rd Avenue South, and the Link light rail extension to Federal Way Downtown station opened in December 2025. Commutes average 32.1 minutes, which makes quick freeway and station access worth advertising.

Federal Way Public Schools runs the local district. In your listing, mention the closest park, the nearest I-5 exit and how long the trip to the station takes.

What to check before you accept an offer

Offers can look alike on paper and still differ by thousands once costs are added up. Go through this list with each one.

  • Insist on a written offer listing price, closing date and the party responsible for each closing cost.
  • Ask your lender for a payoff statement showing the precise balance.
  • Have the buyer prove funds, and learn whether repairs or an inspection can change the deal.
  • Run the excise tax rates above, then ask escrow for the local rate.
  • Clarify whether the house must be cleared out, and by when.
  • Rank routes by the money you would walk away with, not by the advertised price.

If a tenant lives in the house, read the lease before promising a closing date, since a buyer will need to know who occupies the home and for how long.

Disclosure form timing

Under RCW 64.06.020, a seller of improved residential property owes the buyer a finished disclosure statement. The clock is five business days from acceptance of a written contract, and a buyer may waive the form or the transfer may be exempt. Once it arrives, the buyer has three business days to back out.

Answer only from your own knowledge of the roof, plumbing, sewer and past repairs. A folder holding permit history, loan payoff and tax statement makes the form faster to fill in and buyer follow-ups easier to answer. Cash buyers ask the same things, just without an appraiser or underwriter second-guessing the replies.

Frequently asked questions

Who pays the real estate excise tax on a house sale in Federal Way?

The seller, under RCW 82.45.080. If the seller leaves it unpaid, responsibility shifts to the buyer and a lien may attach to the property.

When are property taxes due on a Federal Way house?

Half is due April 30 and half October 31, paid through King County. Request the latest statement for your parcel from the county.

Which county is Federal Way in?

King County, in its southwest corner about 25 miles south of Seattle. Deeds, excise tax affidavits and property tax bills for a Federal Way home all run through King County offices.

How do I find my parcel number in Federal Way?

Look it up on the city's maps or the King County Parcel Viewer, or ask the Permit Center at 253-835-2607 or permitcenter@federalwaywa.gov. Permit questions and title work both call for it.

Do I have to give a buyer a seller disclosure statement?

Most sellers do. The finished form is due five business days after a written contract is accepted, unless it is waived or the transfer is exempt. Three business days after delivery, the buyer's right to rescind ends.

Selling fast in Yakima

A sale to a cash buyer is typically the quickest path, since it takes the buyer's mortgage approval and appraisal out of the schedule. A listing can still bring a higher price if the house shows well and you can wait for the right offer.

Yakima is the seat of Yakima County, in the Upper Valley about 60 miles southeast of Mount Rainier, and about 97,458 people live there. West Valley and Terrace Heights are unincorporated suburbs treated as part of greater Yakima, so confirm whether your address is inside city limits before you check any city rule. Agriculture drives the local economy, and downtown, once the retail hub, has seen the regional retail core move to Union Gap.

Yakima housing numbers

The median home value is $297,600, and 53.8 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. About 46 percent of housing units are not owner-occupied, so rentals make up a large part of the local market. That often means landlords and investors are among your likely buyers.
