Summer heat and your house

Yakima has a cold semi-arid climate and sits at 1,095 feet above sea level. Summers are hot: the city averages 40.2 afternoons a year at 90 degrees or higher and 5.7 at 100 or higher, and July days and nights differ by nearly 35 degrees. Roofing, attic insulation, cooling equipment and exterior paint carry the load from those swings, so collect receipts or warranties for them before you list.

Winter brings about 21.6 inches of snow a year, mostly in December and January. The average last freeze of spring comes on May 13 and the first freeze of fall around September 30, which is useful to know if you are planning outdoor repairs. Hot summers are also when buyers test the cooling system, so a recent service record helps.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Yakima house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Schools and commuting

The Yakima School District runs four high schools in the city: Davis High School, Eisenhower High School, Stanton Academy and Yakima Online High School. West Valley High School is in the West Valley School District, and East Valley High School, just east of Terrace Heights, is in the East Valley School District. Call the district office to verify the boundaries for your street.

Interstate 82 is the main freeway, with U.S. Route 12 crossing the north of the city. The average commute for city workers is 17.8 minutes.

Which repairs need a permit in Yakima?

The city's Code Administration office handles permits. Some jobs can be applied for online without plan review:

  • Same-for-same plumbing and mechanical change-outs
  • Residential reroofs that are tear off and reroof only
  • Water and sewer line replacements
  • Residential re-siding
  • Oil tank abandonment and removal
  • Woodstove or wood-burning device installation

A remodel needs a building permit application plus plans showing existing and proposed floor plans and wall details. Land use review may be needed first, and the building permit is not issued until it is approved. Electrical permits go through the state Department of Labor and Industries, at (509) 454-3700 for the Yakima office. Questions about the process go to codes@yakimawa.gov or (509) 575-6126, and applications run through buildingyakima.com.

A vacant house or one in poor shape

The city responds to complaints about conditions on private property, including garbage, overgrown yards, junk vehicles and vacant buildings that are open to unauthorized entry. In March 2024 the City Council adopted the 2021 International Property Maintenance Code, with local changes, as YMC Chapter 11.40.

Anyone directly affected by a notice or order can appeal to the hearing examiner, provided a written appeal is filed within 20 days after service. Reports and questions go through the Yak Back portal or the hotline at (509) 576-6657.

If you inherited a vacant house and have not yet secured it, securing it early gives you more options with a buyer, whether that buyer is a family or an investor planning a rehab. Fix or document any open notice before showings begin, so a buyer never finds it first.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Yakima houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How a deed transfer works in Yakima County

Yakima County splits the job between two offices. Every transfer of real property needs a Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit processed through the County Treasurer's Office with the conveyance document. The Auditor's Recording Division then records the document. Excise tax and transfer fees must be paid in cash or certified funds.

The same order applies statewide under RCW 82.45.090, which keeps the auditor from recording a deed ahead of the tax payment or a not-due notation. The amount includes both a state and a local portion, so ask the Yakima County Treasurer what applies at your price.

A mobile home follows a different path. If the sale does not require moving it, a Mobile Home Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit is used, and the Auditor's Vehicle Licensing Division handles the new owner's title. Property taxes must be paid in full before that processing.

The seller disclosure and offers

For a house, the seller also fills out the condition form from RCW 64.06.020 and gives it to the buyer shortly after contract, with five business days as the default limit.

When offers come in, compare what you would net after repairs and carrying costs, ask who pays the excise tax, and get the closing date in writing. A cash buyer will often take an older roof or siding as it is, which saves you from doing the work first. A title or escrow company can walk the affidavit and deed through both county offices.

Before you accept, gather the paperwork a buyer will ask about: receipts or warranties for the roof, siding, cooling equipment and exterior paint, permits for any remodel, and any notice or order from the city. Known defects and unpermitted work belong on the disclosure form. If the house has a tenant or stored belongings, agree in writing on what stays and when the house will be empty.

A cash sale skips the appraisal and loan approval, so the timeline depends mostly on title work, the county steps above and your own move. A listing adds showings and the buyer's financing, which is worth the wait if the house shows well and you are in no hurry.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a Yakima house with an old roof or siding?

Yes. Plenty of buyers take older roofs and siding as they are. If you decide to fix them first, the city lets residential reroofs (tear off and reroof only) and re-siding be applied for online without plan review.

What payment form does Yakima County accept for excise tax?

Cash or certified funds. Excise tax and transfer fees must be paid that way at the County Treasurer's Office.

Can I appeal a city notice about my Yakima property?

Yes. Anyone directly affected by a property maintenance decision, notice or order may appeal to the hearing examiner. The written appeal must be filed within 20 days after the notice is served.

Where do I get an electrical permit in Yakima?

From the state Department of Labor and Industries, not the city. The Yakima office is at 15 W Yakima Ave., Suite 100, and the phone number is (509) 454-3700.

Is my house in the Yakima School District?

It depends on the address. The Yakima School District runs Davis, Eisenhower, Stanton Academy and Yakima Online, while West Valley and East Valley are separate districts. Call the district office to verify the boundaries for your street.

How to sell a house fast in Kirkland

You can sell in Kirkland by listing with an agent, going without one, or taking a cash offer from a buyer who needs no mortgage. Cash skips loan approval and often the repair list, so it is the fastest. All three roads finish at the same Washington closing items: excise tax, a prorated property tax bill and a completed seller disclosure statement.

Owning here is costly. An owner-occupied home has a median value of $1,115,400, and 60.8 percent of homes are lived in by owners. With numbers that high, the stepped state excise tax and the upkeep on an empty house both weigh heavily, which can make a quick close worth real money.

Kirkland neighborhoods

The city occupies Lake Washington's eastern shore, and downtown curves around Moss Bay, where condominiums built since the 1990s are common. Interstate 405 ties Kirkland to Bellevue, Renton and Bothell, while State Route 520 heads to Seattle and Redmond. Because several areas were annexed over time, a Finn Hill house may differ sharply in lot size, age and street layout from a Moss Bay one, and appraisers compare each home with its own surroundings.

  • Moss Bay and downtown: condominiums, apartments and the waterfront.
  • Houghton: where the first homesteads went up in the late 1860s.
  • Rose Hill: North and South Rose Hill, annexed in 1988.
  • Totem Lake: annexed in 1974 and served by Sound Transit and Community Transit buses on I-405.
  • Juanita, Finn Hill and Kingsgate: the northern neighborhoods, with Finn Hill, North Juanita and Kingsgate annexed in 2011.

The Lake Washington School District covers most of Kirkland, with smaller pieces in the Bellevue and Northshore districts. Look up your address before writing about schools.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Kirkland house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Taxes and fees at closing

Washington's real estate excise tax is ordinarily the seller's cost and goes to the county treasurer as of the sale date. Leave it unpaid and it can turn into a lien, with interest running once a month has gone by. Your escrow officer can quote the combined total, since the city's local excise tax sits on top of the state share.

RCW 82.45.060 builds the state share in four steps. For closings on or after January 1, 2027, the Department of Revenue shows these bands:

  • Up to $551,000: 1.1 percent.
  • $551,000 to $1,551,000: 1.28 percent.
  • $1,551,000 to $3,051,000: 2.75 percent.
  • Over $3,051,000: 3 percent.

A closing before January 1, 2027 falls under the earlier bands, and escrow will apply the right set. More detail sits on the Department of Revenue excise tax page.

King County property tax due dates

The bill splits into April 30 and October 31 payments, and the first-half deadline ahead is April 30, 2027. Pay the King County Treasury online, by mail postmarked on or before the due date, at the counter at 201 S. Jackson Street in Seattle, or in that building's drop box.

If a sale closes mid-year, escrow divides the bill between you and the buyer. Look in the online portal to be sure your last payment was credited before closing day. The King County Assessor runs exemption and deferral programs that seniors and people with disabilities may qualify for.

Selling a Kirkland house with tenants or a short-term rental

You can, though Kirkland regards renting as a business. Both long-term and short-term rentals need a city business license, and running one without it can be a misdemeanor. Expect a buyer planning to keep the rental to ask for the license history.

Stays under 30 days are governed by Ordinance O-4607. For single-family homes the main limits are:

  • Full-time resident owner or agent: no yearly day cap, with up to two rentals at once.
  • Owner or agent living there at least 245 days a year: up to 120 rental days a year.
  • Nobody home: name a property manager located within 15 miles to the city.
  • Parking: one stall per rental, plus two extra stalls when permanent residents share the home.

The business license carries a $100 base fee plus a $130 per-employee regulatory fee, which comes to $230 for many short-term rentals. The city levies no business and occupation tax. Condominiums are generally outside these rules, though association rules still apply, and owners remain responsible for lodging tax under state law.

Seller disclosure in Kirkland

RCW 64.06.020 obliges the seller of improved residential property to give the buyer a finished disclosure statement, unless it is waived or the transfer is exempt. Questions cover sewer or septic, roof leaks within five years, structural trouble, and hazards like lead-based paint or storage tanks. You report only what you know. Once the form is delivered, the buyer can rescind for three business days unless both sides agree otherwise in writing.

Fill in every line and write NA where a question does not apply, because a half-finished form breeds disputes whether the buyer finances or pays cash. Winter inspections happen in the wettest weather, which exposes roof, gutter and drainage flaws fast. Repair those before listing, or sell as-is to a cash buyer who does not care about the season.

What happens between offer and closing

After you say yes to an offer, escrow combines your loan payoff, the excise tax and your property tax share on one settlement statement. You sign the deed, the affidavit and payment reach the county treasurer, and the transfer is recorded. A cash purchase has no appraisal visit and no loan committee, so title work and the date you pick set the pace.

Before listing, pull together the deed, your newest tax statement, rental license papers and repair records. That folder cuts down the back-and-forth with buyers, escrow and the title company. If the house was inherited, add the paperwork showing who may sign, because title work cannot move until that is settled. If you rent it out, include the business license and any lease, since those are the first items a buyer asks about.

Frequently asked questions

How fast can a Kirkland house sell for cash?

Usually faster than a financed sale, since no lender must approve anything. Title work and your chosen closing date set the timing, and the excise tax and recorded deed are still required.

Who pays the real estate excise tax in Kirkland?

Typically the seller. If it goes unpaid, the buyer is on the hook. King County's treasurer collects it as of the sale date, and interest begins after a month.

Do I need a business license to rent my Kirkland house before selling?

Yes. The city wants a business license for long-term and short-term rentals, and short-term rentals need a state license as well. Renting without one can be a misdemeanor, so fix that before a buyer looks at your records.

Are King County property taxes still due if I am selling?

Yes, up to closing. April 30 and October 31 are the due dates, and escrow prorates the bill at the table. Use the Treasury's online portal to confirm your payment posted.

Can I sell an inherited house in Kirkland?

Yes, as soon as someone with legal authority to sign the deed is in place. A Washington estate attorney or your title company can tell you who that is. The deed still travels with an excise tax affidavit to the King County treasurer.

Selling in Bellingham

Bellingham is a bayfront city of 96,395 people (July 1, 2025) and the seat of Whatcom County. A seller here can hire an agent, go it alone, or accept cash from a buyer with no mortgage. Western Washington University, Whatcom Community College and Bellingham Technical College keep rental and starter-home demand steady, and renters outnumber owners here, so many buyers are investors.

Housing measureBellingham figure
Owner-occupied housing rate, 2020 to 202444.6%
Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020 to 2024$627,500
Median gross rent, 2020 to 2024$1,577
Households, 2020 to 202441,500
Population, 2020 Census91,482

Neighborhoods and school districts

Buyers sort Bellingham by neighborhood before anything else. The city recognizes areas such as Alabama Hill, Barkley, Birchwood, Cordata, Cornwall Park, Edgemoor, Fairhaven, Happy Valley, the Lettered Streets, Roosevelt, Samish, Sehome, South Hill, Sunnyland, Whatcom Falls and York, along with the university district.

  • Fairhaven has a historic commercial district.
  • Sehome is part of today's downtown.
  • Cordata has a Whatcom Transportation Authority station near Bellis Fair Mall.
  • Alabama Hill is one of the higher points in town, at about 500 feet.

Most addresses sit in the Bellingham School District, with four public high schools: Bellingham, Options, Sehome and Squalicum. One small northern piece of the city belongs to the Meridian School District. Look up the district for your street before you put a school name in an ad.

Roads, water and weather

Interstate 5 splits Bellingham and links it to Seattle and Vancouver. State Route 539 heads to Lynden and the border, and State Route 542 climbs toward Mount Baker. Whatcom Transportation Authority runs frequent Go Lines on several corridors, and Amtrak Cascades stops at Fairhaven Station twice a day.

Rainfall averages 34.84 inches a year, with November the wettest month. A winter pattern called a north-Easter can push Arctic air down the Fraser River Canyon with strong wind, and a warm Pineapple Express spell can melt snow fast enough to strain drainage. Inspectors and buyers look first at roofs, gutters, crawl spaces and drainage.

Lake Whatcom supplies the city's drinking water and forms part of its eastern edge, which is why short-term rentals are barred inside the watershed.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Bellingham house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Landlord and short-term rental rules

Bellingham runs a Rental Registration and Safety Inspection Program under Bellingham Municipal Code 6.15. Owners register each rental, pass a safety inspection before renting, renew the rental license every year, and have the property re-inspected about every three to three and a half years. The program now requires a city checklist for private inspectors and offers a single appeal step. Tenants get 120 days of notice before a rent increase, and an increase of 8 percent or more triggers relocation assistance under BMC 6.14.

  • Short-term rentals fall under BMC 20.10.037 and need a land use permit.
  • In residential zones the operator must live there at least 270 days a year, and the whole home can be rented no more than 95 days a year.
  • Short-term rentals are not allowed in the Lake Whatcom watershed or in shoreline areas.
  • Detached accessory dwelling units cannot be short-term rentals in single-family zones.

Inherited a rented Bellingham house? Call the Permit Center at 360-778-8300 and ask for the registration and inspection record before you list.

Closing costs and excise tax

Washington puts real estate excise tax on the seller, and RCW 82.45.060 scales the state share by price. Sales closing on or after January 1, 2027 pay 1.1 percent of the first $551,000, 1.28 percent of the slice to $1,551,000, 2.75 percent of the slice to $3,051,000, and 3 percent of everything over that. The county treasurer adds the local rate for your parcel.

  • The obligation is yours under RCW 82.45.080, and payment is due when the sale happens.
  • Wait too long and RCW 82.45.100 adds interest after one month, then penalties of 5, 10 and 20 percent at one, two and three months.
  • A Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit must reach the Whatcom County Treasurer, on the first floor of the courthouse at 360-778-5160, before the Auditor will record the deed.
  • The deed's first page needs a three inch top margin, grantor and grantee names, a legal description and the 16 digit assessor parcel number.

Separately, a finished disclosure statement goes to the buyer under RCW 64.06.020. Plan on five business days after signing. The buyer may waive it and some transfers are exempt; otherwise the buyer holds a three-business-day right to rescind once it arrives.

Whatcom County property tax dates

Whatcom County mails bills in mid-February. Pay one half by April 30 and the other by October 31. A bill under $50 is one payment, due April 30. Deadlines that fall on a weekend or holiday slide to the next business day. Skipping the first half turns the whole year delinquent, with interest and penalty figured on the full year at the rates in RCW 84.56.020.

Closing in spring or fall? Ask the closing agent how the half-year then in progress gets split with the buyer. A missing statement does not stop interest, so look up the bill online even when nothing arrives by mail.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Bellingham houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Your options for a quick sale

Most Bellingham sellers pick one of three routes. Condition, tenants and your target closing date decide which.

  • List with an agent and prepare for showings, which suits a clean, vacant property in a sought-after neighborhood.
  • Sell it yourself, which saves the commission but leaves marketing, disclosure forms and negotiation to you.
  • Accept a cash offer, which suits deferred repairs, a rental that failed inspection, an inheritance or a short fuse.

Whichever you choose, pull together the last tax statement, rental registration papers, utility account details and the recorded deed. Then weigh a cash offer against the listing net once commission, repairs and holding costs come out.

What happens after you accept an offer

Escrow opens and title work turns up unpaid taxes or liens. You sign the affidavit and deed; the treasurer takes the excise tax first and only then can the deed be recorded. Sellers of a rental should confirm the city registration is current, since buyers often ask. With no lender involved there is no appraisal or loan sign-off, so title work and your own documents set the date.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell my Bellingham house as-is?

Yes. As-is does not cancel the disclosure statement, which Washington still expects unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt. Be honest about known defects.

Who pays excise tax on a Bellingham sale?

You do, as seller. The state share starts at 1.1 percent and rises with price, and the county treasurer adds the local rate when the affidavit is filed.

When are Whatcom County property taxes due?

Half by April 30, half by October 31. A bill under $50 is paid once, in April, and weekend or holiday deadlines roll forward a business day.

Do I need to deal with the rental program if my Bellingham house was a rental?

Yes. While the house is rented, the owner keeps the city registration current and renews it every year. Ask the Permit Center at 360-778-8300 about the registration and the last safety inspection before you sell.

Can a buyer use my Bellingham house as a short-term rental?

Ways to sell a Kennewick house

Kennewick homeowners have three realistic routes: list through an agent, deal directly with another household, or take a cash purchase. Which one fits turns on your timeline, your repair list and how much you still owe.

  • Agent sale: someone else stages, shows and negotiates. Best for a home in decent shape when you can wait for the right buyer.
  • Private sale: pricing, marketing and the contract are your job. You save on fees and spend more time.
  • Cash purchase: with no lender involved, loan approval drops off the schedule. Measure every offer by the check you would receive at closing.

Kennewick housing at a glance

The city lies in Benton County, on the Columbia, and ranks first among the Tri-Cities by size, with Richland upstream and Pasco across the water. Population is 88,366, up 5.3 percent from 2020. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $370,700, a citywide midpoint that says little about any single house.

Hanford and the national laboratory still shape the local economy, alongside agriculture and health care, and growth at the Port of Morrow in Hermiston has pulled more residents into commuting to jobs there.

Irrigation, utilities and flood history

Water works differently in Kennewick than in many cities. The city supplies drinking water and sewer, Benton Public Utility District provides electricity and Cascade Natural Gas provides gas. Many owners water lawns with irrigation water delivered separately by the Kennewick Irrigation District, or by the Columbia Irrigation District on parts of the east side. Ask the district that serves your address for any assessment balance before closing.

Flooding is part of the record. The worst Columbia River flood came in 1948 and led to the McNary Levee System, and the river threat has dropped since the dams went in. Zintel Canyon Dam near the Southridge Sports and Events Complex protects parts of the city from a 100-year flood, but summer thunderstorms over the Horse Heaven Hills can still send flash floods down the dry creek. Ask the city for the status of your parcel if you are near that canyon.

Benton County taxes and filings

One office, the Benton County Treasurer, bills property tax for the county, cities, school districts, fire departments and other taxing districts, using values set by the Assessor. Stop by the Kennewick location at 7122 W Okanogan Pl, Suite E110, Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., or call 509-735-8505.

  • Property tax: a bill of $50 or more splits into two payments, April 30 and October 31, per RCW 84.56.020. Anything paid past those days is delinquent.
  • Excise tax: sellers normally owe Washington's real estate excise tax. A price within the first $525,000 bracket is taxed by the state at 1.1 percent, plus a local rate.
  • Forms: the treasurer's forms page carries the Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit, a supplemental statement and a refund request.

Excise tax is due to the county treasurer on the sale date, with penalty and interest if it sits unpaid for a month. Your escrow officer will normally prepare the affidavit.

Which projects need a permit in Kennewick?

Small fixes before a sale may not need one. Kennewick's Building Safety Division exempts these from a building permit:

  • a detached accessory structure of 200 square feet or less that meets setbacks and avoids easements
  • retaining walls up to 4 feet high
  • finish work such as painting, tiling, carpeting and cabinets
  • prefabricated pools under 24 inches deep
  • window awnings projecting 54 inches or less

A new single-family residence of up to two units needs a building permit but no land use permit. Questions go to Building Safety at 509-585-4276 or Community Planning at 509-585-4280.

Roads, schools and transit

Interstate 82 passes south of the city and connects to Seattle through I-90 and to Portland through I-84. U.S. 395 runs north to south, State Route 240 crosses the Blue Bridge to Pasco, and State Route 397 crosses the Cable Bridge. Ben Franklin Transit runs routes through two transit centers, Three Rivers near the Toyota Center and Dayton Transfer Point downtown. Commutes average 21.3 minutes, and the nearest commercial airport is Tri-Cities Airport in Pasco.

The Kennewick School District runs 17 elementary schools, five middle schools and three high schools for more than 18,000 students. Confirm the zone for your address when you advertise.

  • See price, closing date and each cost you will carry spelled out on paper.
  • Get your lender's payoff, then take away that amount, the excise tax and any irrigation balance. What remains is your true take.
  • Have the buyer describe the funding and name anything that hinges on an inspection.
  • Ask Building Safety whether a shed, addition or remodel you doubt was ever permitted.
  • Learn the current tax status of your parcel from the Benton County Treasurer.

Utility accounts to hand over

Kennewick buyers deal with several providers, so a short list saves them a scramble. The city bills for drinking water and sewer. Benton Public Utility District supplies electricity, and Cascade Natural Gas supplies gas. Lawn irrigation is separate again, through the Kennewick Irrigation District or, on parts of the east side, the Columbia Irrigation District.

Write down the account details for each one and mention in your listing that irrigation water is delivered apart from city service. A buyer from outside the area may not expect that, and an assessment balance owed to the irrigation district can show up in the title search if it is not cleared before closing.

From acceptance to closing

Accepting an offer opens escrow and sends the title company searching. Liens, overdue property tax and irrigation district balances surface in that search, so clear them early. A loan payoff statement from your lender also goes to escrow.

The affidavit gets drawn up at closing and the tax goes to the county treasurer. One folder with permit papers, your latest tax statement and irrigation bills lets you answer buyer or escrow questions the same day. Cash buyers frequently skip the appraisal and loan committee, so their closings can come sooner. If the buyer needs time to arrange funds, the offer should say how long and what happens if the date slips.

Which county is Kennewick in, and where do I pay property tax?

Benton County. Pay the county treasurer, who bills for the county, the city and school districts. The Kennewick location is 7122 W Okanogan Pl, Suite E110, phone 509-735-8505.

When are property taxes due on a Benton County house?

Half by April 30 and the rest by October 31, per RCW 84.56.020. Later payments are delinquent and pick up interest and penalties. The treasurer can give you a current statement for your parcel.

Do I need a permit to put up a shed in Kennewick?

Sometimes not. A detached accessory structure of 200 square feet or less skips the building permit when it meets setbacks and avoids easements. Larger sheds need one. Building Safety is at 509-585-4276.

Which school district serves Kennewick?

Public schools come from the Kennewick School District. It enrolls over 18,000 students across 17 elementary, five middle and three high schools, and it helps fund the Tri-Tech Skills Center.

Does the Columbia River still flood Kennewick?

The river risk has dropped since the dams and the McNary Levee System were built after the 1948 flood. Flash floods from the Horse Heaven Hills can still occur in Zintel Canyon during summer thunderstorms. Ask the city about your parcel.

Auburn at a glance

Auburn has 86,301 residents (July 1, 2025). About 60.6% of homes are owner-occupied, households average 2.79 people, and owner-occupied homes were worth a median $547,900 across 2020 to 2024. Median household income was $97,884 and the average commute was 30.5 minutes. Most of Auburn lies in King County. A sliver reaches into Pierce County, and that decides who sends your tax bill.

Auburn grew by annexation. In 2008 it took in the West Hill and Lea Hill areas of unincorporated King County, about 15,000 residents, and on January 1, 2024 it added the 155-acre Bridges neighborhood from Kent. Lakeland Hills, the master-planned community southeast of downtown, is split between King and Pierce counties.

Is the address really inside Auburn?

An "Auburn" mailing address does not always mean the City of Auburn. Some addresses that carry the name belong to King County, Kent or Federal Way. Before you assume city permit and rental rules apply, run the property through the city's interactive map. A wrong guess can send you to the wrong office for permits and change which tax bill you pay.

School districts

Most of the city is in the Auburn School District, which also serves Algona, Pacific and some unincorporated areas. Parts of north Auburn are in the Federal Way and Kent districts, and the Pierce County portion falls in the Dieringer School District. District lines follow streets, so look up your own address before listing. Buyers with children ask first, and the answer can differ between two houses on the same road. Put the district name in your listing notes so nobody has to guess.

Getting around

State Route 167 (the Valley Freeway) and State Route 18 run through town. Sounder trains from Auburn station reach downtown Seattle in about 30 minutes, Sound Transit buses connect to Federal Way, Sumner and Kent, and King County Metro buses serve Auburn Way and Green River College. Highlight the commute options in your listing, since many Auburn buyers work elsewhere in the valley or in Seattle.

Do I need a rental license in Auburn?

For most rentals, yes. Auburn requires an owner to hold a Rental Housing License for most forms of renting residential property, so the city has current ownership and management details for homes the owner does not live in. Selling a house with tenants in it? Check that the license is current first. Rental license rules are in Auburn City Code 5.22, and the Permit Center answers questions at 253-931-3090, option 2.

Rental typeCity requirement

ApartmentsCity business license required; no inspection.

Permits and disclosures

Auburn takes permit applications online through MyBuildingPermit.com. Electrical permits inside city limits come from the Washington Department of Labor and Industries. A house on a septic system needs approval from the King County or Pierce County health department for most changes. If you built a deck, finished a basement or changed wiring, find out now whether a permit exists, because buyers and inspectors ask.

Washington also hands you a form to complete. Under RCW 64.06.020 you complete a disclosure statement on the property and deliver it after both sides sign a written contract. The deadline is five business days from mutual acceptance. Two exceptions exist: the buyer waived the form, or the transfer is exempt. Once the buyer has it, a three-business-day window opens in which the buyer may rescind. The form opens with questions on title and water, so pull your records together before you list.

Property tax and closing

King County parcels are billed by the King County treasurer. Pierce County parcels go through the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer, (253) 798-6111. The two installments fall on April 30 and October 31 (RCW 84.56.020). The lien starts January 1. Absent a contract term, RCW 84.60.020 assigns each of you the days you owned the house, and escrow runs the numbers at closing.

The seller generally pays the state's excise tax on the transfer, remitted to the county treasurer on the day of sale. Under the schedule for sales starting January 1, 2027, price up to $551,000 is taxed at 1.1%, price between that and $1,551,000 at 1.28%, and anything above at higher rates. Auburn's median value of $547,900 sits just under the first bracket, so a typical sale there would pay the lowest state rate plus the local share. Your closing agent can confirm the local rate and any exemption.

Senior and disabled exemption

RCW 84.36.381 offers a property tax exemption to owners who are 61 or older, to certain disabled owners, and to some who served in the military. If you sell, the status can follow you to a replacement home. The county assessor has the current income limits.

What to have ready for escrow

Gather these before you accept an offer: your latest tax statement from whichever county bills you, any permit records for decks, basement work or wiring, the rental license if tenants live in the house, and the completed disclosure form. If the house is on a septic system, add the health department approvals. A buyer who sees complete records tends to move faster, and escrow can answer payoff questions without chasing you for papers. If anything is missing, the Permit Center line above is the first call for city records, and the county treasurer is the call for tax balances.

How a sale usually runs

Step one is checking which county and which school district the house falls in. Step two is gathering permit records, rental license paperwork if tenants live there, and your latest tax statement. Step three is completing the disclosure form and handing it over within the five-business-day window. Escrow then orders title work, prorates taxes and settles any unpaid balance from your proceeds. With a cash purchase there is no lender appraisal or underwriting to wait on, so timing rests on title work and how fast your own paperwork is ready.

Frequently asked questions

Which county bills my Auburn property tax?

Most Auburn parcels are in King County and are billed by the King County treasurer. Homes in the Pierce County portion, including part of Lakeland Hills, are billed by the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer.

Does my Auburn mailing address mean I am inside city limits?

Not always. Some addresses that include Auburn fall under King County, Kent or Federal Way. Use the city's interactive map before assuming city permit and rental rules apply.

Do I need a city license to rent rooms in my Auburn home?

You need a City of Auburn business license if you rent rooms to more than two people. Renting to two or fewer people in an owner-occupied home does not require one, and the occupancy limit is family plus 2.

How soon does the buyer get my disclosure statement?

Five business days from the moment both sides accept the written contract. The form can be skipped if the buyer waived it or the transfer is exempt, and the buyer gets three business days after delivery to rescind.

What state transfer tax rate would apply to a typical Auburn sale?

The first bracket for sales starting January 1, 2027 is 1.1% up to $551,000, and Auburn's $547,900 median value sits inside it. A local rate comes on top.

Heat, cold and the items buyers check

Pasco sits in the rain shadow of the Cascade Range, so it is dry and windy. Summers run hot, and winters can get cold enough to freeze pipes. A few items get extra attention from buyers:

  • Air conditioning age and capacity, since cooling runs for months.
  • Roof condition and attic insulation under strong summer sun.
  • Irrigation systems and landscaping that live on little rain.

Schools

The Pasco School District runs the city's public schools. Pasco High School and Chiawana High School are the longer-standing high schools, and Sageview High School opened in 2025 to relieve crowding at Chiawana. Delta High School, a STEM program shared with the Kennewick and Richland districts, opened in 2015. Confirm the boundary for your address with the district before you quote a school in an ad, and tell buyers which of these campuses is closest.

City permit and rental rules

Pasco's Ordinance No. 4770, adopted June 2, 2025, removed permit requirements for several small jobs, listed on the city's permit page. They matter if you want to tidy the house before listing:

  • One-story detached sheds or playhouses up to 200 square feet in residential areas.
  • Fences under 7 feet, retaining walls under 4 feet, and decks under 200 square feet and 30 inches high.
  • Residential roofing and siding replacement limited to shingles, underlayment, flashing, siding, barrier and veneer.

Structural work, anything habitable, and building in an easement or too close to a property line still need a permit. A permit is good for 180 days from issue, and passing an inspection renews that clock.

The city's ADU guide, published in 2023, allows one attached or detached ADU per residential parcel, up to 1,000 square feet or 55 percent of the main house, whichever is less. The unit must be long-term housing, with occupants living there more than 180 days a year, and short-term rentals are not allowed. Landlords need a rental business license under PMC 5.60.010. Call Pasco Community and Economic Development at (509) 545-3441 to confirm current rules for your zone.

Excise tax on a Pasco sale

This one is the seller's bill under RCW 82.45.080. State tax starts at 1.1% and tops out at 3% on the highest slice, and a local portion is added. Franklin County property taxes at closing

Taxes are payable on or after February 15, with the full amount due by April 30. Bills over $50 may be split, half by April 30 and half by October 31. The Treasurer is at 1016 N 4th Avenue in Pasco, phone 509-545-3518.

For real property, the Treasurer starts foreclosure action when taxes have been delinquent for three years, so a seller with old arrears should pay them off at closing. Ask your closing officer for a current tax status before you sign.

A deduction may be available to owners who are 61 or older or disabled, and to certain disabled service members. Applications go to the Franklin County Assessor, 509-545-3506. If you are selling because you can no longer keep up with the house, ask whether a reduction would have applied in a prior year. Taking five minutes to call the Assessor before closing can show a break you missed, and it costs nothing to ask.

Seller disclosure

An improved residential property needs a seller disclosure statement, handed over five business days after mutual acceptance unless the buyer waives it or the sale is exempt. List cooling, roof and irrigation history, which dry-climate buyers ask about most.

Your selling options in Pasco

Pasco owners pick among an agent listing, a sale without an agent and an as-is cash deal. The deed, affidavit and tax steps do not change, so timing, condition and price decide.

  • Listing works when the house is in good shape and you can sit through showings and a buyer's financing.
  • Selling as-is for cash works better for deferred repairs, a tenant in place or an inherited property.
  • Whoever the buyer is, ask who pays the excise tax, how the sale date is set and how back taxes are dealt with.

If you inherited the house, check the tax status first. Old arrears are easier to clear from proceeds at closing than after, and the Treasurer can tell you where the account stands. A tenant in place calls for a lease copy and a plan for notice, so raise both with any buyer early. Whatever route you choose, line up the permit history, since sheds, fences and roofing changes are the items most likely to come up.

Payment opens February 15. The whole bill is due April 30, or if it is over $50 you may pay half then and half by October 31.

Can I rent out an ADU in Pasco as a vacation rental?

No. The city's ADU guide requires long-term residential use, with occupants living there more than 180 days a year, and short-term rentals are not allowed.

Not for a shingle, underlayment and flashing replacement. Ordinance 4770 removed that requirement, but structural roof work still needs a permit.

A cash buyer needs no loan approval, so title work and your own plans mostly set the timeline. Ask every bidder to put price, closing day, who pays which costs and any repair credit on paper, then compare the offers side by side.

Over half of Redmond households rent. Plenty of sellers are therefore retired landlords or heirs who inherited a rental, and the permit and short-term rental notes below may apply to you.

Housing measureRedmond, 2020 to 2024
Median value of owner-occupied homes$1,167,800
Households living in a home they own43.2%

Medians blend condos with big lots. For a real read on your house, look at what sold recently close to your address.

Median rent of $2,409 a month is worth noting if you are weighing whether to keep a rental or sell it.

Neighborhoods, light rail and schools

Overlake, southwest of downtown, holds the Microsoft headquarters plus apartments and houses. Education Hill lies north of downtown. New construction has concentrated downtown and in Overlake, both on the 2 Line light rail. That line's first stretch began service in April 2024, and trains reached Downtown Redmond on May 10, 2025.

Nearly all of Redmond is in the Lake Washington School District. The southernmost blocks, mainly below NE 40th Street, fall under the Bellevue School District, and the unincorporated English Hill area belongs to Northshore. Buyers filter listings by district, so put yours in the description.

What the state disclosure form covers

Washington's seller disclosure form digs into water problems and construction history, and buyers study your answers. Expect prompts like these:

  • Any roof leak in the past five years.
  • Basement flooding or leaking, standing water, or drainage trouble.
  • Whether permits and final inspections exist for additions, conversions or remodels.
  • Critical areas, wetlands or floodplains on the lot.

RCW 64.06.020 sets the timing. The signed form reaches the buyer within five business days of a mutually accepted written contract, unless both sides agree to something else. After delivery the buyer gets three business days to back out, unless that right was waived. Sellers must also supply a smoke detector and install carbon monoxide alarms where the state building code requires them.

Permits and short-term rentals

Redmond expects a building permit before you add on, remodel, convert a garage, build a deck or create an accessory dwelling unit. A few jobs need none: a one-story detached accessory structure up to 200 square feet, a retaining wall no higher than 4 feet, and window replacement within existing openings. Newly built homes and detached accessory dwelling units need fire sprinklers.

Built something without a permit? Put it on the disclosure form. An as-is cash sale lets you hand the house over without finishing the paperwork, though the buyer will discount the price for the risk. Development Services can show you what is on file under your address.

Short-term rental rules are recent. Ordinance 3239 (December 2, 2025) created a Redmond business license for short-term rentals, effective January 1, 2026, in addition to the state license. One license is issued per rental address in single-family zones, and one per operator in multifamily or mixed-use buildings. Stays under 30 consecutive nights are covered. An owner-occupied home renting fewer than three rooms for at least six months a year is outside the definition. Running without a license brings a penalty of 100 percent of the fee, so check your standing before you transfer a working rental.

Before the Development Services counter

A short visit to Development Services can save a deal. Bring your street address and any permit numbers or contractor invoices from past additions, a finished basement or a garage conversion. Ask whether each project has a final inspection on file, and whether a detached accessory unit meets the sprinkler requirement.

Write down what you learn and keep it with your sale folder. A buyer's inspector is likely to raise the same questions, and a clear answer from the city is stronger than your memory of what a contractor did years ago.

If you find a gap, you have two choices. You can finish the permit work yourself before listing, or you can sell as-is and disclose the gap so the offer reflects it.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Redmond houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Excise tax and property tax

Washington's real estate excise tax normally lands on the seller. Payment goes to the treasurer of the county where the property sits, and the Department of Revenue counts the notarized deed date as the sale date. The state share is tiered and a local share is added. Starting with sales on January 1, 2027, the tiers are:

  • 1.1% up to $551,000
  • 1.28% from $551,000 to $1,551,000
  • 2.75% from $1,551,000 to $3,051,000
  • 3.0% over $3,051,000

Ask your escrow officer or the King County Recorder's Office for the local share on a Redmond address, and for the tiers that apply if you close before the new year. Late payment starts accruing interest one month after the sale, and the Department of Revenue shows an assessment rate of 6 percent for 2026.

A separate property tax bill also follows the parcel. Its due date is April 30 (RCW 84.56.020), and a total of $50 or more may be paid in two halves, the second by October 31. At closing the agent divides the year's amount between you and the buyer. King County Treasury can supply a current statement before you commit to a date.

Comparing your three options

Every path swaps something for something else.

  • Agent listing: broad Eastside exposure, plus showings, inspections and repair haggling.
  • Do-it-yourself sale: no commission, but you take on marketing, the disclosure form, the contract and the excise tax affidavit.
  • As-is cash sale: fewer moving parts and a date of your choosing, with a price that reflects condition.

Pull together the same folder in every case: the deed, a loan payoff statement if you owe, permit records, HOA documents for an association home, and the newest property tax statement.

A cash deal can move briskly. After you accept, escrow opens and title is searched. Any mortgage is cleared out of your proceeds. Signing happens before a notary, the affidavit and tax reach the county, and funds are released after the deed is recorded. Nobody orders an appraisal or lender review, so repairs you never made fall to the buyer, who has already priced them in.

Frequently asked questions

How long does a cash sale take in Redmond, WA?

Title work and the buyer decide it, so request the closing date in writing. Without an appraisal or loan underwriting, a cash deal usually wraps up sooner than a financed listing, though your own payoff or probate step can slow it.

Who pays the excise tax on a Redmond sale?

The seller, normally. Payment goes to the county treasurer by the sale date. If the seller skips it, liability shifts to the buyer and a lien can attach. Escrow works out the state and local portions.

Must I hand a Redmond buyer the disclosure form?

Yes for most improved residential sales, unless the buyer waives it or RCW 64.06.010 exempts the transfer. Deliver it within five business days of an accepted written contract. The buyer then has three business days to rescind.

Can I sell a Redmond house with unpermitted work?

Yes, and the work should be disclosed. The state form asks about permits and final inspections for additions and remodels, and an as-is buyer will reflect that in the offer. Development Services can show what is on file.

Does a former short-term rental need a license before I sell?

Selling needs no license. The requirement, in force since January 1, 2026, applies to operating a qualifying short-term rental. If yours ran unlicensed, ask the city about a penalty before closing.

Choosing how to sell in Marysville

A Marysville seller picks between an agent's listing, a private sale to someone found on your own, and a cash buyer who takes the place with its flaws. The real difference is how long each takes. The city is now the second largest in Snohomish County, with an estimated 77,686 residents in July 2025, up 9.9 percent from the April 2020 base. Owners live in 69.4 percent of homes. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $567,900, a mortgage holder pays about $2,409 a month, and typical gross rent is $1,997. Those are citywide figures, so use them as background only. Your price depends on your own house, its condition and recent sales on your street.

Whichever way you go, start by collecting:

  • The deed and your latest Snohomish County tax statement.
  • Payoff letters from your lender and any lienholder.
  • Receipts and permit records for big jobs such as a roof, addition or deck.

Commutes and roads

Marysville is mostly a commuter city. Roughly 9 percent of residents work inside the city, about 20 percent in Everett and 13 percent in Seattle, and the mean trip is 31.5 minutes, with 70 percent driving alone. Community Transit runs four local routes plus express service from park and ride lots, including all-day trips to Lynnwood City Center station and peak service to the Boeing Everett Factory. The city sits outside the Sound Transit district.

Buyers pay attention to access to I-5 and State Route 529. Say plainly how long the drive is from your house to the on-ramp and to Everett.

Low ground, creeks and flood questions

Downtown sits about 5 feet above sea level beside Ebey Slough, while eastern parts of town climb past 465 feet. Quilceda and Allen creeks drain the area. If your house is low or close to water, ask the county for the flood zone and get a survey in hand so a buyer's lender does not raise the issue first.

Accessory dwelling units help on bigger lots. A lot may hold two, each at least 200 square feet and up to the greater of 1,000 square feet or 50 percent of the main house, capped at 1,400 square feet. Plan on one parking space per unit and, in most cases, separate water and sewer connections. Short-term rental units are prohibited in the city, so never pitch a house or ADU as a nightly rental.

The city publishes a zoning map. For property lines, a professional survey is the only reliable answer, and recorded surveys can be searched through the Snohomish County Auditor.

Disclosure form and excise tax

Two state rules drive most Marysville closings. Under RCW 64.06.020 the seller disclosure statement must reach the buyer five business days after both sides sign, unless they agree on a different timetable, and the buyer then holds a three business day right to back out. Excise tax is due at the moment of sale and is typically the seller's expense.

State rates climb in four bands, from 1.1 percent to 3 percent, and a local rate rides on top, so ask the Snohomish County Treasurer for the combined figure at your price. The first band ends at $551,000 for sales starting January 1, 2027 and at $525,000 before that. The city's median value of $567,900 puts a typical sale into the 1.28 percent band.

Valuation, tax dates and appeals

The assessor must value real property at 100 percent of true and fair market value, using a sales comparison, replacement cost or income approach. Each January 1 the county sets a fresh value, and the notice arrives in June. The following year's tax is built on it.

Doubt the number? Call the assessor's line printed on the notice and ask for an appraiser. If the answer is unsatisfying, petition the Board of Equalization, using whichever of two cutoffs comes later: 60 days after the mailing or July 1. Questions about that go to 425-388-3407. The tax itself is split into April 30 and October 31 installments, and a postmark on mail is enough. Escrow prorates the current bill at closing.

From accepted offer to closing

Your sequence is short. Sign the accepted offer, then deliver the disclosure inside the five business day window. Let the title company set the closing date and prepare a settlement statement showing payoff and excise tax. Hand over keys when funds are released.

With a cash buyer there is no loan approval to wait for and little inspection haggling. A listing keeps both, so it runs longer but can fetch more for a house in good shape.

What the buyer will see on a Marysville lot

Marysville runs north to south along Interstate 5, with the Tulalip reservation to the west and State Route 9 to the east. Parts of the city sit in the Arlington, Lake Stevens or Lakewood school districts, though the Marysville School District covers most of it, so a buyer with children should confirm the district for your exact address. A buyer will also ask who supplies what at the house and whether there are open permits, so settle both before you list.

Newer subdivisions and older neighborhoods trade at different prices, and a nearby sale of a similar house tells you more than the citywide median does. Ask an agent or a cash buyer which recent sales they used and how they adjusted for condition.

Judging a cash offer

Look at what lands in your account. Take the offer, subtract the payoff and excise tax, and set the result beside a list-price scenario after commission, repair credits and the months of payments you would carry. Get the closing date in writing and run the transfer through a title company.

Frequently asked questions

How long does a Marysville permit take to review?

It varies by type. First quarter 2026 averages were 8 days for decks, 18 for remodels, 26 for new residential and 34 for accessory dwelling units, counted as calendar days of staff review. Revisions can add time.

Can I use a Marysville ADU as a short-term rental?

No. Short-term rental units are currently prohibited in Marysville, so a buyer planning nightly rentals would need another plan.

What is the deadline to appeal my Snohomish County assessed value?

Use whichever date is later: 60 days after the notice was mailed or July 1. The petition goes to the Board of Equalization, and the clerk answers questions at 425-388-3407. An attorney is optional. Evidence that the value is wrong is not.

Who pays the Washington excise tax on a house sale?

Typically the seller. The county treasurer collects it as of the sale date, and a closing agent ordinarily subtracts it from what you receive. If a seller leaves it unpaid, the obligation can shift to the buyer.

Do I have to give a Marysville buyer a disclosure statement?

Usually yes, for improved residential property. RCW 64.06.020 prescribes the form and a five business day delivery window, after which the buyer has three business days to rescind. A written waiver or an exempt transfer changes that.

Neighborhood and association questions

Shoreline is split into 14 neighborhoods, with Richmond Beach in the northwest corner, and The Highlands is a gated community that has its own sewer district. Does your street have special rules or a homeowners' association? Say so up front. The state disclosure form asks about association assessments, common areas and approvals needed for remodeling, and buyers prefer to hear it from you.

If an association applies, request its governing documents, dues schedule and any notice of upcoming assessments as soon as you decide to sell. Associations can take days to answer, and a buyer's review period runs on a clock.

Permits before you sell

Shoreline treats a missing permit as a violation that stays with the property. Starting work without one breaks city code and can mean fines and penalties, with permit fees possibly doubled. The current owner answers for what earlier owners skipped, so check the record before you list.

The city sorts everyday jobs roughly like this:

  • Cabinet replacement, painting and tiling usually need no permit, unless plumbing, electrical or gas work comes with them.
  • Moving a wall, door or window probably needs a building permit. So does swapping a water heater or adding a permanently wired light fixture.
  • Plumbing and mechanical permits can sometimes be issued the same day. Other reviews take longer, depending on project type and how complete the documents are.
  • Applications go through the city's eTRAKiT system, where anyone can check a permit's status without an account. Send questions to pcd@shorelinewa.gov.
  • When work started without a permit, the city can require a separate investigation inspection permit before it will take the building permit application.

Look at trees as well. A tree that poses an imminent hazard can come down under the municipal code, but a healthy tree with only moderate risk may still need a permit, and cutting one without a permit can draw penalties sometimes reaching $15,000 or more.

A quick way to start: walk the house with a list of every project since you bought it, then email the city with addresses and descriptions of anything doubtful. Keep the replies with your sale papers.

Buyers' agents often ask who serves an address, because several providers split the work.

  • Trash, recycling and compost: Recology.
  • Natural gas: Puget Sound Energy.

Wastewater is handled by the city everywhere but The Highlands. Two treatment plants serve Shoreline, one operated by Edmonds and one by King County, and a layer on the city's managed assets viewer shows where a given parcel drains. The disclosure form asks if the property is on public sewer, whether the house is hooked up, and whether extra sewer charges apply, so verify each answer with the city before you sign.

Closing costs and the disclosure form

Excise tax on the sale is the largest closing cost, and the seller is the normal payer. If the seller leaves it unpaid, the buyer becomes liable and the unpaid amount may become a lien. For sales starting January 1, 2027 the breaks sit at $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. The local rate comes on top.

Call the King County treasurer for the Shoreline rate and the property tax balance on your parcel, and ask escrow how the year's tax will be split.

Expect to deliver the disclosure statement within five business days after both sides accept a written contract. From delivery, the buyer has three business days to rescind, unless that right was waived. The form also has you confirm that carbon monoxide alarms and smoke detection are in place.

From accepted offer to closing day

Knowing the order of events helps you plan a move. After you and a buyer sign a written contract, the clock starts on your disclosure statement, due within five business days. The buyer then reads it and, within three business days of delivery, may rescind unless the right was waived.

While that window runs, title work goes on in the background. The title company looks for liens and unpaid taxes, asks for your loan payoff figure, and prepares the deed. If the file shows unpermitted work or an unclear sewer connection, expect questions, and have your answers ready from the permit emails and city records you collected.

On closing day you sign the deed before a notary. The notarized date is the sale date for excise tax, and the tax and affidavit go to the county. Funds reach you once the deed is recorded. If you are moving out, plan your last day in the house around that date, and keep copies of utility final bills for Seattle City Light and your water provider, since the buyer will want service transferred.

Cash sale or listing?

When the house needs more work than you want to take on, a cash buyer who accepts it as-is is the alternative to listing. Weigh any offer against what a repaired and listed sale would leave you after repairs and carrying costs.

Both routes need the same folder: the deed, a loan payoff figure, permit records for work you or earlier owners did, and your latest property tax statement. In a cash sale, escrow opens once you accept and the title company searches the record. The loan is paid from proceeds, you sign the deed in front of a notary, and the county receives the excise tax and affidavit. Funds are released after recording. No appraisal or lender review slows things down.

How many people live in Shoreline, WA?

The July 1, 2025 estimate is 66,542. The 2020 census counted 58,608, a gain of about 13.8 percent.

Do I need a permit to remodel a Shoreline house before I sell it?

It depends on the work. Painting, tiling and replacing cabinets generally need no permit, but moving walls, doors or windows likely does, as does replacing a water heater. Email pcd@shorelinewa.gov with a description if you are unsure.

Am I responsible for unpermitted work a previous owner did?

Yes, the owner answers for earlier unpermitted work. The city may ask for an investigation inspection permit before it accepts the building permit, and fees can be doubled.

Can I remove a tree from my Shoreline lot before listing?

Only if the rules allow it. A tree that is an imminent hazard can be removed, and dead or dying trees outside critical areas have exemptions, but healthy trees may need a permit. Penalties for removing one without a permit can reach $15,000 or more.

Who supplies electricity and water in Shoreline?

Seattle City Light provides electricity citywide. Water comes from Seattle Public Utilities or North City Water District, depending on the address. Puget Sound Energy supplies gas, and Recology picks up trash, recycling and compost.

South of it is the Issaquah School District, with Issaquah and Skyline high schools and Beaver Lake, Pacific Cascade and Pine Lake middle schools. The line runs through the middle of the city, so two neighbors a few blocks apart can sit in different districts. Look up your address instead of guessing from the street name. Buyers with children often start their search with the district and narrow from there, which makes a correct label in the listing worth the minute it takes.

Zoning and accessory dwelling units

Zoning can add value to a lot. The R-4 zone allows up to 4 dwelling units per acre, a maximum floor area ratio of 50 percent for single-family homes and 40 percent hardscape coverage. A detached accessory dwelling unit in R-4 needs setbacks of 15 feet in front and 5 feet on the sides and rear, with a 24-foot height limit.

Accessory units are broadly welcome. The city permits up to two on a lot with a detached single-family home, whether attached, detached or converted from an existing structure. A detached unit is capped at 1,000 square feet, and an attached unit can reach 50 percent of the house or 1,000 square feet, whichever is larger. No extra parking is needed when the property already has four or more spaces. If your lot has potential, mention these rules in the listing, and tell buyers to confirm current standards with the city.

Setbacks and height limits matter most when a buyer is picturing a backyard cottage. Confirm the current numbers with the city rather than quoting them from memory, and keep a copy of the answer.

A plateau lot with room for a second structure may appeal to a buyer with extended family or a rental plan. Ask whether the existing house leaves space for a unit that would meet the setbacks, then describe the possibility without promising approval.

Roof, drainage and the disclosure form

Winters are cool and wet, and snow is rare. Inspectors pay the most attention to the roof, gutters, drainage and crawl spaces, and the state disclosure form asks about roof leaks in the past five years, standing water and drainage problems. Fix what you can before you list, and answer the rest plainly.

The completed statement goes to the buyer within five business days after the contract is accepted. Inside it is a notice that restrictive covenants based on race or other protected classes are void and unenforceable under RCW 49.60.224, and the form asks about homeowners' association dues, special assessments, shared common areas and recorded covenants. If your home is in an HOA, order the documents early.

Excise tax and property tax at closing

Washington's real estate excise tax is usually the seller's bill, payable to the county treasurer by the sale date. Sales beginning January 1, 2027 are taxed at 1.1 percent on the first $551,000, then 1.28 percent up to $1,551,000, with steeper tiers beyond. The local rate is layered over that. Escrow or King County can tell you the local rate, and which tiers govern a closing before January 1.

Property tax follows the parcel, not the owner. When the county meets its deadlines, statements are mailed by March 15, and each one has to explain the senior exemption and deferral programs (RCW 84.56.020). Bills of $50 or more are split into April 30 and October 31 halves. Treasurers may set up payment agreements on current or past-due taxes, so ask King County Treasury about your balance before closing.

Plan on the closing agent dividing the current year between you and the buyer by the closing date. Ask for a statement early so the contract numbers match what the county shows.

Checklist and how a cash closing works

Put these in a folder before any contract is signed:

  • Your deed and a loan payoff statement.
  • HOA bylaws, dues and any pending special assessments.
  • Permit and final inspection records for additions or an accessory unit.
  • The newest King County property tax statement.

Cash closings follow a brief script. Accept the offer and escrow opens. Title is searched, your mortgage is cleared from the proceeds, and you sign the deed in front of a notary. The county receives the affidavit and tax, and funds go out once the deed is recorded. Because no appraisal or lender review is involved, the timetable depends on title work and your own plans.

If the house has an accessory unit, add its permit file and any lease to the folder. If an HOA governs the property, ask for its paperwork on day one, since associations can take time to respond.

Frequently asked questions

How quickly can I sell a house in Sammamish, WA?

Cash buyers can close when title work wraps up, often on your chosen date. Listings run longer through showings, inspections and the buyer's loan. Whoever buys, request the closing date in writing.

Can I sell my Sammamish house as-is?

Yes. Repairs are optional, but the state disclosure form is still required unless the buyer waives it or an exemption applies. Expect an as-is buyer to price in the condition.

Does the school district matter when I sell in Sammamish?

Yes, buyers search by it. Southeast 8th Street divides the Lake Washington School District to the north from the Issaquah School District to the south, and a small eastern area is in Snoqualmie Valley. Check your address.

Can a buyer add an accessory dwelling unit to a Sammamish lot?

In many cases. The city allows up to two ADUs where a lot has a detached single-family home, and a detached unit tops out at 1,000 square feet. Setbacks and height limits vary by zone, so check with the city.

When are property taxes due on a Sammamish home?

Bills of $50 or more are paid half by April 30 and half by October 31. King County Treasury collects, and the closing agent normally divides the year between buyer and seller.

Can I sell my house fast in Richland?

Yes, and you have a few ways to do it. Some owners list with a broker, some sell without one, and others hand the house to a cash buyer who accepts it with all its flaws. Cash usually wins on speed because nobody waits for a lender to say yes. Even so, title work and your own paperwork decide the real closing day.

The house sits in Benton County, in the Tri-Cities of southeastern Washington. Richland has been growing, from 60,580 in the April 2020 estimates base to 65,258 on July 1, 2025, a gain of 7.7 percent. Homes cost far less than in the Seattle area.

  • A listing is best for a house that is ready for showings, when you can afford to wait for the buyer's financing.
  • A cash buyer fits an inherited property, a rental with tenants, a house in need of work, or a move date that will not budge.
  • Selling it yourself works when you are at ease with the contract, the seller disclosure form and the county excise tax affidavit.

Whoever bids, get the price, the closing date and the division of closing costs in writing before comparing.

Richland housing figures

The numbers below cover the entire city. Your own street may look different.

Housing measureRichland
Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020 to 2024$436,700

With an average commute of just over twenty minutes, Richland has an easy drive to sell. Say so when you describe the house.

Pricing here moves with the heat and the yard, so a house with a working irrigation system and a recent air conditioner can stand out from nearby listings.

If your house is an alphabet home

Much of the older housing here goes back to World War II. The U.S. Army acquired land beside the Columbia River in 1943 for the Manhattan Project, and the town swelled from roughly 300 people to 25,000 by war's end. Planners put up prefabricated duplexes and single-family houses in many floor plans labeled with letters, hence the name alphabet houses. The government owned the homes into the 1950s, and the final government-owned home sold on May 16, 1960.

Owners of one of these houses should be ready for buyer questions about the roof, wiring, insulation and any additions. North Richland's Gold Coast Historic District, built during the Cold War expansion, joined the National Register of Historic Places in 2005. If your house is in it, verify what that status means before planning any changes.

Older plumbing and electrical systems are worth checking before a buyer does. A seller who can say what has been replaced, and when, usually spends less time haggling over price.

Photographs of the original floor plan or old building papers can help buyers picture what they are getting, so look through your files for them.

Desert climate and what inspectors check

Richland is semi-arid. Rainfall averages about 7 inches a year, summers are hot, and the 2021 heat wave pushed the city to 118 degrees. A home inspector will probably ask how old the air conditioner is, what the attic insulation looks like, whether the roof is sound and how the irrigation system works. Lawns and plantings rely on irrigation water, which also shows up on tax bills and on the disclosure form discussed below.

Before listing, run the cooling system once and check the sprinkler timers and valves. A house that stays comfortable in July and has a tidy yard in a dry climate tells buyers that it has been looked after.

Property taxes in Benton County

The Benton County Treasurer bills and collects tax on behalf of every district that taxes your parcel: county, city, schools and the rest. The debt attaches to the property, not to a person. Bills are certified around mid to late January. Miss April 30 and the first half is late, and miss October 31 and the second half is. A deadline that lands on a weekend slides to Monday, and the postmark date is what counts.

Residential property with four or fewer units carries 9 percent yearly interest on delinquent tax under RCW 84.56.020, with no extra penalties. The county waits until real property is three full years delinquent before it will foreclose. Only one statement goes out, early in the year, addressed to the owner of record on December 1 of the prior year. At closing you and the buyer settle who covers what, and the title company can verify the balance before you sign.

Irrigation may add a line to the bill. Charges from Benton Irrigation District, Columbia Irrigation District and Kiona Irrigation District come through the Treasurer. Kennewick Irrigation District is different: payment goes straight to that district. Learn which one serves your lot.

Owners who are 61 or older, or retired because of a disability, may qualify for a senior or disabled exemption, and deferral is possible too. The Benton County Assessor, reachable at (509) 735-2394, handles both programs. To dispute a valuation, take it to the Benton County Board of Equalization.

Paperwork at closing

No Benton County title transfer goes through without a Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit attached to the deed. The Treasurer sends back any affidavit with sections 1 through 7 blank, and a mobile home needs its own affidavit. You can pick up forms online or at either Treasurer office: 620 Market Street in Prosser, or 7122 W Okanogan Place in Kennewick. Sellers normally pay the tax. It falls due on the sale date, which the Department of Revenue defines as the day the deed is notarized.

From January 1, 2027, the state charges 1.1 percent on sales up to $551,000, plus a local rate. For that local rate, and for the brackets that govern a closing before the new year, talk to your escrow officer or the Benton County Treasurer.

RCW 64.06.020 also puts a disclosure statement in the buyer's hands within five business days of an accepted contract. After delivery the buyer may rescind for three business days. Look for sections on household water, irrigation water rights, sewer or on-site systems and wood-burning appliances, all of which come up with Richland's blend of city and rural-edge lots. As for permits, the City of Richland handles them through an online system that went live on June 3, 2024, and the Building Division works from 625 Swift Boulevard.

Before you say yes to an offer

Gather these first:

  • Your deed, a loan payoff number and a current Benton County Treasurer tax statement.
  • Any irrigation district bill or water rights document attached to the lot.
  • Permit records for additions, decks or a finished basement.
  • A filled-in excise tax affidavit, sections 1 through 7.

A cash deal has few steps. You accept, escrow opens, and a title search follows. Proceeds clear any mortgage, the deed is signed before a notary, and the affidavit and tax travel to the county. Release of funds comes after recording. With no appraisal or lender review in the way, you can choose the date.

Owe back taxes or an irrigation bill? Tell the title company at once. Open balances come out of your proceeds at closing, and surprises in the final week are harder to fix.

Frequently asked questions

How long does a Richland, WA sale take?

Cash deals can finish when title work does, often on a day you name. Listings take longer because of showings, inspections and the buyer's loan. With any buyer, ask for the closing day in writing.

When are Benton County property taxes due?

Half is due April 30 and half October 31. Interest begins if the first half is paid late, and a postmark on or before the due date counts as on time.

Do I owe the real estate excise tax when I sell in Richland?

Most likely. The seller ordinarily pays, and the money goes to the county treasurer by the sale date, with a completed affidavit submitted alongside the deed.

Can I sell a Richland house that needs repairs?

Yes, as-is. Just answer the state disclosure form candidly on roof leaks, structural defects, water and sewer systems and permits. An as-is buyer will lower the offer to match the condition.

Where do I ask about a senior property tax exemption in Richland?

Call the Benton County Assessor, who runs the senior and disabled exemptions and the deferral programs. The Treasurer cannot lower your bill until the Assessor signs off, so pay by the due dates meanwhile.

In Lakewood you may hire an agent, sell it yourself or take a cash offer for the house as it stands. What the house is and how it is used should pick the route. An empty, tidy house can go on the market. One with tenants, postponed repairs or an estate behind it usually moves quicker through a direct sale.

Owners live in fewer than half of Lakewood homes, 47.5 percent to be exact. Rent runs a midpoint of $1,525 a month, and owner-occupied homes have a median value of $461,200. A city registration and inspection program for rentals, described below, affects how a rented house sells.

Lakewood was incorporated on February 28, 1996 and became the second largest city in Pierce County at once. Joint Base Lewis-McChord, a military installation with about 55,000 employees, sits beside the city, and the local economy is closely tied to it. How the Rental Housing Safety Program affects a sale

The city's Rental Housing Safety Program requires owners of rental property to register every year, and registered properties are inspected once every five years. An initial inspection may be done by a city inspector or by a qualified private inspector, and every re-inspection is done by the city. Inspectors look at structural integrity, weather exposure, plumbing and sanitation, heat and water, ventilation, electrical wiring, exits, and smoke and carbon monoxide detectors.

An owner who fails to register can face penalties under the city's fee schedule and the Lakewood Municipal Code, and a rental business license can be revoked. A buyer of a rented house will ask for registration and inspection records, so gather them before you list. Exemptions under LMC 5.60.025 include:

  • Units occupied by the owner, or by the owner's parent or child.
  • Mobile and manufactured homes, shelters and transitional housing.
  • Condominiums and townhouses in multi-unit structures under multiple ownership, unless one owner holds them.
  • Units built in the past 10 years with a certificate of occupancy and no code violations.

Renting rooms in a home you live in does not require registration, but moving out and renting the whole house does. Contact the program at 253-512-2261 or rentals@cityoflakewood.us.

Short-term rental rules

Rentals of under 30 days are allowed in most zones. The city excludes Commercial 1 to 3, the Industrial Business Park, Industrial 1 and 2, Public and Semi-Public Institutional and Open Space Recreation 1 and 2. A short-term rental must register with the Rental Housing Safety Program, hold a business license, renew annually and be inspected every five years, with a free first inspection. The city handles the permit as a Type II administrative decision. Check your zoning before you promise a buyer short-term rental income.

Utilities and local services

Several providers share the city's services, so it helps to list them when you transfer utility accounts to a buyer:

  • Electricity comes from Lakeview Light and Power on the east side, Tacoma Power on the north side and Puget Sound Energy on the west side, which is also the only natural gas provider.
