  • Pierce County Public Works and Utilities maintains sanitary sewer, and the city manages stormwater.
  • West Pierce Fire and Rescue covers the city.

List the providers for your address in the sale file so the buyer knows whom to call on day one.

When Pierce County property taxes are due

Statements arrive in February. A bill over $50 can be paid in two installments, April 30 and October 31, while $50 or less must be paid in full on April 30. If a payment envelope is postmarked before the statutory deadline, interest and penalty are waived. Check your statement for the exact amounts due.

Pay online or at the Assessor-Treasurer's Office, 2401 S. 35th St., Room 142, Tacoma, which also has a drop box. Foreclosure avoidance payments go by cashier's check to that office. For status, call the Assessor-Treasurer hotline at (253) 798-6111. Mortgage companies follow the same payment rules as the owner.

What a Lakewood seller owes and discloses at closing

The seller normally covers the state real estate excise tax, payable on the sale date, with a city local tax on top. Under RCW 82.45.060 the state rate climbs in steps from 1.1 percent on the first slice, and the thresholds change January 1, 2027. Your escrow officer can give you the exact figure for your price, state and local together.

The disclosure form under RCW 64.06.020 asks about the sewer connection, roof leaks and environmental items. A buyer who receives it may rescind within three business days, unless the contract says differently.

From offer to closing

Once you accept an offer, escrow orders a title search and requests your lender's payoff. The excise tax, the prorated property tax and other costs are added up on the settlement statement. For a rented house, the registration certificate and inspection results should be in the file by then. If the inspection is not current, ask the program whether a private inspector or a city inspector should do it, because the choice can affect timing.

A cash buyer often skips the appraisal and loan committee, so these steps can finish sooner. Whatever route you pick, compare offers by what you take home after the payoff, taxes and any repairs, and confirm your last property tax payment has posted before closing day.

Getting ready to sell a rented Lakewood house

With a tenant in place, begin with documents. Find your current registration certificate and inspection results, and call 253-512-2261 to ask if an exemption covers your unit. Add the lease and rent records so a buyer can see exactly what comes with the property.

An investor keeping the tenant cares about those records and the next inspection date. A buyer moving in cares about condition and about when the unit can be emptied. A tidy file speeds talks in both cases. Before agreeing to a closing date, ask a Washington attorney how your lease and notice duties apply.

Do I have to register my Lakewood rental before selling?

Each year the house is rented, unless an exemption applies. Buyers ask for the certificate and inspection history, so register and inspect first if you have not.

Can I sell a Lakewood house with tenants?

Yes. Expect a buyer who keeps the tenant to review the city's registration and inspection records. A Washington attorney can explain your lease and notice duties.

When are Pierce County property taxes due?

Two installments, April 30 and October 31, except that $50 or less is due in full April 30. April 30, 2027 is the next first-half date.

Are short-term rentals allowed in Lakewood?

Yes, in most zones, with a business license, registration in the Rental Housing Safety Program and a permit. Commercial 1 to 3 and several industrial and open space zones are excluded.

Who pays excise tax when a Lakewood house sells?

Usually the seller, payable to the county treasurer on the sale date. Unpaid tax accrues interest starting that day.

Complexes of five or more rental dwelling units must also register with the city every year. For one rented house, ask the city if any other requirement applies.

A change in how a building is used requires a city permit under the construction permit rules, filed through the city's online portal. Open permits or unpermitted work can delay closing if a buyer wants to convert part of the house, so ask the city to tell you what permits it holds for your address before signing.

What to gather before you list

Most buyer questions trace back to three documents: your newest tax statement, a lender payoff letter and permit records for any work on the house. Your county treasurer's record shows whether either tax half is still open. The city can say which permits sit on file for your address, which matters most after a garage, addition or finished space went in.

Septic owners should add tank and drainfield records, and landlords should file the rental license and lease alongside. With everything on hand from the start, a cash buyer can price the house fast and an ordinary buyer has less to argue about after the inspection.

If taxes or loans are still open

A tax debt will not stop a Lacey sale. Title work totals what is owed, and escrow pays it from your sale proceeds along with interest and penalties that have piled up. Do not expect the county to bend, because it offers no hardship extensions. For a balance spanning several years, ask the Treasurer about a payment plan before you accept any offer, so the subtraction at closing is not a shock.

A mortgage works the same way. Request the payoff letter early and compare it with your own loan records. Tight cash timelines are doable, provided payoff and tax figures are in hand before anyone fixes a closing date.

From accepted offer to closing

Once you accept, the title company hunts for liens and overdue taxes. Your lender provides the payoff, and escrow rolls the excise tax, prorated property tax and other costs into what you take home.

A financed buyer's appraisal and loan steps control the calendar. For cash, title work and your chosen date do. Both paths end with the deed and the excise tax affidavit at the county treasurer. Nothing is final until the tax is paid and the deed is recorded.

How quickly can I sell a house in Lacey?

A cash sale can wrap up as soon as title work is done and a date is picked. Financing brings appraisal and lender steps, and a listing brings showing time.

When are Thurston County property taxes due?

Two payments, April 30 and October 31. A weekend deadline slides to Monday, and the next first-half date is April 30, 2027.

Can I sell my Lacey house if I am behind on property taxes?

Yes. The balance, plus any interest or penalties, gets paid from proceeds or before closing. There are no hardship extensions, though prior-year delinquencies can go on a payment plan.

Does Lacey require a rental inspection before I sell a rented house?

Registration covers complexes of five or more rental units, and any rental activity needs a business license. Ask the city about other rules for a single rented house.

Who must sign the seller disclosure in Lacey?

The seller fills it out, then dates and signs every page. Three business days after delivery, the buyer's rescission window closes, unless the parties agreed to different terms in writing.

Selling a house in Olympia

Washington's capital is also the Thurston County seat. It sits at the south end of Puget Sound on Budd Inlet, about 47 miles southwest of Seattle, with Lacey and Tumwater on its borders. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 56,724 residents, 2.4% above the April 2020 base.

Much of downtown is built on reclaimed land. A house near the water or on fill can draw questions about soil and drainage, so collect any past inspection reports before you list. Most sellers deal with the city only when they have open permits, a rental, or a lot that could hold more housing, and the sections below cover those, followed by the state and county steps every sale goes through.

Under half of homes are owner-occupied, so many buyers and neighbors are renters or landlords. Treat the $486,200 median as a rough guide across all owner-occupied homes, not a price for yours.

Rain, moisture and what buyers inspect

The climate is wet, cloudy and mild, and November through January bring the most rain. City streets, creeks and rivers can flood between November and February. Summers are less extreme but can reach the 90s. Buyers walking an Olympia house tend to check the same few things:

  • Roof, gutters and downspouts, since the wet season runs for months.
  • Crawlspace and basement moisture, especially in older homes near the inlet or on fill.
  • Moss, rot and drainage around the foundation.
  • Cooling or ventilation for the warmer summer days.

Fix or document these before a showing and the inspection phase gets shorter. A buyer taking the house as-is still reads your seller disclosure, so answer it accurately.

City rules for ADUs, middle housing and rentals

Olympia allows up to two accessory dwelling units on almost all lots, each up to 1,000 square feet and 24 feet tall, attached or detached. Middle housing is allowed in every residential zone: up to four units on a lot when zoning standards are met, and up to six within a half mile of frequent transit routes or when at least two units stay affordable for 50 years. That flexibility can raise what a lot is worth to a builder, so mention it if your lot is large. The city offers six pre-approved ADU plans on its middle housing page.

Rental owners have extra steps. The city may require rental registration and, for short-term vacation rentals, an additional permit, both filed through the online permit portal, as the Department of Revenue's Olympia endorsement page explains. A general city business license costs $30 when reported gross income is above $4,000.

  • Permit Center: City Hall, second floor, 601 4th Avenue E, phone 360.753.8314.
  • Counter hours: Monday to Thursday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., closed Fridays.
  • Inspections and permit status run through the online permit portal.

Did an old project skip its final inspection? Phone the Permit Center ahead of listing and find out what the record shows.

Real estate excise tax

Washington puts the excise tax on the seller under RCW 82.45.080, with any local portion added. The state schedule begins at 1.1% and reaches 3% on the top slice. Its first band ends at $525,000 now and at $551,000 for sales beginning January 1, 2027, and the other breakpoints rise too, to $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. A sale at the median value stays inside the first band for the state share. Phone the Thurston County Treasurer for the local rate at your address.

Notarizing the deed sets the sale date, recorded that day or not, and interest starts if payment is a month late. Take the affidavit, deed and money to the treasurer in the county where the property is located. The Department of Revenue REET page has the forms.

Thurston County property taxes at closing

The bill is split into two halves, one due April 30 and the other October 31, and a weekend deadline slides to the following Monday. Tax attaches to the parcel rather than the person, and no fresh statement is mailed when ownership changes. Deciding who pays what at closing falls to you, so find out whether the year is fully paid. Have your closing agent prorate the year and pay any unpaid half out of proceeds.

Sellers who are 61 or older, or retired from a disability, may qualify for a tax reduction or a deferral. Those programs run through the Thurston County Assessor at 360-867-2200. A deferral is repaid from the estate, so confirm the payoff with the county before closing.

  • Treasurer's office: 3000 Pacific Avenue SE, Suite 130, Olympia, phone 360-786-5550.
  • Special charges such as stormwater can appear on the same bill and are liens too.
  • A parcel is not sold for unpaid tax until three full years of delinquency have run.

What you hand the buyer

An improved residential property sale comes with a completed disclosure statement, though a buyer can waive it and some transfers are exempt. The clock in RCW 64.06.020 is five business days from mutual acceptance unless you agree to another schedule, and rescission rights run three business days from delivery. If no statement is provided, the buyer may waive the right to rescind before or after the contract.

Complete every line, write NA where a question does not apply, and explain each yes on an attached sheet. The form covers what you actually know, so past roof leaks, drainage problems and permit history in an older house belong on it.

Ways to sell in Olympia

Three routes cover most sales, and the same deed, excise tax and tax proration steps apply to each.

  • List with an agent and accept the time showings, repairs and buyer financing take.
  • Go solo, which makes the disclosure form, the contract and the closing paperwork your job.
  • Accept an as-is cash offer. That trims repairs and financing waits, and the price usually lands under a fully prepared listing.

Written offers make the comparison easy, and each buyer should say what you will owe at closing. Watch deed and affidavit timing so the sale date and tax payment match.

Frequently asked questions

What will excise tax cost on an Olympia sale?

The answer turns on your price and the local rate. State tax starts at 1.1% on the first $525,000 and climbs in bands, with new thresholds from January 1, 2027. The Thurston County Treasurer knows the local rate for your address.

What are the Thurston County tax deadlines?

April 30 and October 31, one half each. Any deadline on a weekend shifts to Monday. Your closing agent can prorate the current year.

Can I build an extra unit on my Olympia lot before selling?

Often yes. Olympia allows up to two ADUs on almost all lots, each up to 1,000 square feet and 24 feet tall, and middle housing of up to four units in residential zones when standards are met. Call the Permit Center at 360.753.8314 to check your lot before you start.

In Washington, does the buyer or seller owe excise tax?

The seller, under RCW 82.45.080. If a seller fails to pay, the buyer can end up responsible, and unpaid tax can attach to the property as a lien.

Where does the Olympia excise tax affidavit get filed?

File it with the Thurston County Treasurer along with the deed and your payment. Your closing or escrow officer usually takes care of this at signing.

The tax is yours under RCW 82.45.080 and falls due at the time of sale. Under RCW 82.45.100, interest begins after one month and penalties climb to 20 percent at three months. For a King County parcel, call the county's Treasury Operations to confirm the amount before you sell.

Late tax on residential property with four or fewer units carries nine percent annual interest under RCW 84.56.020. Make sure nothing is delinquent before you list.

Choosing how to sell

With a median value above $900,000, carrying costs add up while a house sits, so weigh the routes first.

Parts of Burien that shape appeal

Burien borders Seattle and the unincorporated communities of White Center and Boulevard Park on the north, Tukwila and SeaTac on the east, and Normandy Park on the south. Where your house sits within that frame changes how buyers describe it.

  • Ambaum Boulevard follows the old Lake Burien Railway route.

Roads and transit

Burien sits at the junction of State Routes 509 and 518, northwest of the airport, and Ambaum Boulevard and Des Moines Memorial Drive carry traffic north. Rental rules when a tenant lives there

Burien requires an annual rental housing business license, handled by the state Business Licensing Service, but single-family residences, condos, townhomes, manufactured homes and accessory dwelling units are exempt. For other rentals, the 2026 fee per complex is $323.80 for 1 to 10 units, $809.50 for 11 to 50 units and $971.41 for 51 or more.

  • Under the Rental Housing Policy in BMC 5.63, a landlord needs one of a list of just causes to evict, and wanting to sell the unit counts only after the tenant gets at least 90 days' written notice.

  • The inspection program, in place since 2021, requires at least 20 percent of covered units to be inspected every three years.

Does a Burien single-family rental need the city rental housing license?

Can I end a tenancy in Burien because I am selling the house?

Yes, but only with at least 90 days' written notice, because selling the unit is one of the just causes in BMC 5.63.070. Without a valid cause, the city rules do not allow the eviction.

Selling in Bremerton

Selling a house in Bremerton starts with the Navy. The city of 45,482 residents (July 1, 2025) is the largest on the Kitsap Peninsula and is home to Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and the Bremerton Annex of Naval Base Kitsap. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $439,400. Fewer than half of households own, which means plenty of houses are rentals. Owners here choose between an agent, a sale by owner, and a cash buyer.

Housing measureBremerton figure
Owner-occupied housing rate, 2020 to 202448.1%
Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020 to 2024$439,400
Median gross rent, 2020 to 2024$1,641
Median household income, 2020 to 2024$74,940
Population, 2020 Census43,505

Ferries, bridges and neighborhoods

Commute routes decide which blocks sell fastest. The Port Washington Narrows cuts the city in two, and two bridges join the halves: the Warren Avenue Bridge on State Route 303, opened in 1958, and the Manette Bridge, rebuilt in 2011. State Route 3 runs as a freeway through the west side, and a tunnel carries ferry traffic from the terminal to State Route 304.

Washington State Ferries takes about an hour from Bremerton to Seattle, and Kitsap Transit's passenger-only fast ferry covers the crossing in 28 minutes. Shipyard workers and Seattle commuters will ask how far the house is from the terminal or the gates.

  • Downtown and the waterfront have new apartments, restored older buildings and the Admiral Theatre.
  • Manette sits on its own peninsula and reaches downtown over the Manette Bridge.
  • Charleston centers on Callow Avenue.
  • Union Hill is mostly residential, between downtown and Charleston.
  • Evergreen has water views and a park with a beach and boat ramp.
  • Haddon surrounds Bremerton High School and the Olympic College campus.

Three school districts reach into the city: Bremerton, Central Kitsap and South Kitsap. Check which one applies to your address before naming a school in the listing.

Rain and older houses

Rainfall averages 56.93 inches a year, while snow averages about 3 inches. With that much water, roofs, gutters, siding, crawl spaces and drainage deserve attention before a showing or an inspection, especially on an older house.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Bremerton house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Landlord business license

Anyone who rents or leases real property inside Bremerton limits needs a City of Bremerton Landlord Business License under BMC 3.48.025. It is a city license, separate from any Washington state business license, and it costs $75 a year. Each license covers a calendar year and must be renewed by January 31.

  • Renting rooms inside your own home counts as rental activity.
  • A relative living in your house counts as a rental even if no rent is paid, unless you live there more than half the year.
  • Landlords join the Landlord Notification Program (BMC 5.06) by giving the Police Department a list of rentals and a contact method.
  • Landlords certify that units meet RCW 59.18.060, and the city does not run physical inspections.
  • Stays under 30 days, such as vacation rentals, fall under state business licensing instead.

An unlicensed property can limit the owner's ability to pursue an eviction. If you inherited a Bremerton rental, bring the license in line before you list it, and call the Tax and License Division at 360-473-5311 with questions.

Excise tax at closing

Excise tax on the sale is the seller's cost, collected by the Kitsap County Treasurer. Kitsap lists the local portion at 0.50 percent, and the state portion is graduated. Because a home at Bremerton's median value sits under the $525,000 first band, the state portion there is the lowest rate, 1.1 percent. A $5 state technology fee is added. Ask the treasurer to confirm the total for your parcel.

  • Payment is due within 30 days of the date on the conveying document, and the deed cannot be recorded until it is paid.
  • Seller and buyer, or an agent for each, sign the Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit.
  • The treasurer takes cash or check payable to the Kitsap County Treasurer, and cards carry fees.
  • Late payment adds interest and penalties under RCW 82.45.100, which reach 20 percent of the tax after three months.

From January 1, 2027 the state's three break points rise to $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000.

Kitsap County property tax

Kitsap splits the bill into halves due April 30 and October 31, honoring the postmark. Anything at $50 or less is a single April payment. For residential property with four or fewer units, delinquent tax carries interest of 0.75 percent a month, which works out to the nine percent a year in RCW 84.56.020. Not receiving a statement does not erase interest.

If you refinanced recently, check the account. Kitsap warns that tax money collected at a refinance is sometimes not forwarded to the treasurer until April or October, so confirm it shows as paid before you list. The Assessor's Office at (360) 337-5777 handles the senior and disabled exemption and deferral, the limited-income deferral, the residential improvement exemption and the destroyed property exemption. State law also bars interest and penalties on the home of an active duty service member stationed outside the United States during a period of armed conflict.

Choosing how to sell

Orders to a new duty station, an inherited rental or a house that needs work all push owners toward a faster sale. The routes are familiar.

  • List with an agent and time showings around the crowds that fill downtown for events such as the Armed Forces Day parade in May and the Blackberry Festival over Labor Day.
  • Sell the house yourself, handling the disclosure statement and the excise tax affidavit on your own.
  • Ask a cash buyer for an offer on the house as it stands, so you skip repairs and open houses.

On every route the buyer is owed a seller disclosure statement, five business days after signing, unless waived or exempt. Under RCW 64.06.020 the buyer can rescind for three business days after getting it.

Confirming city limits and closing steps

Enter the address in the Kitsap County Parcel Search, the tool the city points owners to. City limits decide whether the landlord license and other city rules apply. After that, the path runs as follows: accept an offer, open escrow, let title work surface any unpaid tax, sign the affidavit and deed, and pay excise tax to the treasurer before recording. A cash buyer needs no lender appraisal, so a transfer for a house that needs work can close on a short calendar once the paperwork is ready.

Frequently asked questions

How much does a Bremerton seller pay in excise tax?

That depends on price. The state share begins at 1.1 percent of the first $525,000, Kitsap adds a local 0.50 percent, and there is a $5 state technology fee.

Does Bremerton require a license to rent out a house?

Yes. Anyone renting real property inside city limits needs a Bremerton Landlord Business License, which costs $75 a year and renews by January 31. The city does not inspect the unit and relies on the landlord's certification.

When are Kitsap County property taxes due?

Half is due April 30 and half October 31, judged by postmark. A bill of $50 or less is paid in full in April.

Can I sell a Bremerton house I inherited with tenants inside?

Yes, but confirm the Landlord Business License is current first, because an unlicensed property can limit the owner's eviction options. Review the lease and ask the Tax and License Division at 360-473-5311 about the license record.

How can I confirm a house is inside Bremerton city limits?

Enter the address in the Kitsap County Parcel Search, the tool the city points owners to. City limits decide whether the landlord license and other city rules apply.

Edmonds housing snapshot

Edmonds is a Puget Sound waterfront city in southwest Snohomish County, about 15 miles north of Seattle. Its 42,748 residents (July 1, 2025) are older than most Puget Sound suburbs, and the count is close to the 42,853 of 2020. Almost one resident in four is 65 or older. Owners occupy 70.9 percent of homes, and 88.2 percent of people were in the same house a year earlier, so turnover is low.

Who sells, and why, follows from that profile. Common triggers include downsizing, an inherited house, a move toward family and a rental the owner wants out of. Each brings its own paperwork.

A sale at the median value would cross into the second tier of the state excise tax, covered below.

Neighborhoods and getting around

Hillside neighborhoods ring a downtown valley here, so where a house sits inside the city matters to buyers. Expect distinct pockets:

  • Downtown and the Bowl: a valley with views of Puget Sound and the Olympic Mountains, close to the beach, the fishing pier and the ferry dock.
  • Five Corners, Firdale, Perrinville, Seaview, Sherwood and Westgate: hillside neighborhoods, several with their own small commercial centers.
  • The State Route 99 corridor: the eastern commercial edge, home to the city's car dealerships.
  • Esperance: an unincorporated enclave in the southeast corner that has resisted annexation, so confirm whether an address is inside city limits.

Transportation is a selling point. The Washington State Ferries route runs to Kingston, the downtown station is served by Amtrak and Sounder, and Community Transit buses reach outlying areas. Only about 11.7 percent of residents work inside the city and about 11 percent commute to Seattle, so buyers ask about transit and drive times first.

When you write the listing, name the pocket and its walk to the beach, pier or ferry dock, and say plainly if the house is a short drive from the Bowl instead of in it. A buyer shopping Five Corners or Westgate wants different details than one eyeing a view lot near the water, and a clear description saves showings that go nowhere.

Landlord license and backyard units

The City of Edmonds requires a business license for any business operating in the city, including property owners, and it places home rentals in the General Business License category. The fee is $186.87 to apply and $74.75 to renew each year. You apply through the state Business Licensing Service on the Department of Revenue website, and the city then asks for a floor plan and a supplemental questionnaire. Business Licensing can be reached at 425-775-2525.

If tenants live in the house you are selling, check that the license is current and share the lease terms with the buyer. For building questions, the Planning and Development Department is at 121 5th Ave N, phone 425-771-0220. The city runs a Pre-Approved DADU Plan Program for detached accessory dwelling units, but no plans are in the catalog yet, so any existing backyard unit should come with permit records. Counter hours since September 2, 2025 are Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 3 p.m., closed Wednesdays, with phone and digital help weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Call to confirm hours before you go.

  • Gather permit and inspection records for additions, decks and converted space.
  • Keep the rental license, lease copies and security deposit ledger together for the buyer.
  • Ask the department how to confirm an unpermitted structure before it surprises a buyer's inspector.

Ways to sell quickly

Three routes cover most Edmonds situations, and the choice turns on condition, timeline and how much preparation you want to do.

  • A traditional listing: strong demand for views and walkable streets, but staging, showings and financing contingencies take time.
  • A direct sale to an investor or cash buyer: fits an older house, an estate or a rental with tenants, with few repair requests and a closing date you can move.
  • A for-sale-by-owner sale: you keep the agent fee but carry the disclosure, negotiation and paperwork.

Selling an estate? Have the probate attorney confirm that the personal representative can sign before you take an offer. Whatever the route, judge offers by what lands in your hands after excise tax, liens and any mortgage payoff.

Disclosure and excise tax

A completed disclosure statement is part of any Edmonds house sale. RCW 64.06.020 excuses it only when the buyer waived it or the transfer is exempt. Plan to hand it over in five business days from mutual acceptance, unless both sides agree to a different schedule; the buyer then gets three business days to rescind. The form asks about title, water, sewer, structural issues and more, and it says to write NA rather than leave blanks.

The tax falls due on the sale date, which the Department of Revenue defines as the day the deed is signed before the notary, no matter when it is recorded. Miss the one-month mark and interest runs back to the sale date, at 6 percent for 2026. Hold on to your sale records for four years or more. The state can audit a sale and ask you to back up the price or an exemption.

The state tiers start at 1.1 percent and rise to 1.28 percent above $525,000, plus a local rate. Sales beginning January 1, 2027 shift the first tier to $551,000.

Snohomish County property tax

Property tax in Snohomish County is paid in two installments, April 30 and October 31. Under RCW 84.56.020 a statement should arrive by March 15. If you are selling, confirm the second half was paid. The next installment is due April 30.

The county treasurer tells owners with a mortgage escrow to read their escrow statements, because money collected at a refinance may sit until April or October before it reaches the treasurer. Mailed payments only need a postmark by the due date. A late residential parcel of four or fewer units owes 9 percent interest a year and no extra penalty. At the treasurer's office the excise tax counter keeps weekday hours of 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.

From offer to closing in Edmonds

Once you accept an offer, escrow opens and title work shows any unpaid tax or lien. You complete the disclosure statement, sign the deed and settle the excise tax with the county treasurer. For an inherited house, line up the probate paperwork first. For a rental, hand the buyer the lease copies and the license record. With a cash buyer there is no bank appraisal, so your documents and title work set the pace. That helps a downsizing owner who needs a firm date.

Frequently asked questions

Is a business license required to rent out an Edmonds house?

Yes. Edmonds treats home rentals as a General Business License, with a $186.87 application fee and a $74.75 annual renewal, filed through the state Department of Revenue system. Call Edmonds Business Licensing at 425-775-2525.

When must an Edmonds seller deliver the disclosure statement?

Five business days from the day both sides accept, unless they agree to another schedule. After delivery the buyer can rescind for three business days, or waive the form.

When is the excise tax due on an Edmonds sale?

It is owed when the deed is signed, and goes to the county treasurer. If a month passes unpaid, interest is charged back to the sale date.

Is Esperance part of Edmonds?

No. Esperance is an unincorporated area in the southeast corner, surrounded by Edmonds, that has resisted annexation. Ask the county which jurisdiction handles permits and taxes for the address.

Do I need records for a backyard unit before selling?

Yes. The city has no plans in its DADU catalog yet, so any existing backyard unit should come with permit and inspection records. Planning and Development at 425-771-0220 can help.

Selling in Puyallup

Puyallup is a Pierce County city on the Puyallup River, roughly 10 miles from Tacoma and 35 miles from Seattle. Population stands at 42,682 as of July 1, 2025, a 0.7% dip from the April 2020 estimates base. Home values run above $550,000, and many buyers drive to Tacoma, Seattle or other job centers, so commute time shapes offers.

Many sellers get caught by one detail. A Puyallup mailing address can sit in unincorporated territory such as South Hill. Confirm that your parcel is within city limits, because that decides your permit office, zoning code and utility rules. The county bills property tax in both cases.

If you are weighing a quick sale, start by sorting out three facts: where the parcel sits, whether any permit is still open, and whether a tax deferral is attached.

Puyallup housing figures

Think of this as a loose yardstick for price talks: citywide averages, not a read on your street.

What is measuredPuyallup, 2020 to 2024
Share of homes lived in by their owners52.1%
Typical value of an owned home$551,800
Typical monthly rent$1,812
Number of households16,570
Household size2.53 people
Commute each way31.4 minutes
Typical household income$97,826

That typical value blends every owned home in town, from tired to freshly remodeled. A refreshed house can sell well above it. One with deferred repairs may land under it.

Buyers who commute north on the freeway tend to compare Puyallup with Tacoma suburbs, so be ready to explain what your street offers in space and quiet.

Can I build a cottage or add a unit in the lahar zone?

Downtown Puyallup and nearby neighborhoods lie within a hazard zone for lahars, which are mudflows that a moderate or large Mount Rainier eruption could send down the Puyallup Valley. The city writes its building rules around that danger. Under Puyallup Municipal Code 20.20.010(11)(L), accessory dwelling units are banned across the lahar exclusion area. The one exception covers land within a half mile of the base of the surrounding elevation of the valley floor.

A September 2025 city tip sheet spells out what is still allowed there:

  • An addition or remodel is fine if it connects to the main house through an interior doorway and is not sealed off by a full fire wall.
  • That added space can be rented to relatives, or to a single person who is not family.
  • A detached guest house is allowed when it has no separate cooking facilities and nobody lives in it full time, with narrow exceptions for family and employees.

Own a converted garage, a basement apartment or a backyard cottage? Ask the Planning Division how the city treats it before you list. An unpermitted second unit can complicate a sale. Call 253-864-4165, option 3, or email Planning@PuyallupWA.gov.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Puyallup house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Permits and open work

Permit questions go to the Permit Center on the second floor of City Hall, 333 South Meridian. The counter is staffed from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., and the main number is 253-864-4165. Before you take an offer, call about any building permit still open on the house. Unfinished permits tend to turn up in a buyer's inspection or at title review, and closing one out is simpler while the deadline is yours.

Have the street address ready, plus the permit number and contractor paperwork if you kept them. Staff can pull the file and tell you which inspection is missing.

If a buyer asks about work done before you owned the place, the Permit Center file is your best answer, and a short call to 253-864-4165 usually settles it.

Excise tax on the sale

Washington charges the seller a graduated state excise tax on the price (RCW 82.45.080). The county adds a local share, and the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer can quote the combined figure for your address. The schedule in force through December 31, 2026 starts at 1.1% on the portion up to $525,000. It rises to 1.28% up to $1,525,000, 2.75% up to $3,025,000, and 3% beyond that.

Sales beginning January 1, 2027 use higher breakpoints: $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. Puyallup's median home value of $551,800 lands almost exactly on the first of those, which makes a closing date near year end something to raise with your escrow officer.

Tax timing follows the day the deed is notarized, not the day it is recorded. The deed, the affidavit and the payment all go to the county treasurer. If you overpay, you have four years from the sale to ask for a refund, and the request is made by whoever paid.

Due dates, interest and appeals

Your annual Pierce County bill arrives in two parts. Part one is due April 30, part two October 31, and a weekend date rolls to the next Monday. A small bill of $50 or less is settled in a single payment by April 30.

Miss the April deadline on a residential parcel of one to four units, and interest runs at 0.75% a month on the whole year's tax from May 1 (tax years 2023 and later). Paying the first half with interest by October 31 is still allowed. If a late balance exists at closing, the closing officer can pay it out of your proceeds.

The county revalues every property at 100% of market value each year and sends someone to look at each parcel roughly every six years. If you think the value is wrong, file with the Board of Equalization by July 1 of the assessment year, or within 60 days after a value change notice if that is later. The board hears arguments about market value only. The size of the tax bill is not up for debate.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Puyallup houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

If you have a tax deferral

Older owners and owners with disabilities can defer property tax under RCW 84.38. The state covers the bill, and what it paid becomes a lien that comes due, with interest, once the property changes hands. A sale triggers that repayment, so get the payoff number early and hand it to the title company before the closing numbers are drawn up.

Visit the Assessor-Treasurer at 2401 South 35th Street, Room 142, in Tacoma, or call 253-798-6111.

Ways to sell and how closing works

Puyallup owners usually pick among an agent listing, a do-it-yourself sale and a cash buyer who takes the house as it stands. The paperwork at the end is identical: a deed, an excise tax affidavit and a property tax split.

  • Agent listing: the most exposure, with showings and a buyer's loan approval to wait through.
  • Cash buyer, as-is: a fit for postponed repairs, a second unit nobody permitted, or a conversion inside the lahar zone.
  • With any offer, ask what the price includes, who carries the excise tax, and when the deed gets notarized.

Expect this sequence. You and the buyer sign a purchase agreement and open escrow. The title company searches records and orders payoffs, including any deferral lien. You sign the deed in front of a notary, the county gets the affidavit and payment, and the year's tax is divided by closing date. Funds go out after recording.

Before the first call, set aside your deed, loan payoff statement, permit records and latest Pierce County tax bill. A cash purchase has no appraisal and no lender review, so only title work and your own calendar affect the closing date.

Sitting inside the lahar area? Tell buyers early. Anyone dreaming of a cottage or rental unit should hear the rule from you, with the Planning Division number to verify it.

Frequently asked questions

Can I build a backyard cottage in Puyallup's lahar zone?

No. Puyallup Municipal Code 20.20.010(11)(L) prohibits accessory dwelling units in the lahar exclusion area, with an exception near the edge of the valley floor. A guest house with no independent cooking, not lived in full time, may be allowed.

What are the Pierce County property tax deadlines?

Installments come due April 30 and October 31. A weekend October 31 slides to the Monday after. Bills of $50 or less are paid once, by April 30.

What changes about the excise tax in 2027?

Through December 31, 2026 the state tiers break at $525,000, $1,525,000 and $3,025,000. For closings from January 1, 2027 the breaks move to $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000, and the notarized deed date picks the schedule.

Does a South Hill address mean my house is in the city of Puyallup?

Not necessarily. Addresses labeled Puyallup extend into unincorporated pockets such as South Hill. Ask the city Planning Division or the county which jurisdiction holds your parcel.

What happens to a senior property tax deferral when I sell?

Whatever the state paid for you becomes a lien, payable with interest at transfer. Request the payoff number from the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer well before closing.

Fast-sale routes in Lynnwood

You can put a Lynnwood house on the market with an agent, find a buyer on your own, or sell for cash to someone who accepts the place with its flaws. Exposure is widest with an agent. Cash buys you a firm date and fewer surprises, and you pay for that with a lower number. People relocating, closing out an estate or paying two mortgages often decide the date matters more.

Values run high here. The median owner-occupied home is worth $686,900, which means a few percentage points of difference between offers is a big sum. Before choosing, tally the money that leaves your pocket on each path:

  • The loan payoff and any lien or home equity line against the property.
  • Agent fees if you list, plus whatever the buyer's inspector talks you into fixing.
  • Seller-side excise tax at closing.
  • Carrying costs, meaning loan payments, tax, insurance and utilities, for every month the house sits unsold.

Put the three take-home numbers next to each other. A cash bid that seems low can finish near a listing once commission, repair credits and carrying costs are subtracted.

Lynnwood housing figures

Lynnwood is a fast-changing city in southwest Snohomish County, roughly 16 miles north of Seattle at the I-5 and I-405 junction. Renters make up about half of all households.

Because owners and renters are nearly even, plenty of local houses, condos and townhomes have been rented at some point. Anyone buying to keep a tenant in place will want to see the lease, so have a copy handy.

Light rail and commuting

Lynnwood City Center station opened on August 30, 2024, and trains there run to Downtown Seattle and the airport. Buses meet the trains, and Community Transit's Swift Blue Line on State Route 99 and Orange Line through Alderwood add more options. The mean trip to work runs 29.9 minutes.

Live close to the station or a Swift stop? Spell out the distance in your ad. Farther out, point to State Routes 99 and 524 and both interstates instead.

Permits and what you can build

A Lynnwood mailing address does not guarantee the house sits inside the city, so begin with the city's address verification map. Inside the limits, the Development and Business Services department handles permits online, and the walk-in Permit Center at 19100 44th Ave W keeps weekday hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.

Fences under six feet, painting, playground equipment and decks up to 200 square feet need no permit. Remodels commonly need a structural permit, and electrical, plumbing or mechanical changes add their own. Ask the center for the file on your parcel so past work is documented when a buyer asks.

Lots with space for an accessory dwelling unit attract attention. The Residential Neighborhood zone permits attached and detached units up to 1,000 square feet, and a detached unit needs separate utility meters. Lot minimum is 6,000 square feet, with a 10 foot street setback and a 5 foot interior setback. The Planning Division, 425-670-5410, can confirm today's code before you advertise ADU potential.

Disclosure form and excise tax

Under RCW 64.06.020, a Lynnwood seller of improved residential property fills out a disclosure form for the buyer. The deadline is five business days from mutual acceptance unless both sides pick a different one, and rescission rights last three business days after the buyer receives it.

Excise tax is the bigger expense. In most deals the seller bears it, and it goes to the county treasurer as of the sale date. Washington layers a local charge over a graduated state rate. Sales that close from January 1, 2027 start at 1.1 percent and step up to 3 percent in the highest band, with breakpoints at $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. Earlier closings use $525,000, $1,525,000 and $3,025,000. A sale near Lynnwood's median value reaches the 1.28 percent band.

Before accepting an offer, have the escrow office add up the state and local tax for your specific price.

Snohomish County tax dates and appeals

The county's two installments fall on April 30 and October 31, and a postmark on or before the date counts for mail. Miss the April deadline on the first half and the full year goes delinquent, with new charges starting the first of each month. Small bills under $50 are paid in full on April 30. For homes with four or fewer units, RCW 84.56.020 sets delinquent interest at 9 percent a year and adds no penalty.

Values reset every year on January 1, and the notice arrives in June. That figure drives next year's bill. Think it is wrong? An appraiser at the Assessor's Office is the first stop. The formal route is a petition to the Board of Equalization, filed within 60 days of the mailing or by July 1, whichever is later. Phone the board's clerk at 425-388-3407.

At the closing table, escrow splits this year's bill between you and the buyer.

Utilities at closing

Electric service comes from Snohomish County PUD, gas from Puget Sound Energy, and tap water from the Alderwood Water and Wastewater District. Schedule final readings with all three near closing, and give the new owner this list so service is ready on move-in day.

From accepted offer to keys

The sequence barely changes between routes. Only the clock does.

  1. Request payoff letters and locate your newest tax bill and permit paperwork.
  2. Complete the disclosure form with what you truly know about the house.
  3. Sign an accepted offer, then get the form to the buyer inside five business days.
  4. Have the title company produce a settlement statement listing the payoff and excise tax.
  5. Sign the deed, hand off keys, and book last utility readings.

Listings spend weeks on showings, the buyer's inspection and lender approval. In a cash sale those pieces drop out, and you and the buyer mostly set the closing date between you.

Questions for a cash buyer

Insist on written answers to these before signing anything.

  • Price and closing day, stated exactly.
  • Which side covers each closing cost.
  • Whether inspection or financing can still derail the deal.
  • Which title company closes, and whether its settlement statement shows your payoff and the excise tax.

An attorney should review the contract first. With a tenant in the house, ask what the buyer plans for the lease.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a Lynnwood house as-is?

Yes. Washington permits as-is sales, though the disclosure statement is still required unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt. The price will reflect whatever repairs the buyer takes on.

Does a house with a Lynnwood address always fall under Lynnwood permit rules?

No. Some addresses labeled Lynnwood fall outside the city. The city's address verification map shows whether the city or the county issues permits for your lot.

When do Snohomish County property taxes come due?

April 30 for the first half or the whole year, October 31 for the second half. Mail counts as on time with a postmark by the due date. Skipping April turns the entire year delinquent.

How long do I have to appeal my assessed value in Lynnwood?

Sixty days after the notice goes out, or July 1 if that comes later. Send a completed petition to the Snohomish County Board of Equalization, and call the clerk at 425-388-3407 with questions.

Who pays the excise tax when a Lynnwood house sells?

Normally the seller. If the seller skips it, the buyer can end up responsible. It goes to the county treasurer as of the sale date, and the closing agent usually takes it out of your proceeds.

Lake Stevens at a glance

Lake Stevens lies about 35 miles northeast of Seattle and 6 miles northeast of Everett, between Marysville and Snohomish. The city stands on a plateau over the Snohomish River delta, with the Cascade foothills to the east. Its namesake lake is the biggest and deepest in Snohomish County. Shopping centers on Frontier Village, at State Routes 9 and 204, and Cavalero Hill and Machias are among the named neighborhoods.

Commutes run long, with a mean of 35.2 minutes. Three state highways cross the city: State Route 9, State Route 92 and State Route 204. Short-term rental rules

Stays shorter than 30 days fall under Lake Stevens Municipal Code 14.44.064 and Ordinance 1139. The limits the city lists are:

  • Residency: the owner or operator lives on site as a primary residence for at least 240 days a year, unless their permanent home is in the Lake Stevens Urban Growth Area.
  • Units: one rental per property, whether the main house, an accessory dwelling unit or a duplex unit.
  • Cap: 50 active licenses citywide, with permitted properties at least 150 feet apart.
  • Parking: one off-street stall for every two bedrooms, each at least nine feet by 19 feet.
  • Events: the rental cannot serve as a paid venue for weddings, banquets or fundraisers.

Both a city business license and a short-term rental permit are needed. The listed fees are $500 to apply and $100 a year to renew, and the city at (425) 622-9400 can confirm current amounts. If a buyer hopes to keep the rental income, the Planning and Community Development Department can say whether the permit travels with the property or must be reissued in the new owner's name.

If your house has a rental unit

Because the city allows the one permitted rental to be the main house, an accessory dwelling unit or a duplex unit, a property with a second unit raises a few extra questions at sale. Ask the Planning and Community Development Department what is on file for the address, including any business license and short-term rental permit. A buyer who plans to live in the main house and rent the other unit will want to know whether the permit can be transferred, and a buyer who wants no rental will want it closed out.

Keep leases, rent records and the permit paperwork together. Tenants have their own rights, so a cash buyer often asks for the lease terms before making an offer, and the closing date may depend on when the unit can be vacated or when the new owner takes over the lease.

How Snohomish County handles excise tax and recording

In Snohomish County, recording waits on the Treasurer's Office. Staff review each deed for real estate excise tax, and any tax owed must be paid in full first. That covers statutory warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, transfer on death deeds, personal representative deeds, trustee's deeds and deeds in lieu of foreclosure. The excise staff answer questions at 425-388-3366.

Sellers normally pay, and the due date is the sale date even if recording comes later. You will find the Recording Division in the Drewel Building, 3000 Rockefeller Avenue, Everett. Have escrow send the excise affidavit and the deed together to avoid a recording delay.

Property tax due dates and contesting value

Payments open February 15. The county wants half by April 30 and half by October 31. Under RCW 84.56.020, skipping the first half makes the whole year delinquent, and interest or penalty then applies to the entire amount, posted on the first of each month. April 30, 2027 is the next first-half deadline.

An owner who disputes an assessed value must get a petition to the Board of Equalization by July 1 of the assessment year, or inside the longer window printed on the notice. RCW 84.40.038 sets the filing rules and allows late filing in narrow cases. January 1 is the valuation date, so a sale at a price that differs sharply from the assessed value is a useful reference when you file.

What a Lake Stevens seller must disclose

Among other items, the RCW 64.06.020 form asks about fire protection district coverage, roof leaks within five years and sewer service. Some Lake Stevens homes connect to the Lake Stevens Sewer District, so read your bill before you answer. Delivery starts a three business day window in which the buyer may rescind, unless both sides agreed otherwise in writing.

Getting the house ready to close

Washington does not require repairs, yet the disclosure form still asks about roof leaks and structural trouble. Buyers on a listing can negotiate fixes after the inspection, while a cash buyer can take the house as-is, which suits one that needs work.

Ahead of accepting any offer, request a payoff statement from every lender, look for open property tax halves and collect rental license or permit papers. Yes. Cash buyers will take it as-is, and listing buyers can ask for repairs. Either way, the disclosure form covers roof leaks, structural problems and similar issues.

Do I need a permit to keep a short-term rental in Lake Stevens?

Yes, a business license and a short-term rental permit, and only one rental unit per property. Check fees and transfer rules with the city before listing.

Who pays real estate excise tax on a Lake Stevens sale?

Usually the seller. The Snohomish County Treasurer's Office reviews the deed and collects the tax before it can be recorded.

When are Snohomish County property taxes due?

April 30 and October 31, with payments accepted from February 15 on. Missing the first half makes the whole year delinquent.

How far is Lake Stevens from Everett and Seattle?

Roughly 38,000 people live in Longview, and owners hold just over half of the homes, which leaves a large rental share. When a tenant occupies your house, read the lease before you commit to a closing date. The median home value comes from a survey of owner-occupied homes, so order a real valuation for yours.

Older homes and the outside of the house

A lumber company drew up Longview on paper before building it, and the Civic Center is a National Register historic district. Buildings from the 1923 to 1934 boom years lean Georgian-revival, Tudor and craftsman. A house from that period can charm buyers who want character, yet an inspector may flag aging wiring, plumbing or foundation. Western valley subdivisions arrived later, in the 1960s.

Wet, windy, overcast weather means roofs, gutters and drainage get close scrutiny from buyers and inspectors. Walk the exterior before you list or accept an offer.

  • Look at roof surfaces and flashing for pieces lifted or missing after windy spells.
  • Clear the gutters and make sure downspouts send water away from the foundation.
  • Check crawl spaces and low walls for damp spots.
  • Cut back branches hanging over the roof or the power line.

Handle these first and buyers have fewer reasons to ask for credits.

Permits and records to check

The city's Community Development office is your first stop. It issues building, electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits and handles zoning and code compliance. Find it at 1525 Broadway Street in Longview City Hall, where hours are 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday through Thursday, with Fridays closed. Call 360-442-5086 or write permits@ci.longview.wa.us. Archived and recent property records are searchable online too.

Three questions are worth answering there before you sell.

  • Did you or a past owner obtain permits for an addition, finished basement, new deck or re-roof?
  • Does any code compliance case remain open on the property?
  • Does zoning permit what the layout now shows, such as an accessory dwelling or a second kitchen?

Unpermitted work does not make a sale impossible, but it often becomes a repair credit, a lower price or a question from the buyer's lender. Cash buyers commonly accept the work as it is and lower the offer. In every case, describe the work honestly on the disclosure.

What Washington law requires from a Longview seller

For most sales of improved residential property, Washington requires the seller to hand over a completed disclosure statement and places the real estate excise tax on the seller. RCW 64.06.020 gives you five business days from the buyer's and seller's acceptance of a written contract to deliver the statement, unless you both agree to another timeline in writing. The buyer may then rescind within three business days.

Excise tax has a state share and a local add-on, and the county treasurer where the property is located collects it on the sale date. RCW 82.45.060 sets the state share in four bands. Beginning January 1, 2027, the lowest band covers the first $551,000 at a rate of 1.1 percent. The next covers up to $1,551,000 at 1.28 percent, then up to $3,051,000 at 2.75 percent, with 3 percent charged on anything higher.

A closing before 2027 uses the earlier breakpoints of $525,000, $1,525,000 and $3,025,000. The Cowlitz County Treasurer can tell you the local rate for your address and the combined amount at your price. With a median home value near $361,600, most Longview sales land in the lowest band.

Cowlitz County property taxes at sale time

Bills go out from Cowlitz County each February, with payments due April 30 and October 31. Mail yours to the Treasurer at 207 N 4th Ave in Kelso with a postmark on or before the deadline, since a late payment adds interest and penalties. A mid-period closing means title or escrow divides the bill between you and the buyer, and your settlement statement should show a proration line.

To challenge the assessed value, phone the Assessor at 360-577-3010 and speak with an appraiser. That call alone does not protect an appeal. You also need a petition filed with the Board of Equalization, 207 4th Avenue N in Kelso, and the county's deadline is July 1 of the assessment year or 30 days after the value notice went out, whichever comes later.

Weighing a cash offer against a listing

Rate each route by the money you actually keep, never the advertised figure. Commissions, excise tax, buyer repair requests and months of carrying an unsold house all shrink a listing price. A cash offer usually starts lower but can eliminate several of those costs and shorten the schedule.

Put identical questions to every buyer. What is the exact price? Which closing date can they commit to? Who covers excise tax and title costs? Does the offer hinge on an inspection or on financing? Before you sign, let a title company or attorney read the purchase agreement.

Roads, transit and schools

Interstate 5 passes through the corridor. State Routes 4 and 432 lead to Kelso and Wahkiakum County, and the Lewis and Clark Bridge on State Route 433 crosses the Columbia into Rainier, Oregon. Buses from RiverCities Transit connect Longview and Kelso. The city stands where the Cowlitz and Columbia rivers meet and borders Kelso, the county seat.

Buyers with children ask about schools early. Longview Public Schools operates eight elementary schools, three middle schools and two high schools.

Frequently asked questions

Do I have to make repairs before selling my Longview house?

No, Washington does not require repairs before a sale. You must still complete the seller disclosure statement honestly, and a buyer who sees defects may ask for a lower price or credits. A cash sale as-is skips the repair work but usually lowers the offer.

Who pays the real estate excise tax in a Longview sale?

Typically the seller. If the seller does not pay, the buyer becomes responsible. It goes to the Cowlitz County Treasurer on the sale date, so include it when you estimate proceeds.

When are Cowlitz County property taxes due?

April 30 and October 31. The county mails bills each February, and a mailed check postmarked by the due date is on time. Later payments add interest and penalties.

How long does the seller disclosure take in Washington?

You have five business days after both sides accept a written contract, unless you agree to another time in writing. The buyer then has three business days to rescind. RCW 64.06.020 contains the form and the timing.

Can I sell a Longview house with unpermitted work?

Yes, but disclose it. Call the city's Community Development office at 360-442-5086 to learn which permits are on file. A buyer using a loan may ask for the work to be permitted or priced in, while a cash buyer may accept it as is and trim the offer.

Fastest way to sell in Wenatchee

Cash is normally fastest in Wenatchee, since nobody has to wait for an appraisal or a loan to be approved. An agent listing is still worth considering if you can spend time prepping the house and hosting showings.

Wenatchee is Chelan County's seat and biggest city, where the Wenatchee and Columbia rivers join near the eastern foothills of the Cascades. East Wenatchee sits across the Columbia in Douglas County, and the two cities anchor a metro area of about 110,884 people. The city itself has an estimated 35,547 residents.

Wenatchee housing numbers

Median home value is $433,700, with owners in 53.8 percent of homes. The 17.0 minute average commute is a handy selling point, and the city spans about 10.6 square miles of land. Wenatchee calls itself the Apple Capital of the World, and the 10-mile Apple Capital Recreation Loop Trail along both banks of the Columbia draws buyers who like to be outdoors. Building design numbers and hillside lots

The winters are cold and the summers hot and dry. Keep roof and plumbing records handy, since a buyer will ask about both. The Building Division publishes the design numbers local work must meet:

  • Roof snow load of 40 pounds per square foot
  • Climate zone 5B
  • Design wind speed of 85 mph
  • Footing and foundation freeze depth of 18 inches
  • Waterline depth of at least 3 feet, and 5 feet under a driveway

Houses on the hillsides ringing the city sit against ridges that form a wall on the west and south sides, so slope, drainage and retaining walls deserve attention. Most retaining walls up to four feet high are exempt from a permit, though setbacks and shoreline rules still apply.

Schools and roads

The Wenatchee School District provides public K-12 education and serves Malaga, Olds Station, South Wenatchee, Sunnyslope and Wenatchee Heights. It runs seven elementary schools, three middle schools and one high school, Wenatchee High School. Check which attendance area your address falls in before you list.

U.S. Route 2 passes less than a mile north of city limits near Sunnyslope, and U.S. Route 97 also passes north of the city. State Route 28 runs through East Wenatchee across the river. Three bridges cross the Columbia: the Richard Odabashian Bridge and the Senator George Sellar Bridge for vehicles, and the Old Wenatchee Bridge for pedestrians. Link Transit runs buses across Chelan County and into parts of Douglas County.

Do I need a permit before selling?

Only when you do work before the sale. The Building Division's advice is blunt: if you have to ask, you probably need one. A permit covers any building or structure that is erected, constructed, enlarged, altered, repaired, moved, improved, removed, converted or demolished, while painting, papering and similar finish work is exempt.

Also exempt: one-story storage sheds up to 200 square feet kept the required distance from structures and property lines, and decks no higher than 30 inches above grade that do not serve a required exit door. Replacing a leaking sink trap needs no permit, but moving a fixture or installing new drain or supply lines generally does. If a furnace fails, emergency replacement can go ahead right away, though you should get the permit and an inspection once the work is done.

The Building Division is at City Hall, 301 Yakima, and answers at (509) 888-3244, Monday through Friday from 7:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. For rules on short-term rentals or rentals in general, ask Community Development staff or Chelan County before you promise a buyer that use.

How the deed is handled in Chelan County

Any document that conveys property stops at the Chelan County Treasurer before the Auditor records it. There the Real Estate Excise Affidavit is processed and either the excise tax or, for an exempt transaction, a $10 fee is collected. The papers then move on to the Auditor. An exempt transfer still needs the affidavit.

RCW 82.45.090 reinforces the order by blocking recording until the tax is paid or marked not due. Because the tax combines a state and a local part, the Treasurer can tell you what your price owes. Ask early, since the figure is needed before the deed can be recorded and the sale finished.

The Auditor accepts only properly formatted documents with original, notarized signatures and the correct fee. Common reasons for refusal are:

  • A missing parcel number
  • A first-page top margin under 3 inches
  • Illegible text
  • A missing legal description
  • An inadequate fee

Getting the house ready for a buyer

Gather what buyers ask for: roof and plumbing records, permits for anything built or replaced, and notes on hillside drainage or retaining wall work. Did something go in without a permit? The Building Division at (509) 888-3244 can say how to make it compliant.

Then pick your path. Listing reaches the most buyers but demands prep work and showings. Selling for cash gives up reach in exchange for speed, with the buyer accepting the house as is, which helps when repairs look daunting. If the house is a rental, tell buyers early whether a tenant stays, and put what stays with the house in writing so closing day holds no surprises. Collect the receipts and manuals for equipment that stays, and keep a copy of every document you hand to the buyer, the title company or the county. A cash buyer will usually still want to see title cleared before the Treasurer and Auditor steps begin.

The seller disclosure and what to expect

Washington sellers of improved residential property fill out the condition form in RCW 64.06.020, and by default it is due five business days after both sides sign. Disclose problems you know of, such as earlier work done without a permit.

With a cash buyer the sale does not wait on a lender's appraisal, so the schedule depends on title work and the county steps above. Ask each buyer who pays the excise tax, compare what you would net after repairs and carrying costs, and get the closing date in writing. A title or escrow company can carry the affidavit and deed through the Treasurer and the Auditor for you.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell my Wenatchee house without making repairs?

Yes. Cash buyers often purchase houses as they stand. The state disclosure form in RCW 64.06.020 still goes to the buyer, with any problems you know about listed.

What does the Chelan County Treasurer do in a sale?

The Treasurer processes the Real Estate Excise Affidavit and collects the excise tax due, or a $10 processing fee when the sale is exempt. Only after that does the Auditor record the deed.

Do small projects need a permit in Wenatchee?

Some do not. Painting, certain small sheds, retaining walls up to four feet and low decks are exempt. Moving a plumbing fixture or adding new supply or drain lines generally does require a permit, so call the Building Division at (509) 888-3244.

What snow load and freeze depth apply to Wenatchee homes?

A 40 pound per square foot roof snow load and an 18 inch freeze depth for footings and foundations. The climate zone is 5B, and design wind speed is 85 mph.

Which school district covers Wenatchee?

The Wenatchee School District, which also serves Malaga, Olds Station, South Wenatchee, Sunnyslope and Wenatchee Heights. It runs seven elementary schools, three middle schools and Wenatchee High School.

Street projects can also affect showings on your block, so ask the city what work is planned near your address. Raked leaves belong in yard waste bags rather than the street, where they clog storm drains.

Real estate excise tax on a sale

University Place levies its own 0.5 percent excise tax on the sale price, and the Pierce County Treasurer collects it alongside the state tax. Each month the county forwards 99 percent to the city for capital projects and keeps 1 percent to cover collection.

Washington's own portion steps up with price, starting at 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 and moving to 1.28 percent through $1,525,000. Sales on or after January 1, 2027 use higher thresholds of $551,000 and $1,551,000. You owe the tax when the sale happens, and unpaid tax draws interest after 30 days. A house priced near the $624,800 median crosses the first bracket, which means the total is a blend of rates. Ask a title company to run the exact math. Title or escrow orders payoff figures from the Pierce County Assessor-Treasurer, and the excise tax is calculated on the final price and paid to the county treasurer at the time of sale.

Before the closing date, collect permit records for any finished work and note any gaps with Planning and Development Services. If a gap turns up, fixing it early costs less than a renegotiation. Ask the closing agent which fees you owe and which the buyer covers, and get that division in writing.

Recording the deed completes the sale. A cash purchase tends to move through these steps faster because no lender adds conditions, although title review still has to finish. Keep copies of everything you sign, and make sure utilities and keys are handled on the agreed day.

List when the house shows well and you can wait out showings and a buyer's loan. Lean toward cash when the house needs work, is part of an estate or must close by a set day.

  • Learn which side pays excise tax, title and recording costs with each cash buyer.

Skagit County's seat sits in the river valley about 60 miles north of Seattle and 51 miles south of the Canadian border. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 35,193 residents. Because the Skagit River runs beside downtown, flood zones come up early in most sales, and the next section covers that.

Flood zones and the Skagit River

Many Mount Vernon properties sit in the 100-year floodplain. The city tells owners to check FEMA's Map Service Center or ask Development Services for the zone and what it means for a parcel. Learn your zone before listing day, since buyers and lenders ask early.

Do these three things early:

The city finished a permanent flood wall in 2019, but a buyer will still want your records, not a story. Rain falls mostly from October through March, so show that gutters, drainage and crawl space are in good order.

Permits to check before you list

Development Services is at 910 Cleveland Avenue, phone 360-336-6214, email permittech@mountvernonwa.gov. The Building Division reviews permits, interprets codes, inspects work and enforces the code. The city uses the 2021 International Codes with Washington amendments. This is how common projects are treated:

ProjectPermit rule

Doing this before you list keeps the surprise out of the inspection period.

Excise tax, deed and recording

Two county offices handle your closing. The seller signs a Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit with the deed, the treasurer receives the tax, and state law sends the deed to the county auditor for recording.

The state portion has four bands. Closings through December 31, 2026 pay 1.1 percent on the first $525,000, then 1.28 percent to $1,525,000, 2.75 percent to $3,025,000 and 3 percent beyond. From January 1, 2027 the bands start higher, at $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. The local portion is extra. Notarizing the deed fixes the sale date for the Department of Revenue, and payment is owed that day.

Skagit County's Treasurer can confirm the local rate and tell you what to bring. Raise the current half of the property tax with that office too.

Selling an older Mount Vernon house

Interstate 5 was built through downtown in 1969 and separated downtown from most of the residential district, so location within town shapes how buyers see a street. The city runs on a mayor-council form, with a seven-member council, so code changes pass through meetings you can attend. If your house is older, expect its age, any past flood history and its permit file to be the topics a buyer raises first. Pull the paperwork together before the first showing.

Getting around

Interstate 5 cuts through downtown, and State Route 9 runs parallel to it, with State Routes 536 and 538 linking downtown and the Baker Heights area. Skagit Station connects Amtrak Cascades, Skagit Transit, Greyhound and local taxis, and a commuter bus runs to Everett Station for the Sounder train. Workers average 22.9 minutes getting to work. Mention whichever of these is closest to your house, and give the walking or driving distance if it is short. Bellingham International Airport is 25 miles north, which some buyers care about.

What happens after an accepted offer

After an offer is accepted, the sequence is predictable. A contract is signed and the disclosure form goes out. A title company opens the file and orders a settlement statement. You sign the deed and the affidavit, and the tax gets paid. The county then records the deed and the funds are released.

A cash purchase leaves out the buyer's loan, which removes one common cause of delay. Gather your flood records now, as the sections above suggest, so nothing waits on you.

When cash makes sense

Three situations point toward it: the house is in a flood zone and you want no financing contingency, repairs are overdue, or you inherited a home and want to close on your own schedule.

Before agreeing, make the buyer verify funds, put the closing date on paper, and name who pays excise tax and title fees. Then run the comparison against a listing by taking off excise tax, agent fees and repair credits, and counting the weeks the house would sit on the market. A request for an offer on your address shows where it lands.

If you take a listing instead, the buyer's inspector will likely ask about floodplain status and any open permit, so the records you gathered earlier carry over.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Do I have to disclose flood risk when I sell a Mount Vernon house?

The statutory disclosure form asks about flooding, standing water, drainage problems and floodplain location, and you answer from your own knowledge. Many properties are in the 100-year floodplain, so check your zone with FEMA's Map Service Center or Development Services first.

Who handles permits for a Mount Vernon home?

Call the Development Services permit technicians at 360-336-6214 or email permittech@mountvernonwa.gov. The office is at 910 Cleveland Avenue and can also tell you your zoning district and flood zone.

Does a fence need a permit in Mount Vernon?

Yes. All new fences and replacements need one: a planning permit under 7 feet and a building permit at 7 feet or taller.

How is the excise tax on a Mount Vernon sale figured?

State tax opens at 1.1 percent on the bottom slice and rises in bands, with a local rate added. For a total at your price, ask the Skagit County Treasurer or your title officer.

Is the excise tax due when the deed is recorded or when the sale happens?

The sale date controls, and the Department of Revenue means the day the deed is notarized, even if recording follows later. Wait more than a month after it and interest and penalties begin.

Before you sell in SeaTac

SeaTac is a small, fast-growing city south of Seattle, built around the region's main airport. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 34,578 people, a 10.0 percent jump over the 2020 base. Older neighborhoods such as Angle Lake, Bow Lake, McMicken Heights and Riverton Heights predate the city's 1990 incorporation. Owners live in fewer than half of the homes, and typical values sit well below Seattle's.

Share of homes occupied by owners46.5%
Typical value of an owned home (2020 to 2024)$519,700
Typical monthly rent$1,660

Renters fill many SeaTac homes, which means plenty of sellers are landlords or heirs of a rental. If that fits you, the rental section below comes first.

Living next to the airport

Almost every parcel in SeaTac is touched by the airport, and buyers know it. Sea-Tac International sits on roughly three square miles inside city limits, owned and run by the Port of Seattle, and the city's boundaries wrap around it. Noise complaints in the 1960s and 1970s led the Port and King County to the Sea-Tac Communities Plan of 1976, the first program in the country where an airport operator bought homes and school buildings near the airport and soundproofed others. Around 420 acres of vacated land north of the field became North SeaTac Park, with fields, trails and a community center.

Buyers will bring up noise and flight paths, so decide ahead of time what you will say about both. The roof deserves a look as well. On the state disclosure form, one question covers any roof leak during the past five years, and an old leak should be repaired or reported before the house goes on the market.

Written records help here. If you ever received sound insulation or other work tied to the airport, or have receipts for new windows, keep copies in your sale folder. They show a buyer that the house has been looked after and may answer a noise question before it is asked.

Transit and schools buyers ask about

Commuters like the city's links. Link light rail stops at SeaTac/Airport station and Angle Lake station. King County Metro runs the RapidRide A Line on International Boulevard (State Route 99) and the RapidRide F Line on Southcenter Boulevard. State Route 518 and the Airport Expressway tie the city into the freeway system, and some Sound Transit Express buses end at the airport and nearby hubs.

Highline Public Schools covers most of the city. Most residents are zoned to Chinook Middle School and Tyee High School, some go to Sylvester Middle School and Highline High School in Burien, and residents north of the airport are generally zoned to Glacier Middle School and then Highline High School. Small parts of SeaTac are in the Kent School District and the Renton School District. If your house sits near a boundary, confirm the district before you give buyers an answer.

Light rail and RapidRide stops give some SeaTac streets a clear selling point. Name the nearest station or bus line in your listing, along with the commute of 25.4 minutes that the average resident faces, and let buyers do the math for their own workplace.
