If your SeaTac house is a rental

A business license is required to run a rental unit in SeaTac, and the city points owners to the Washington Department of Revenue for the online application. Each tenant must also receive the city's Renting in SeaTac Guide, a handout on rights, evictions, deposits, repairs and notices.

Ending a tenancy so you can sell follows its own statute. For a single-family rental, RCW 59.18.650 calls for 90 days of written notice. After the tenant moves out, the owner has 30 days to start selling in earnest, typically by listing at a reasonable price or advertising on the multiple listing service. If the home goes back on the rental market or comes off the market inside 90 days, the law assumes there was never a plan to sell. Tenants removed in violation may recover whichever is greater, actual damages or three months of rent, plus fees and costs.

Also call the city of SeaTac before listing to find out whether any code complaint or unfinished permit sits on the address.

Closing costs for a SeaTac seller

Excise tax is the largest cost, and Washington puts it on sellers in the usual case. A buyer inherits the duty when the seller leaves it unpaid, and the balance may become a lien. The state tiers are 1.1 percent up to $525,000, 1.28 percent up to $1,525,000, then 2.75 percent and 3 percent. Starting with sales on January 1, 2027, the first break rises to $551,000. King County layers a local rate over the state's.

Money goes to the county treasurer at the time of sale, with the notarized deed date as the date the Department of Revenue uses. Interest builds on late payments. Call the King County treasurer to learn the SeaTac local rate and your property tax balance, and have escrow explain how the year's property tax is divided with the buyer.

A seller disclosure statement is part of every standard sale here. The buyer receives it within five business days of contract acceptance, then gets three business days to rescind. Look for questions on easements, shared driveways, sewer hookups, wood stoves, drainage, shorelines, wetlands, floodplains and critical areas.

Costs are easier to manage when you know them early, so ask escrow for a rough estimate of your net proceeds before you commit to a closing date.

Is a cash sale worth considering?

For some owners it is. Think about it if the house needs work, a tenant lives in it, or a title or tax issue would trip up a buyer relying on a loan. Measure each offer against what a listing would leave you after repairs, excise tax and months of carrying costs.

  • Get the closing date and the split of escrow and title charges in writing.
  • Round up permits and receipts for additions or major repairs.
  • Disclose tenants and the lease term before you sign anything.

The path is short. Once you accept, escrow opens and a title search runs. Proceeds pay off any loan, you sign the deed with a notary, and the county gets the affidavit and tax. Funds are released after recording. Nobody orders an appraisal or lender review, so your timetable is set by title work and your own plans.

Gather the deed, a loan payoff statement and your latest King County tax statement before the first conversation, so you can answer questions without delay.

Frequently asked questions

How many people live in SeaTac, Washington?

About 34,578 as of July 1, 2025, compared with 31,454 in the 2020 census. Roughly 46.5 percent of homes are lived in by their owners.

Do I need a business license to rent out a house in SeaTac?

Yes. SeaTac requires one for any rental unit, and the application is online through the Washington Department of Revenue. Tenants must be given the city's Renting in SeaTac Guide.

Which school district is SeaTac in?

Highline Public Schools serves most of the city, mainly Chinook Middle School and Tyee High School. Small parts are in the Kent and Renton districts, so check your address.

How much notice must I give a tenant if I want to sell the house?

For a single-family home, RCW 59.18.650 requires 90 days of written notice. After the tenant leaves, list or advertise within 30 days at a reasonable price, or the law assumes you never meant to sell.

What is the state excise tax on a SeaTac sale?

Four state tiers apply: 1.1 percent to $525,000, 1.28 percent to $1,525,000, 2.75 percent to $3,025,000 and 3 percent beyond, plus a local rate. Break points shift for sales beginning January 1, 2027.

Selling fast in Walla Walla

The quickest routes are a cash sale or an as-is sale to an investor, since neither waits on a mortgage approval. A standard listing still makes sense for a house in good shape, though it brings showings, an appraisal and the buyer's loan timeline.

Walla Walla is the seat of Walla Walla County, in a valley of southeastern Washington about 6 miles north of the Oregon line. The city is compact, around 13 square miles, and sits beside College Place, which adds a second small city to the same housing market.

Walla Walla housing numbers

The median home is valued at $393,600 and 57.1 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. The population is nearly flat at 34,058, down 0.6 percent from the 2020 base, so buyers will compare your house closely against others for sale instead of assuming rising demand will lift it. The average commute is under 13 minutes, which is a real asset when you describe the location.

Housing measureWalla Walla

Design numbers for repairs and additions

Walla Walla sits in the Cascades' rain shadow, so rainfall is modest, but winters can still turn cold. Anything you repair or add has to meet the city's building design numbers, which are published by Development Services:

  • Ground and minimum roof snow load of 30 pounds per square foot
  • Design wind speed of 110 mph
  • Seismic design category D
  • Frost depth of 24 inches
  • Ice shield underlayment required

If you replaced a roof or built a structure, keep the permit paperwork to hand over at closing. A buyer's inspector often asks for it.

Schools and getting around

Most of the city is in Walla Walla Public Schools, with seven elementary schools, two middle schools, one traditional high school (Wa-Hi) and two alternative high schools, Lincoln and Opportunity. The far western edge belongs to the College Place School District. Private options include Walla Walla Catholic Schools and several Christian schools.

U.S. Route 12 is the main east-west highway, and State Route 125 runs through town into Milton-Freewater, Oregon. Valley Transit serves Walla Walla and College Place and has been fare-free since 2022. The regional airport has commercial flights to Seattle-Tacoma twice a day.

Permits for fix-up work

If the job is structural, mechanical or plumbing, Development Services handles the permit. The department issues permits and inspections for new construction, remodels, mechanical and plumbing work, signs and other land use activity inside city limits, and it adopted the 2021 International Building Codes.

Applications, payments and inspection requests are now online for permits processed after August 19, 2025. Older permits may still involve calls to the permit technicians for payment and inspections. For a project that is not clearly covered, ask Development Services before you start. Work done without a required permit can turn up in a buyer's inspection, so it is cheaper to sort out beforehand than during escrow.

Short-term rentals

The rules depend on which type of short-term rental you have. A Type 1 rental is the owner's principal residence, either with rooms rented while the owner is present or the entire dwelling rented no more than 90 days a year. A Type 2 rental is a dwelling that is not the owner's principal residence.

Ordinance 2017-33 bans new Type 2 rentals. Those lawfully operating before November 9, 2017 may continue as non-conforming uses, and that status runs with the property as long as the use has not been abandoned. A buyer of such a property must obtain a Type 2 permit and license at closing, with proof of ownership. The permit can be lost in several ways:

  • Use is presumed abandoned if the location was not rented at least a total of 29 days in the preceding year
  • Use ends if the location sits unrented for 6 consecutive months or more
  • A fourth nuisance violation leads to revocation, after fines of $750 and then $1,000

If you own a Type 2 rental, ask Development Services for the current permit status before you advertise, since a buyer's offer may depend on it.

How the deed and excise tax work

The real estate excise tax goes to the treasurer of the county where the property sits, who acts as the state's agent under RCW 82.45.090. The county auditor cannot take the deed for recording until payment is verified or the treasurer notes that nothing is due. In Walla Walla County that means the Treasurer first, then recording through the Auditor.

The tax combines a state portion and a local portion, so ask the County Treasurer for the total at your sale price. A title or escrow company normally carries the affidavit and deed through both offices.

You also owe the buyer a written condition disclosure. RCW 64.06.020 prescribes the form for improved residential property and sets delivery at five business days after a signed contract, unless the parties agree otherwise. Receiving it gives the buyer three business days to back out.

What to do first

Start by deciding which kind of buyer suits your house. A cash buyer or investor takes a house with deferred maintenance and does not wait on a lender. A conventional buyer will expect the repairs to be done or priced in.

Then gather what any buyer will ask for: permit paperwork for roofs and additions, the status of a short-term rental permit if you have one, and the excise tax figure from the Treasurer. Known defects and unpermitted work belong on the disclosure form. Getting this ready first keeps a cash sale quick and keeps a listing from stalling after an offer.

When offers arrive, compare them on what you net after repairs and carrying costs, who pays the excise tax, and the closing date. A cash buyer skips the appraisal and loan approval, so the closing date is mostly a matter of title work and your own move. Ask a title or escrow company to confirm the payoff before you sign anything, and keep a copy of every document you hand over. If the house has a tenant or stored belongings, agree in writing on what stays and when the place will be empty.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a Walla Walla house that needs repairs?

Yes. Investors and cash buyers often take houses with deferred maintenance. The seller disclosure under RCW 64.06.020 still goes to the buyer, and known defects or unpermitted work belong on it.

Can a new owner keep running my Walla Walla house as a short-term rental?

Only in limited cases. New Type 2 rentals are banned, but a lawfully established one that has not been abandoned keeps its non-conforming status with the property. The new owner must obtain a Type 2 permit and license at closing with proof of ownership.

What building design numbers apply to Walla Walla houses?

A 30 pound per square foot roof snow load, a 110 mph wind speed, seismic design category D and a 24 inch frost depth, plus ice shield underlayment. These apply to new work under the 2021 International Building Codes.

Who collects the excise tax when a Walla Walla house sells?

The county treasurer, acting as the state's agent under RCW 82.45.090. Recording waits until the tax is paid or noted as not due, so ask the Walla Walla County Treasurer for the figure at your price.

Which school district serves my Walla Walla address?

Most of the city is in Walla Walla Public Schools, and the extreme western edge is in the College Place School District. Confirm the boundary with the district for your street.

Selling a house in Pullman

Pullman is a college town in the Palouse, in eastern Whitman County about 65 miles south of Spokane and 32 miles north of Lewiston, Idaho. On July 1, 2025 the estimate stood at 33,756 residents, 2.6% above April 2020. Washington State University is the reason most buyers and renters come.

Selling here usually means thinking about two kinds of buyer: families who want to stay, and investors who want a student rental. Registering and licensing a rental, covered below, matter to that second group.

Pullman housing figures

About two of every three Pullman homes are rented. Just 32.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied (2020 to 2024). The median owner-occupied home is valued at $424,800 and median gross rent is $1,062. There are 12,682 households of 2.07 people on average, with a median income of $46,812. A mere 65.6% of residents stayed in the same house for a year, which shows how much of the market turns over with the school year. Pricing works better from nearby sales of comparable houses than from the citywide median.

Registering and licensing a rental

Owners of residential rental property must register with the City of Pullman under Pullman City Code 6.98. The Police Department's permits and licenses page names the Code Enforcement Supervisor, at 509-334-0802, for questions. Short-term rentals follow a separate process under chapter 17.109, with application instructions that spell out what an owner submits.

RequirementCost or detail
Rental registration (code 6.98)One-time $15 per address
Short-term rental fee$200, paid before review starts
Business licenseNAICS code 721199, applied for before final approval
Insurance and liability coverageAs required by RCW 64.37.050

A short-term rental application also needs a floor plan showing beds, smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, fire extinguishers and an emergency egress light, plus an evacuation plan and a plot plan showing off-street parking. Approval can carry an occupancy limit of the number of sleeping rooms plus two. If your house runs as a rental, tell a buyer which registrations are current and hand over the paperwork.

Hills, weather and building permits

Pullman sits across four hills of windblown loess: Military Hill, Pioneer Hill, Sunnyside Hill and College Hill. Downtown lies in a valley where Missouri Flat Creek and Paradise Creek join the South Fork of the Palouse River. Steep lots and drainage are worth documenting if your house sits on a slope.

Winters are cold and wet and summers hot and dry. The building division's design criteria include a ground snow load of 30 pounds per square foot, a frost depth of 30 inches and a required ice barrier underlayment on roofs. Pullman adopted the 2021 International Building and Residential Codes, effective March 15, 2024.

Reroofing, residing and replacement windows often need no plan review, and the city can issue those permits online, over the counter or next day. Projects that change the structure or footprint go through plan review that can take four to six weeks. Email applications to pwcd-admin@pullman-wa.gov, or visit 190 SE Crestview Street, Building A. Close any open permit before listing, since a buyer's lender or inspector may raise it.

Schools and roads

The Pullman School District covers Franklin, Jefferson, Sunnyside and Kamiak elementary schools, Lincoln Middle School and Pullman High School, the city's only public high school. U.S. Route 195 and State Route 27 run north toward Spokane, US 195 also runs south to Lewiston, and State Route 270 connects Pullman with Moscow, Idaho. Pullman Transit serves residents and WSU students. Mean travel time to work is 14.6 minutes, a short commute that is part of the appeal. If your house is close to campus or a bus line, say so in the listing, and name the school it feeds, since families look at that early. Pullman High is on Military Hill, and students can take Running Start courses through WSU and Spokane Falls Community College.

Excise tax on a Pullman sale

RCW 82.45.080 puts this tax on the seller. The state rate runs from 1.1% on the first slice to 3% on the highest, with a local portion added, and the Whitman County Treasurer knows which local rate applies in the city. The first band ends at $525,000 now. Sales beginning January 1, 2027 have breakpoints of $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. Notarization of the deed decides which set applies, so a closing signed in late December uses the 2026 numbers.

The Whitman County Treasurer handles real estate excise tax, so the affidavit, deed and payment go to its office at 400 N Main Street in Colfax. If the seller leaves it unpaid, a lien can attach and the buyer may become responsible.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Pullman houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Whitman County property taxes at closing

Two payment dates, April 30 and October 31, come from RCW 84.56.020, and a bill of $50 or less is paid whole by April 30. Call the Treasurer to confirm which schedule your parcel follows.

  • Treasurer: 400 N Main Street, Colfax, mailing address P.O. Box 550, phone 509-397-6230.
  • Office hours: 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Ask your closing officer to prorate the year and clear any unpaid half from sale proceeds.

Ask the Whitman County Assessor whether a senior, disability or other reduction applies to your parcel, and ask the Treasurer how the year's tax will be split at the closing table. Behind on taxes? Phone the Treasurer first, ahead of listing.

Preparing your paperwork

Before a buyer or investor visits, assemble what they will ask for. Bring your deed, the latest Whitman County tax statement and any payoff letter. If the house has been a rental, add the city registration, current leases and any short-term rental approval. Add permit records for reroofing, residing or window replacement, since the city issues those quickly and a buyer may want proof. For work on a slope, include drainage notes or a survey.

When the buyer is ready, the title company or closing officer drafts a settlement statement, you sign the deed and affidavit, and the Treasurer receives the tax. A cash sale usually moves faster because there is no lender to satisfy, but the documents are the same.

Selling options in Pullman

Pullman owners can list, sell privately, or accept an as-is offer in cash. Deed and excise tax steps match across all three.

  • A listing does best when the timing fits the academic calendar and the house shows well.
  • An investor purchase suits a rental with tenants, deferred repairs or a lease that ends mid-year.
  • Quiz each buyer on tenant notice, registration records and the closing date.

For a rented house, gather the leases, the registration confirmation and any short-term rental approval before you speak to a buyer. Tenants usually care about the dates, and a buyer will price in whatever turnover they expect. If the house is owner-occupied, the school year may shape the best time to show it, since families tend to shop around it. Sorting these facts first shortens the conversation with every buyer, whether you list or sell directly.

What is the owner-occupied rate in Pullman?

For 2020 to 2024 it was 32.0%, so roughly two of every three occupied homes are rented. Many buyers will be investors or will ask for rental history.

Must a Pullman rental house be registered?

Yes. Owners of residential rental property register with the city under Pullman City Code 6.98, paying a one-time $15 per address.

What does a Pullman short-term rental application cost?

The application instructions list a $200 short-term rental fee, paid before review begins. You also need a business license under NAICS code 721199 and the insurance that RCW 64.37.050 requires.

How long does a Pullman building permit take?

Reroofing, residing and window replacement may be issued online, over the counter or next day. More involved projects take four to six weeks for plan review.

Where does the Pullman excise tax go?

The Whitman County Treasurer, in Colfax, since the payment goes to the county where the property is. The seller owes it under RCW 82.45.080.

Des Moines housing snapshot

Des Moines is a King County city on the east shore of Puget Sound with 33,032 residents (July 1, 2025). Federal Way lies to the south, Kent to the east, SeaTac to the northeast, Burien to the north and Normandy Park to the northwest. That puts a house within reach of Sea-Tac Airport, the I-5 corridor and the water. Sea-Tac sits about 2 miles to the north, and some property in the city has been bought out because of aircraft noise, a topic buyers raise.

Housing measureDes Moines figure
Households, 2020-202411,925
Owner-occupied housing rate, 2020-202460.6%
Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020-2024$597,000
Median gross rent, 2020-2024$1,799
Median household income, 2020-2024$92,483

With 39.4 percent of households renting, many sales involve a tenant. The mean commute of 30.8 minutes is why buyers weigh the new light rail station and highway access so closely.

Slopes, neighborhoods and schools

Most of the city rolls down to Puget Sound from about 400 feet along Pacific Highway, which gives many homes a view of the water and Vashon Island. The ravines of Des Moines Creek and Massey Creek cut through that slope. If your lot is near either ravine, expect buyers to ask about drainage, flooding and slope stability, topics the state seller disclosure form raises directly.

  • Marina and downtown: an 838-berth city marina with a fishing pier and boat launch.
  • Zenith and Woodmont: Saltwater State Park sits in a steep ravine between them.
  • Redondo: a boardwalk and aquarium near the Federal Way border.
  • Kent-Des Moines Road area: a park-and-ride with express buses, plus Highline College and a Central Washington University branch.

Highline Public Schools covers most of Des Moines, with Pacific Middle School and Mount Rainier High School as the local secondary schools. Woodmont and Redondo are in the Federal Way School District, so a few streets share a city but not a district.

Transit and highways

Interstate 5 and State Routes 99, 509 and 516 serve the city. The Kent Des Moines light rail station on the 1 Line opened in December 2025 near Highline College. King County Metro buses run to the Burien Transit Center and Kent station, and the park-and-ride at the Kent-Des Moines Road interchange has express service to Seattle and Tacoma. Mention the station and the park-and-ride in a listing for any house within reach of them.

Short-term rental permits

An owner who rents a home for stays of 30 nights or less needs both a city business license and a short-term rental permit, along with a notification letter and a signed Good Neighbor Agreement. The city's rules include:

  • A local property representative must be reachable around the clock and respond to complaints within 30 minutes.
  • Only one booking at a time is allowed per dwelling unit, and occupancy follows a city table.
  • No overnight street parking, and the owner must contract for garbage service.
  • Violations can lead to permit denial or revocation and infractions.

Business licenses are filed and renewed each year through FileLocal. A business outside the city needs one only if it earns $4,000 or more a year in Des Moines. If you hold a permit, ask the Community Development office whether it transfers to a buyer, since the answer depends on the permit terms. The office counter is open Tuesday through Thursday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m., at 21630 11th Avenue S, Suite D.

Ways to sell fast

Sellers here usually weigh four approaches against their deadline and the home's condition:

  • List on the market: best for updated homes with water views or close access to the light rail.
  • Sell as-is to an investor: fits deferred repairs, tenant-occupied homes and inherited houses.
  • Sell to a cash buyer: removes loan approval delays, and the closing date can usually be set to your schedule.
  • Sell by owner: saves the agent fee, but you manage disclosure forms and the closing paperwork.

If a tenant lives in the house, check the lease, the notice rules and whether the buyer wants vacant possession before you accept an offer. Compare bids by net proceeds, after excise tax, any loan payoff and prorated taxes.

Excise tax on a sale

Washington's state excise tax rises with price under RCW 82.45.060. It takes 1.1 percent of the portion up to $525,000 and 1.28 percent of the portion from $525,000 up to $1,525,000. For sales beginning January 1, 2027, the first tier moves to $551,000. Sellers usually bear it. Payment is made to the treasurer of the county holding the property, and a local rate is layered on.

Before closing, ask King County for the current excise tax affidavit steps and the combined local rate for Des Moines, and have your escrow officer show the tax line on the settlement statement.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Des Moines houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

King County property tax dates

Under RCW 84.56.020 the full bill is due April 30. Owners whose total reaches $50 may instead pay half in April and half by October 31. If you are selling, check the parcel for unpaid second-half tax. Statements are due to be distributed by March 15 when the county has the tax roll on time.

A late home of four or fewer units owes 9 percent interest per year but no penalties. Other property faces 12 percent plus penalties of 3 percent and then 8 percent. Get the exact payoff from King County Treasury Operations before closing, since escrow uses that figure to settle the account.

What to prepare before you list

Gather the lease and notice records if a tenant lives there, permit history for any work, a short-term rental permit if you hold one, and your latest tax statement. If your lot is near a ravine, be ready to answer drainage and slope questions on the disclosure form. A clean file makes both a regular buyer and a cash buyer more comfortable.

After you accept an offer, escrow opens and title work turns up any unpaid property tax. You sign the deed and affidavit, and escrow pays the excise tax shown on the settlement statement from what you receive. Cash means no loan approval, so the closing date tends to follow title work and the tenant's situation, if you have one. Ask your closing agent what the combined local rate will be so the net figure holds no surprises.

Frequently asked questions

Which school district serves Des Moines?

Highline Public Schools covers most of Des Moines. Woodmont and Redondo belong to the Federal Way School District, so confirm your own address.

Do I need a permit to run a short-term rental in Des Moines?

Yes. Yes, a city business license and a short-term rental permit, backed by a notification letter and a signed Good Neighbor Agreement. Complaints must get an answer from a local representative within 30 minutes.

How is the state excise tax figured on a Des Moines sale?

By tier. The first $525,000 pays 1.1 percent, and the next slice to $1,525,000 pays 1.28 percent. Add the local rate. The seller normally covers it.

Is Sea-Tac Airport near Des Moines?

Yes. The airport is about 2 miles north of the city, and some Des Moines property has been bought out because of aircraft noise. Ask the county or an agent about noise context for a specific address.

When are King County property taxes due?

April 30 is the due date, though a total of $50 or more can be split with the second half due October 31. Look for unpaid second-half tax before you sell.

Selling in Maple Valley?

Selling fast in Maple Valley

Three paths lead to a sale here: list with an agent, sell privately, or hand the house over to a cash buyer as it stands. Cash fits an owner who cannot sit through showings, loan approvals and inspection demands. What you give up is the premium a polished listing might earn.

Maple Valley is a family suburb southeast of Seattle with 28,482 estimated residents as of July 1, 2025. About 83 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied home is valued at $724,700. Households average about 3.01 people and earn a median of $152,885. With numbers like these, judge each offer by what you keep. A quick checklist:

  • Payoff amounts for your mortgage and any second loan or lien.
  • Repairs an inspector or buyer is likely to put on the table.
  • Commission and excise tax on a listing versus the cost of a direct deal.
  • The number of months you can afford the payments while the house sits.

Tenants matter too. A renter about to leave, or a lease that outlasts your target date, can settle which path works.

Commute and carrying costs

Owners with a mortgage pay a median of $2,984 a month, and the median rent is $2,304. The average commute is 37 minutes, which is long, so lead with how quickly your house reaches State Route 169, State Route 18 and State Route 516.

Lakes, drainage and shoreline lots

Lake Wilderness, Lake Lucerne, Rock Creek and a piece of Pipe Lake lie inside city limits. Rain falls harder here than in Seattle, so walk the roof, gutters, drainage and crawl space yourself before an inspector does.

On or near water? Economic and Community Development wants a call before you cut trees (lakefront lots especially), alter wetlands, slopes or streams, or build or replace a dock. Clear up any question about earlier work with the city before listing day.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Maple Valley house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

When a house needs a permit

The city's Economic and Community Development Department, (425) 413-8800, answers permit questions. Common projects sort out like this:

ProjectBuilding permit
New structure or additionRequired
Installing or replacing windowsRequired
Remodel that moves structural members, plumbing or mechanical fixturesRequired
Fence over 6 feetRequired
Storage building under 200 square feetNot required, setbacks apply
Siding replacement, painting, flooringNot required
Fence under 6 feetNot required

Sale time is when gaps show. On a multiple listing service sale, you disclose improvements and repairs and say whether permits and inspections were obtained. Many lenders refuse to finance without a final inspection on record, and a home with unpermitted changes can face tear-down, vacating or costly repairs. Unsure about your parcel? Ask the department before listing.

Can you add units on your lot?

Often, yes. State law E2SHB 1110 makes cities of Maple Valley's size allow middle housing on lots zoned mostly residential, and the city's FAQ applies it to the R-4 and R-6 single-family zones. Duplexes, triplexes, fourplexes, townhouses, stacked flats, courtyard apartments and cottage housing are all on the menu. A lot with a single-family home may add two accessory dwelling units, three units in all.

Buyers who smell development potential will study lot size and zoning, so get the department's answer on what your parcel allows before calling it a development site.

Disclosure form and excise tax

Most sellers of improved residential property must deliver a disclosure statement under RCW 64.06.020 within five business days of a written contract that both sides accepted, unless they set a different schedule. The buyer's right to rescind lasts three business days.

Excise tax is normally the seller's bill, due to the county treasurer on the sale date. A graduated state rate applies, plus a local rate. Closings from January 1, 2027 use bands starting at $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000 and rates of 1.1, 1.28, 2.75 and 3 percent from bottom to top. Earlier closings use $525,000, $1,525,000 and $3,025,000. A sale at the city median is taxed partly at 1.1 percent and partly at 1.28 percent.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Maple Valley houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Property tax dates and value appeals

King County sends the bill, and the schedule comes from RCW 84.56.020: pay by April 30, or pay half then and the remainder by October 31. Late taxes on residential property with four or fewer units accrue 9 percent a year in interest and no penalties. Statements go out by March 15 when budgets and rolls are ready.

RCW 84.40.038 governs value disputes. File with the county board of equalization by July 1 of the assessment year or within 30 days of the notice (up to 60 if the county chose a longer window), whichever is later. For good cause such as serious illness or a natural disaster, the board may accept a late filing. Read the notice for your exact deadline, and call the King County Assessor or Treasury Operations about your account.

The title company typically prorates the current bill at closing.

Offer to closing in four steps

  1. Collect payoff letters, your latest tax statement and permit records.
  2. Finish the disclosure statement and deliver it within five business days of acceptance.
  3. Accept the offer in writing so the title company can draft a settlement statement.
  4. Pay excise tax out of proceeds and sign the deed.

A cash deal drops showings, buyer financing and most inspection haggling, so it can close faster. A listing takes longer but may pay more when the house shows clean.

Papers to have ready before you list

Buyers and their lenders in Maple Valley tend to ask for the same few records, and having them in a folder saves days. Bring your deed, the latest King County tax statement and any payoff letters. Add permit records for windows, additions and remodels, since those are the projects the city flags. If the lot touches a lake, creek or wetland, include whatever correspondence you have with Economic and Community Development about trees, docks or slopes.

Walk through the house with the disclosure form in hand and answer every line from what you know. Where the answer is yes, attach a short explanation rather than leaving it blank. A complete form shortens the back and forth once an offer is in.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Weighing a cash offer

Set each offer against what a listing would realistically deliver. Take the list price, subtract commission, excise tax, repair credits and holding costs, then subtract your payoff on both sides. Get the closing date and the costs the buyer expects you to cover in writing, and let a title company or attorney read the contract.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a permit to replace windows in Maple Valley?

Yes, new or replacement windows need a building permit. Siding replacement and painting do not. When in doubt, call Economic and Community Development at (425) 413-8800.

What happens if past work on my Maple Valley house had no permit?

Expect friction. Unpermitted changes can mean tear-down, vacating or costly repairs, and many lenders want proof of a final inspection. You also have to disclose improvements and whether permits were pulled, so ask the city what it has on file.

Can I add accessory dwelling units on a Maple Valley lot?

Often. A lot with a single-family home may add two ADUs, giving three units total, under the middle housing rules that follow state law HB 1110. Confirm your zoning and lot details with the city first.

When are Maple Valley property taxes due?

April 30 for the full amount, or half by then and the second half by October 31 under RCW 84.56.020. King County sends the bill. Delinquent taxes on residential property with four or fewer units accrue 9 percent annual interest.

How do I appeal my assessed value in Maple Valley?

Petition the county board of equalization by July 1 or within the days stated on your value notice, whichever is later. RCW 84.40.038 allows 30 days, or up to 60 if the county picked that. Bring evidence of value.

Tumwater housing snapshot

Tumwater lies in Thurston County, roughly two miles south of Olympia at the spot where the Deschutes River empties into Budd Inlet. The middle-priced owned home is worth $472,200, and owners live in 62.5 percent of Tumwater homes. The population climbed from 17,371 in 2010 to 25,350 in 2020 and is now estimated at 28,010, up 7.6 percent from 2020.

Median household income is $95,212 and commutes average 21.3 minutes. Few people move within the city. A year earlier, 85.8 percent of residents were in the very same house, so sellers are often longtime owners with a long history of repairs and permits.

Older homes and the falls district

The city bills itself as the Oregon Trail's endpoint and Puget Sound's oldest lasting American settlement. Settlers arrived at Tumwater Falls in 1845, and incorporation came on November 25, 1869. The Tumwater Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1978, preserves what was left of downtown after Interstate 5 opened in 1958 and about 100 buildings came down.

Own an older place, or one near the falls? Phone Community Development at (360) 754-4180 to find out if a local historic listing or critical area rule affects the lot, ideally before a buyer's agent raises it.

Building and permit questions

The Tumwater Municipal Code governs building, remodeling and new construction, and the Building Division enforces it. That office also reviews plans and inspects for building and fire code, and a Development Review Committee weighs whether a project can go forward.

A few steps help before you list:

  • Locate permits for anything you added or replaced since buying: a deck, a finished basement, a furnace.
  • For a permit that was never finished, the Building Division can explain how to close it. Platting and planned unit development questions go to that same number, (360) 754-4180.
  • Look up your zoning in the city's building codes and development guide.
  • Check the Development Projects map for construction near your street.

A buyer's inspector often catches unpermitted work, and an open permit may delay closing. Fix it while you still set the pace.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Tumwater house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Flood and drainage on low lots

Thurston County has urged residents to prepare for fall and winter flooding from major rivers, heavy rain, saturated soils, rising groundwater and overwhelmed drainage systems. The city is also asking residents to mark places on an interactive map where more attention is needed for climate resilience planning.

If your lot is near the river or in a low spot, ask the city what that map shows and whether any flood or drainage rule applies. Buyers who see standing water in a photo will ask the same question, and a short written answer from the city is better than a guess. Keep any drainage fixes and records with the permit file.

Property tax in Thurston County

Thurston County's Treasurer bills Tumwater parcels. Visit 3000 Pacific Ave SE in Olympia on weekdays between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m., or call 360-786-5550.

The annual bill comes in two installments, April 30 and October 31, and a weekend due date slides to the next business day. You can pay online, at the counter, in the drop box out front or by mail. Mail early, because same-day postmarks are no longer guaranteed.

Find out from the Treasurer if your parcel owes anything, so the title company can deduct it from what you receive.

Excise tax and the disclosure form

Do not confuse property tax with the excise tax charged on the sale itself. That second tax usually falls on the seller, goes to the treasurer of the county where the land lies, and is due when the sale occurs. If nobody pays, a lien attaches to the property, and after a month interest begins. State rates run 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 and 1.28 percent through $1,525,000, plus a local portion.

Washington's RCW 64.06.020 sets a seller disclosure form with questions on the roof, foundation, plumbing, electrical system, heating, drainage and more. Buyers of most homes should have it within five business days after contract signing. A line on the form also notes the carbon monoxide alarm and smoke detection requirement. The statute shows the full form.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Tumwater houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Cash offer or listing?

Cash suits a house in rough shape or a seller in a hurry. The buyer takes the property as is, and with no bank involved there is no appraisal or repair demand to derail things.

Stack a cash price against a listing using these yardsticks:

  • Money left after commission, repairs and holding costs.
  • Whether the closing date matches your move.
  • Who is responsible for excise tax, title and recording fees.
  • How the buyer treats an open permit, a tenant or leftover belongings.

Insist on a written offer. Before signing, have a Thurston County title or escrow company confirm the payoff and walk you through the deed process.

A rough order of work

Begin with paperwork: the tax statement, permit records and anything still open. Then phone the Building Division about unfinished work and the Treasurer about a balance. Armed with those answers, you can weigh a listing against a cash sale using real figures.

Listing brings showings, buyer financing and an appraisal. Selling for cash brings a written offer, a title review and a closing date you negotiate. Either way, the disclosure statement is owed inside five business days of signing, so complete it candidly and keep a copy.

Known problems, including unpermitted work, belong on the form. Disclosing them up front is cheaper than a dispute after closing.

What happens at closing

At closing, the title or escrow officer clears any mortgage, delinquent property tax or lien and remits the excise tax to the county treasurer. Recording the deed finishes the sale. A payoff higher than you expected is much easier to handle in the week before closing, so confirm balances with the Treasurer early.

Gather permit records and any warranties for work done on the house so the buyer receives them with the keys. Also settle in advance which fixtures and equipment stay. Walk through the house with the buyer's agent or the cash buyer so nothing is assumed. If a tenant or stored items remain, agree on a move-out date in writing, since a cash buyer who accepts the house as it stands still needs to know what condition it will be in on closing day.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

How many people live in Tumwater?

The latest estimate is 28,010, compared with 25,350 in 2020 and 17,371 in 2010.

Which county handles property tax in Tumwater?

The county Treasurer, reachable at 360-786-5550 or at the Olympia office on Pacific Ave SE. Half the year's tax is due each spring and fall, so ask about any balance before you close.

Who pays real estate excise tax when a Tumwater house sells?

Normally the seller, paid to the county treasurer when the sale closes. Unpaid tax can become a lien on the house, and a local portion is added to the state rate that starts at 1.1 percent.

Do I need permits closed before selling a Tumwater house?

It is a good idea. Contact the Building Division at (360) 754-4180 about permits for additions or major systems, and keep the records for the buyer.

What is Tumwater known for?

The city calls itself the oldest permanent American settlement on Puget Sound and the end of the Oregon Trail. It sits at Tumwater Falls and was incorporated in 1869.

Camas housing snapshot

Camas is a Clark County city on the Columbia River, about 20 miles northeast of Portland, with Vancouver on its west side and Washougal on its east. The city counts 27,749 residents as of July 1, 2025, a 6.0 percent rise over the April 2020 base. Nearly four of five homes are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied value is $711,700. Layout, schools and the mill site

Lakes, creeks and Prune Hill shape what buyers see. Prune Hill, an extinct volcanic vent, rises in the middle of town, and Lacamas Lake, Round Lake, Lacamas Creek, the Washougal River and the Columbia River all lie inside city limits. Lacamas Park runs along State Route 500 with trails around the lakes.

  • Downtown Camas: the historic core near the paper mill, with the Liberty Theatre and the festival calendar, including Camas Days.
  • Prune Hill: a hillside residential area with a sports park named for it.
  • Lacamas Lake and Round Lake: lakeside homes next to park trails and boat launches.
  • Grass Valley and Forest Home: areas with city parks of the same names.

The Camas School District covers most of town. Some small areas belong to Evergreen Public Schools, which is worth checking for any listing address. Demolition of the paper mill has proceeded, with work expected to finish by 2027, and the site is expected to become waterfront on Camas Slough as an extension of downtown. Buyers who ask about the neighborhood's direction will likely ask about that project.

ADUs and extra units

Camas adopted Ordinance 25-025 in 2025 to align with new state housing rules. The city's ADU definition is a unit of up to 1,000 square feet, attached, detached or a mix of the two, and each lot may hold up to two. Camas also allows two middle housing units per residential lot, or four if at least one is affordable, and it created a unit lot subdivision process that lets parent lots divide into separately owned child lots.

These rules can add value, and they create questions for sellers. ADUs count toward the middle housing total, so a lot with one main home can add two ADUs, while a lot that already holds two middle housing units cannot. Before you list, confirm what was permitted.

  • Ask the Camas Community Development Department, which has Planning, Development Engineering and Building divisions, for permit history on garage conversions, basements and additions.
  • Applications, inspection requests and status tracking all go through the city's online permit system, live since June 12, 2024.

Selling quickly

Most Camas listings are polished and move-in ready, which makes a house needing work easy to spot. A seller in a hurry usually weighs three paths:

  • Prepare and list: fix, stage and show for a few weeks. This brings the best price for a home in good condition.
  • Sell as-is to an investor or cash buyer: a fit for postponed maintenance, an estate, an empty house or a tenant problem, and you choose the closing date.
  • Negotiate a leaseback or delayed possession: helpful when you need time to move after closing.

Request proof of funds and a clear written offer from any buyer. Then compare net proceeds, not only price: excise tax, payoff of any loan and prorated property taxes all come off the top.

Excise tax and paperwork

A deeded transfer sends three items to the treasurer in the property's county, the Clark County Treasurer for Camas: the affidavit, the deed and the payment. Claim only one exemption per transfer, and hold your records for at least four years. Overpaid? Ask for a refund within four years of the sale.

State excise tax climbs by tier. Price up to $525,000 pays 1.1 percent, the slice from there to $1,525,000 pays 1.28 percent, and higher tiers follow. Your escrow officer can price the local add-on and the exact bill.

You also owe the buyer a seller disclosure statement under RCW 64.06.020, normally within five business days of mutual acceptance. The form covers title, water, sewer, structural and other topics, and you sign and date each page. Camas houses near lakes, creeks or slopes should have drainage and septic or sewer details ready, since those questions appear on the form.

Clark County property tax

Clark County splits real property tax into April 30 and October 31 installments. Statements for the first half are ready by March 15, and second-half statements typically by September 15. Once October 31 passes, the following installment is due the next April 30.

From 2023 onward, a late residential parcel of four or fewer units owes 0.75 percent interest per month and no penalty. A mailed payment counts only with a postmark on or before the due date. The county does not take prepayment of future-year taxes now, apart from certain sale transactions such as personal property and mobile homes. Call 564.397.2252 or email treasoff@clark.wa.gov, and ask about the county's tax relief programs for homeowners who meet eligibility requirements.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Camas houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to have ready

Camas buyers are mostly families, and they ask practical questions. Have the permit history for any garage conversion, basement or addition, and know whether an ADU exists and what was approved. If the house sits near Lacamas Lake, Round Lake, a creek or a slope, collect drainage and septic or sewer details. Bring your latest Clark County tax statement and a plan for the school district answer. The city's Community Development Department and the county treasurer are the two offices to call.

Steps from offer to closing

Once you accept an offer, escrow opens and title work shows any unpaid taxes. You sign the disclosure form, deed and affidavit, and payment goes to the Clark County Treasurer. Escrow prorates property taxes and deducts any loan payoff from what you receive. No lender means no appraisal, and a house that needs work can still close on a date you pick. Gather your tax statement, permit history and the disclosure form ahead of time so nothing holds up the signing, and ask the treasurer about any balance before the closing date.

Frequently asked questions

Which school district serves Camas homes?

The Camas School District covers most of the city, but a few small areas are in Evergreen Public Schools. Confirm the district for the exact address.

How many ADUs can I build on a Camas lot?

Up to two. Camas defines an ADU as a unit up to 1,000 square feet, attached or detached. ADUs count toward the middle housing allowance, which is two units per residential lot, or four if at least one is affordable.

When are Clark County property taxes due?

April 30 for the first half or the full year, October 31 for the second. A mailed payment must be postmarked by the due date. Late residential tax on four or fewer units accrues 0.75 percent per month.

Who collects the excise tax on a Camas home sale?

The Clark County Treasurer, because that is the county where Camas properties sit. The seller usually pays, and a deeded transfer sends the affidavit, deed and payment together.

Do I need to keep records of an excise tax exemption?

Yes, for at least four years. You can claim only one exemption per transfer, and any overpayment refund request is due within four years of the sale.

How a Moses Lake sale works

Three ways to sell exist for a Moses Lake homeowner: hire an agent, go it alone, or deal with a cash buyer who purchases the house in its present condition. No matter which, the paperwork is the same: a deed, a state excise tax affidavit and recording through Grant County.

Moses Lake is the most populous city in Grant County, with an estimated 27,469 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 25,146 in 2020. Owner-occupancy runs 61.2 percent, with a median value of $310,000 for those homes. Median gross rent is $1,216, median household income is $74,752, and the mean trip to work takes 18.2 minutes, which is worth quoting to buyers who commute.

Cash tends to appeal to people with inherited houses, rentals or long repair lists who would rather skip showings and close on a date they pick.

Permits that can trip up a sale

Work done without the permit the city requires is the usual snag. A buyer or title company may ask whether your fence, porch or roof had one, and the Building Department publishes a list of permit types.

ProjectWhen a permit applies
FenceBefore installing any fence

Remodels, additions and accessory dwelling units go through the city's permit portal with plans, and demolition and grading or clearing each have their own permit. Not sure about a past project? Call the Building Department at 509-764-3743 and ask how an unpermitted structure can be documented before you list.

Short-term rentals

Nightly rentals need the city's approval, and that approval does not follow the house to a new owner. Chapter 15.650 of the Moses Lake Municipal Code covers stays under 30 days and allows them in specified zoning districts.

An owner applies to the Community Development Department for a short-term rental endorsement, and a business license under Chapter 5.04 is held back until the endorsement is approved. Endorsements are generally not transferable, so a buyer who wants nightly rentals should expect to apply again after closing. If you run the house that way now, tell any buyer the endorsement may not carry over. Excise tax, deeds and recording

The seller files a Real Estate Excise Tax Affidavit, pays the Grant County Treasurer and then has the deed recorded. Payment falls due on the sale date, which is the notarization date of the deed, even when recording happens afterward.

Through December 31, 2026 the state's graduated rate begins at 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 and climbs through 1.28, 2.75 and 3 percent bands. Beginning in 2027 those breakpoints shift upward to $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. A local rate comes on top.

The Grant County Treasurer is at 35 C Street NW, Room 204, in Ephrata, phone 509-754-2010, open weekdays 8 a.m. to noon and 1 to 5 p.m. Ask there how current-year property taxes are handled at your closing; the first half is due April 30.

Seller disclosure

Answer each line from your own knowledge, mention roof, drainage or permit problems where they apply, and keep a copy with your closing papers. Moses Lake has I-90 and State Route 17 bypassing the center, while State Route 171 and I-90 Business serve downtown. Grant Transit Authority runs buses within the city and to Ephrata. Lakefront and location notes

The lake stretches more than 18 miles across its three arms and has over 120 miles of shoreline, so waterfront homes are common here. If yours is one of them, say how close the shore is and what the view looks like, since that drives interest. South of town sit Potholes Reservoir and the Columbia National Wildlife Refuge, a draw for outdoor buyers. The Moses Lake School District runs eleven elementary schools, three middle schools and Moses Lake High School, and buyers with kids will want to confirm assignment for your address.

Closing day in Grant County

Plan the last stretch in this order. Sign the deed in front of a notary, because that date sets the excise tax clock. Bring the completed affidavit and payment to the Grant County Treasurer in Ephrata, or have your closing agent do it. After payment clears, the county auditor records the deed.

Do not forget the property tax side. The first half of the year's bill is due April 30, so ask the treasurer what is outstanding and how a prorated share should be handled at closing. A cash buyer will usually let a title company sort this out; on a listing, your escrow officer does.

When cash makes sense in Moses Lake

Consider it if the house needs work, someone still lives in it, or you need a date you can count on. Worn rentals and inherited homes nobody wants to renovate fit well.

Before agreeing to anything, have the buyer confirm funds, commit to a closing day in writing, and spell out who covers excise tax and title costs. A listing eats time with preparation, showings, inspection and a loan; a cash sale closes when you are ready. Request a bid on your address, then hold it up against the leftover from a listing once excise tax, agent fees and repairs are paid.

If you do list, expect the buyer's lender to want the permit and inspection story straight, which is why the Building Department call above comes first.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need a permit to sell a Moses Lake house?

Selling itself needs no permit. The city does require permits for work such as fences, re-roofs replacing more than 25 percent of the sheathing, retaining walls of 4 feet or more, and covered porches of 200 square feet or more. If past work lacked a permit, call the Building Department at 509-764-3743 before listing.

Who pays the real estate excise tax in Moses Lake?

The seller, as a rule. Skip it and the buyer can end up on the hook, with a lien possible. Payment goes to the Grant County Treasurer as of the sale date, and the local rate sits above the state's graduated rate.

Does a short-term rental permit transfer to the buyer in Moses Lake?

Generally no. Endorsements issued under Chapter 15.650 are generally not transferable, so a new owner may need a new endorsement before renting by the night.

How is the excise tax figured on a Moses Lake sale?

State tax opens at 1.1 percent on the lowest slice of the price, with a local rate added. Have your title officer total it before you accept an offer.

Where do I record the deed and file the excise tax affidavit for a Moses Lake property?

Both go through Grant County. The treasurer takes the excise tax, and state law has deeds recorded with the county auditor. Phone the treasurer at 509-754-2010 to find out what to bring.

The island sits in the southern half of Lake Washington, Seattle to the west and Bellevue to the east, and the city limits match the island. About 22.2 percent of residents are 65 or older, and many owners stay put for years, so inherited and downsizing sales are common. If you have owned a long time, pull the permit history first, because it shows which additions and remodels the city has on file.

Excise tax at closing

Washington taxes a sale with a graduated real estate excise tax, and the seller usually pays. State rates start at 1.10 percent and top out at 3 percent. For closings from January 1, 2027 the bands break at $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. Earlier closings break at $525,000 and $1,525,000 for the first two. At island prices a large share of a sale falls in the upper bands.

Your title officer can quote the exact total, local rate included, for your closing date. Payment is owed on the sale date, which the Department of Revenue counts as the day the deed is notarized, and tax left unpaid can turn into a lien on the property.

Slopes, seismic areas and hazard maps

The city maps four hazard areas on its GIS portal: seismic, steep slope, erosion and potential slide. If your lot falls in one, work on ground or vegetation usually needs a permit, and buyers will ask about it.

The island is a glacial plateau cut by ravines, and the Seattle Fault crosses its northern part. On lots flagged for erosion, potential slide or steep slope, clearing, grading, filling and foundation work are barred between October 1 and April 1 unless the city grants a waiver backed by a geotechnical evaluation. A geotechnical report is also required when a structure goes into a critical area.

Check the map before planning any pre-sale repair. A retaining wall or deck fix that is exempt on flat ground can need review on a slope.

Unpermitted work and permit exemptions

The city's Code Compliance planner handles work done without required permits, and a buyer's lender or inspector may ask about past remodels. An exemption from a building permit does not exempt a project from building or land use codes. Under MICC 17.14.010, a permit covers building, enlarging, altering, repairing, moving or demolishing a structure, plus electrical, gas, mechanical and plumbing systems. The city lists 22 exceptions, among them:

ProjectExempt from a building permit when

Paperwork a seller handles

Three documents matter: the seller disclosure statement, the deed and the excise tax affidavit. The form in RCW 64.06.020 asks about title, easements, boundary disputes, assessments, zoning violations, water, sewer and structural problems. Answer from what you actually know, and attach an explanation to every yes.

  • King County Assessor: property report with lot size, present use and year built.
  • King County Recorder's Office: recorded plats, surveys and deeds.
  • MyBuildingPermit.com: status of building and land use permits.
  • City Online Map Portal: permit files, sewer as-builts and geotechnical reports tied to your parcel.
  • Residential certificate of occupancy: on most island houses, the permit card with the signed final inspection serves as the certificate.

The permit center is at 9611 SE 36th Street, and land use staff take calls at 206-275-7605.

Schools and getting around

The Mercer Island School District runs seven schools on the island, among them Mercer Island High School and Islander Middle School. Interstate 90 crosses the island, with floating bridges toward Seattle and the East Channel Bridge toward Bellevue, and much of the freeway is capped by the Mercer Island Lid. The Sound Transit 2 Line station in the I-90 median opened on March 28, 2026 and has a park-and-ride with 447 stalls. Work them into your listing, or into the description you give a cash buyer.

When cash makes sense

Cash is worth a look when time, condition or paperwork would slow a listing. Inherited houses, homes with deferred repairs, properties with old permit gaps and sales with tenants in place are the usual cases.

Compare the net, not the headline. On a listing, subtract state and local excise tax, any agent fee you agree to, repair credits, and carrying costs such as utilities and insurance during the weeks the house sits. On a cash deal, get the funds verified, the closing date in writing, and a clear split of excise tax and title costs. Then ask for an offer on your address and weigh it against the list-and-wait numbers.

Frequently asked questions

Who pays the real estate excise tax when a Mercer Island house sells?

The seller, in most cases. Leave it unpaid and the burden can move to the buyer, and a lien can follow. County treasurer receives it as of the sale date, and the local rate sits on top of the graduated state rate.

Can I sell a Mercer Island house with work that was never permitted?

Yes, but expect questions. The city's Code Compliance planner handles such cases, and the usual fix is a courtesy letter or correction notice. One path is a cash buyer who accepts the house as it is. Another is a listing, where the buyer's inspector or lender may request the permit history.

Does the seller disclosure form apply to every Mercer Island sale?

Generally, for improved residential property, unless the buyer waives it or RCW 64.06.010 exempts the transfer. Delivery is due five business days after acceptance, if the parties do not agree otherwise, and the buyer then has three business days to rescind.

Does a steep or low-lying lot change how I sell on Mercer Island?

It can. The city maps seismic, steep slope, erosion and potential slide hazards. Permit exemptions for flat lots do not apply in critical areas, and ground work on erosion, slide or steep slope lots is limited between October 1 and April 1 unless the city grants a waiver.

Where do I find recorded deeds and the sale history for my Mercer Island property?

The King County Recorder's Office holds recorded plats, surveys and deeds, and the King County Assessor has values and sales history. The city's Online Map Portal also shows permit files and geotechnical reports tied to your parcel.
